adolescent-sexual-health-clinics-confide.en:
Imagine a 17-year-old in Patna who feels a burning sensation every time she pees, or an 18-year-old in Bundi, married six months ago, who does not want a baby yet. Neither can ask at home. Both turn to a phone, a friend or the man at the medical shop. India runs a government health service built for exactly these questions. This guide explains what it offers, what stays private, and the honest exception the law makes for anyone under 18.

## The questions young people cannot ask at home

Very little information reaches young Indians about their own bodies. In 2019-21, only 54.4% of young women aged 15-24 knew where to get a condom, against 87.3% of young men [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Only 20.1% of young women and 28.5% of young men had comprehensive knowledge of HIV [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

The risks arrive anyway. In 2023-24, 6.7% of women aged 15-19 were already mothers or pregnant. In villages the figure was 7.9%, more than double the urban 3.4% [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]]. The figure includes 18- and 19-year-olds, so it is a marker of early marriage as much as of under-18 pregnancy. Married teenagers are among the least served. Among married women aged 15-19, only 28.1% used any contraception and 17.8% had an unmet need for it, nearly double the national figure [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

The stakes are highest for the youngest. In 2022 UNFPA India said women aged 15-19 face the highest risk of dying from complications of abortion [[unfpa-swop-2022-india-insights]].

## What adolescent health centres offer

The service is the Adolescent Friendly Health Centre, or AFHC. It began in 2006 as a counselling clinic for adolescent sexual and reproductive health [[nhm-afhc-page-2026]]. It now sits under the Rashtriya Kishor Swasthya Karyakram (RKSK), launched on 7 January 2014 to reach 253 million adolescents. RKSK widened the brief beyond sex and pregnancy to nutrition, mental health, substance misuse, injuries and violence, including gender-based violence [[nhm-adolescent-health-rksk-page-2026]].

AFHCs offer counselling and clinical care at primary and community health centres, district hospitals and medical colleges. National guidance says they should not be placed next to labour rooms or HIV and STI testing centres, so that a teenager can walk in without hesitation [[nhm-afhc-page-2026]]. In October 2025 the Health Ministry renamed them from "clinics" to "centres", saying adolescents hesitated to visit because a visit to a "clinic" was "looked upon with suspicion". It said 1.7 crore adolescents used the services in 2024-25, a count that may include repeat visits [[mohfw-afhc-rename-2025]]. Some states use local names such as Yuva Clinic, Umang or Sneha.

You can ask about periods, wet dreams, masturbation, acne, weight, mood, a late period, discharge or itching, an STI worry, a relationship that frightens you, alcohol or drugs. If a condom broke or you had sex without protection in the last few days, ask about emergency contraception: it can be used up to 5 days afterwards, and the sooner the better [[who-ec]].

## What stays confidential

If you are 18 or 19, you are an adult. Your consultation is confidential, and a relationship between consenting adults is not a police matter. Two laws add specific protections. Under the MTP Act, a doctor may not reveal the name or details of a woman whose pregnancy was ended, except to someone authorised by law; breaking this can mean up to one year in prison, a fine, or both [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]]. Under the HIV Act 2017, no one may test you for HIV without your informed consent, and no one can force you to disclose your status except by court order [[naco-hiv-aids-act-2017-gazette]].

If you are under 18, everyday health questions are still treated as private, though a parent or guardian may need to consent to some tests or treatment. This is general information, not legal advice.

## The POCSO reporting duty, explained honestly

Under POCSO, any sexual activity with a person under 18 is an offence, even if both people agreed. Section 19 requires anyone who knows of such an offence, doctors and counsellors included, to report it to the police. Failing to report can mean up to 6 months in prison, a fine, or both, and the head of an institution who fails to report an offence by someone working under them faces up to 1 year and a fine [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. A child cannot be punished for not reporting.

So a counsellor who learns that a 16-year-old is sexually active, or has been abused, cannot promise total secrecy. In 2022 the Supreme Court named the cost of this rule for pregnant girls [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]]:

> "Minors and their guardians are likely faced with two options – one, approach an RMP and possibly be involved in criminal proceedings under the POCSO Act, or two, approach an unqualified doctor for a medical termination of the pregnancy."

An RMP is a registered medical practitioner. The same judgment offered a partial fix: when a minor seeks an abortion, the doctor need not name her in the police report if she and her guardian ask [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]]. You have to ask for it.

Two more honest points. If someone abused you, the report is about the person who harmed you, and the law treats you as the one to protect. If your partner is also a teenager, a report can still lead to a case against them; our Q&A on teenage relationships under POCSO explains how. Either way, an untreated infection or a late, unsafe abortion is far more dangerous than the conversation.

## Other safe places to ask

- **1097**, NACO's toll-free AIDS helpline, offers confidential counselling round the clock in 16 languages. It took 4,32,474 calls in 2024-25 [[naco-sankalak-2025]].
- **Suraksha Clinics**, NACO's 1,127 designated STI clinics, sit in district hospitals and medical colleges [[naco-sankalak-2025]].
- **Tele-MANAS, 14416**, is free support for anxiety, low mood or thoughts of self-harm [[tele-manas]].
- **Child Helpline 1098** or **112**, if someone is hurting or pressuring you.

Start every visit with one question: "What will stay between us?" A good counsellor will answer it plainly. Then you decide what to say.
adolescent-sexual-health-clinics-confide.hg:
Socho Patna ki ek 17 saal ki ladki ko har baar pee karte waqt jalan hoti hai. Ya Bundi ki ek 18 saal ki ladki, jiski shaadi ko chhe mahine hue hain, aur jo abhi baby nahi chahti. Dono ghar par pooch nahi sakti. Dono phone, kisi dost ya medical shop wale bhaiya ke paas jaati hain. India mein bilkul inhi sawaalon ke liye ek government health service chalti hai. Yeh guide batati hai ki woh kya deti hai, kya private rehta hai, aur 18 se kam umar walon ke liye law ka imaandaar exception kya hai.

## Woh sawaal jo young log ghar par nahi pooch sakte

Young Indians tak apni hi body ke baare mein bahut kam jaankari pahunchti hai. 2019-21 mein 15-24 saal ki sirf 54.4% young women ko pata tha ki condom kahan milta hai, jabki young men mein yeh 87.3% tha [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Sirf 20.1% young women aur 28.5% young men ko HIV ki comprehensive knowledge thi [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Risk phir bhi aate hain. 2023-24 mein 15-19 saal ki 6.7% ladkiyan pehle se maa thi ya pregnant thi. Gaon mein yeh 7.9% tha, shehron ke 3.4% se do guna se bhi zyada [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]]. Is figure mein 18 aur 19 saal ki ladkiyan bhi shaamil hain, isliye yeh jitna under-18 pregnancy ka, utna hi early marriage ka nishaan hai. Shaadishuda teenagers sabse kam madad paane walon mein hain. 15-19 saal ki shaadishuda ladkiyon mein sirf 28.1% koi bhi contraception use karti thi, aur 17.8% ki contraception ki zaroorat poori nahi ho rahi thi, jo national figure se lagbhag double hai [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Sabse bada khatra sabse kam umar walon ko hai. 2022 mein UNFPA India ne kaha ki 15-19 saal ki ladkiyon ko abortion complications se marne ka sabse zyada risk hota hai [[unfpa-swop-2022-india-insights]].

## Adolescent health centres kya offer karte hain

Is service ka naam hai Adolescent Friendly Health Centre, yaani AFHC. Iski shuruaat 2006 mein adolescents ki sexual aur reproductive health par counselling clinic ke roop mein hui thi [[nhm-afhc-page-2026]]. Ab yeh Rashtriya Kishor Swasthya Karyakram (RKSK) ke under hai, jo 7 January 2014 ko 253 million adolescents tak pahunchne ke liye launch hua tha. RKSK ne dayra sex aur pregnancy se aage badha kar nutrition, mental health, nashe, injuries aur violence tak kar diya, gender-based violence samet [[nhm-adolescent-health-rksk-page-2026]].

AFHCs primary aur community health centres, district hospitals aur medical colleges mein counselling aur clinical care dete hain. National guidance kehti hai ki inhe labour room ya HIV aur STI testing centres ke bilkul paas nahi hona chahiye, taaki koi teenager bina jhijhak andar aa sake [[nhm-afhc-page-2026]]. October 2025 mein Health Ministry ne inka naam "clinics" se badal kar "centres" kar diya, aur kaha ki adolescents wahan jaane se jhijhakte the kyunki "clinic" jaane ko "looked upon with suspicion", yaani shak ki nazar se dekha jaata tha. Ministry ke mutabik 2024-25 mein 1.7 crore adolescents ne yeh services li, aur is count mein repeat visits bhi ho sakti hain [[mohfw-afhc-rename-2025]]. Kuch states inhe local naamon se chalate hain, jaise Yuva Clinic, Umang ya Sneha.

Wahan tum periods, wet dreams, masturbation, acne, weight, mood, late period, discharge ya khujli, STI ki tension, kisi darane wale relationship, ya sharaab aur drugs ke baare mein pooch sakte ho. Agar pichhle kuch dinon mein condom phat gaya ya bina protection sex hua, toh emergency contraception ke baare mein poocho: yeh 5 din tak li ja sakti hai, aur jitni jaldi lo utna behtar [[who-ec]].

## Kya confidential rehta hai

Agar tum 18 ya 19 ke ho, toh tum adult ho. Tumhari consultation confidential hai, aur do consenting adults ka relationship police ka maamla nahi hai. Do laws aur protection dete hain. MTP Act ke under koi doctor us aurat ka naam ya details nahi bata sakta jiski pregnancy end hui, sivaay us insaan ke jise law ne authorise kiya ho; yeh todne par ek saal tak ki jail, fine, ya dono ho sakte hain [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]]. HIV Act 2017 ke under tumhari informed consent ke bina koi tumhara HIV test nahi kar sakta, aur court order ke bina koi tumhe apna status batane par majboor nahi kar sakta [[naco-hiv-aids-act-2017-gazette]].

Agar tum 18 se kam ho, toh roz ki health ke sawaal tab bhi private maane jaate hain, lekin kuch tests ya treatment ke liye parent ya guardian ki consent lagni pad sakti hai. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## POCSO ki reporting duty, imaandaari se samjho

POCSO ke under 18 se kam umar ke kisi bhi insaan ke saath koi bhi sexual activity offence hai, chahe dono ne haan kaha ho. Section 19 kehta hai ki jise bhi aise offence ka pata ho, doctors aur counsellors samet, use police ko report karna hoga. Report na karne par 6 mahine tak ki jail, fine, ya dono ho sakte hain, aur agar kisi institution ka head apne under kaam karne wale ke offence ko report na kare, toh use 1 saal tak ki jail aur fine ho sakta hai [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Kisi bachche ko report na karne ke liye saza nahi di ja sakti.

Isliye agar counsellor ko pata chale ki koi 16 saal ka teenager sexually active hai, ya uska abuse hua hai, toh woh poori secrecy ka promise nahi kar sakta. 2022 mein Supreme Court ne pregnant ladkiyon ke liye is rule ki keemat khul kar boli [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]]:

> "Minors and their guardians are likely faced with two options – one, approach an RMP and possibly be involved in criminal proceedings under the POCSO Act, or two, approach an unqualified doctor for a medical termination of the pregnancy."

Matlab: minor aur uske guardian ke saamne do hi raaste bachte hain, registered doctor (RMP) ke paas jao aur criminal case ka risk lo, ya kisi unqualified doctor ke paas jao. Isi judgment ne ek aadha solution bhi diya: jab koi minor abortion ke liye aaye, toh agar woh aur uska guardian kahein, toh doctor ko police report mein uska naam likhna zaroori nahi [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]]. Yeh tumhe khud maangna padega.

Do aur imaandaar baatein. Agar kisi ne tumhara abuse kiya, toh report us insaan ke baare mein hai jisne nuksaan pahunchaya, aur law tumhe woh maanta hai jise bachaana hai. Agar tumhara partner bhi teenager hai, toh report se uske khilaaf case ban sakta hai; POCSO mein teenage relationships par hamara Q&A yeh detail mein samjhata hai. Jo bhi ho, bina ilaaj ka infection ya der se hua unsafe abortion is baatcheet se kahin zyada khatarnaak hai.

## Poochne ki aur safe jagahein

- **1097**, NACO ki toll-free AIDS helpline, din-raat 16 languages mein confidential counselling deti hai. 2024-25 mein ispar 4,32,474 calls aayi [[naco-sankalak-2025]].
- **Suraksha Clinics**, NACO ke 1,127 designated STI clinics, district hospitals aur medical colleges mein hain [[naco-sankalak-2025]].
- **Tele-MANAS, 14416**, anxiety, low mood ya khud ko nuksaan pahunchane ke khayalon ke liye free support hai [[tele-manas]].
- **Child Helpline 1098** ya **112**, agar koi tumhe nuksaan pahuncha raha hai ya pressure daal raha hai.

Har visit ek sawaal se shuru karo: "Kya-kya hamare beech rahega?" Achha counsellor iska seedha jawab dega. Uske baad tum tay karo ki kya batana hai.

aids-deaths-india-care-chain-gaps.en:
Consider a 35-year-old man in Ludhiana who has been losing weight for months. A local practitioner treats him for "weakness" and for a cough that will not go away. Nobody suggests an HIV test until he is admitted to the district hospital, and by then his immune system is badly damaged. He is a hypothetical, but this is how an AIDS death can happen in a country where the medicine that prevents it is free at government centres.

An estimated 32,160 people died of AIDS-related causes in India in 2024 [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. It is a modelled estimate, and NACO's uncertainty range runs from 21.47 thousand to 49.95 thousand. To understand them, follow the chain of care and look for where it breaks.

## 32,160 deaths: down from 1.73 lakh, still too many

In 2010, India had an estimated 1.73 lakh AIDS-related deaths [[pib-world-aids-day-backgrounder-2025]]. By 2024 that had fallen 81.4% [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. What keeps HIV from progressing to AIDS is antiretroviral therapy (ART) [[who-hiv]]. In March 2025, 18.60 lakh people with HIV were on ART: 17.54 lakh at 800 government ART centres, where it is free, and about 1.06 lakh in the private sector [[naco-sankalak-2025]].

But India has an estimated 25.61 lakh people living with HIV [[naco-sankalak-2025]], so fewer than three in four are on treatment. NACO measures the gap against the UN's 95-95-95 targets: 95% of people with HIV should know their status, 95% of them should be on treatment, and 95% of those should have the virus suppressed.

| Link in the chain | 2020-21 | 2024-25 |
|---|---|---|
| Know they have HIV | 70.7% | 83.9% |
| Diagnosed and on treatment | 82.5% | 86.6% |
| On treatment, virus suppressed | 84.9% | 97.6% |

India has improved on every step [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. The last link is now the strongest: the medicine works. The chain breaks earlier.

## Gap one: diagnosed too late

In 2024-25, roughly one in six people with HIV in India did not know they had it [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. HIV can stay silent for years while it weakens the immune system. AIDS, the most advanced stage, develops mainly when HIV goes undiagnosed or untreated, and it opens the door to serious infections that a healthy body would fight off [[who-hiv]]. A person tested only after falling ill starts treatment from far behind.

Testing finds people when it is aimed well. NACO ran 4.13 crore HIV tests among at-risk people in 2024-25, and 0.40% were positive. People who walked in on their own made up only 14% of those tests, but had the highest positivity of any group, 1.1% [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Families are the other strong signal. Of 6.6 lakh spouses, partners and children of people with HIV who were tested, 4.1% were positive, about ten times the overall rate [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. A diagnosis in one family member is a chance to find another early.

## Gap two: diagnosed but not on treatment

Of people who knew their status in 2024-25, 86.6% were on treatment [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. More than one in eight were not, despite free medicine.

The figures alone do not say why. India has 800 government ART centres [[naco-sankalak-2025]], and for someone in a small town or village the nearest one may be a long way off. Consider a hypothetical daily-wage worker there: every visit can mean a bus fare, a lost day's wages and the fear of being seen by someone he knows. Others may feel well and see no reason to start, or may not yet be ready to accept the diagnosis.

The law offers less than many people assume. The HIV Act 2017 obliges governments to provide ART only "as far as possible" (Section 14), so free treatment is a policy, not an absolute legal right [[naco-hiv-aids-act-2017-gazette]]. What the Act does guarantee is protection from discrimination: Section 3 bars it in healthcare, employment, education and housing [[naco-hiv-aids-act-2017-gazette]]. Every state must appoint an HIV Ombudsman to hear complaints [[naco-hiv-aids-act-2017-gazette]]; by March 2025, 34 States/UTs had one [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. This is general information, not legal advice.

## What staying on treatment takes

ART does not cure HIV. It is a daily medicine, taken for life [[who-hiv]]. Taken regularly, it works: in 2024-25, 97.6% of people on treatment whose viral load was tested had the virus suppressed [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. A person who stays undetectable does not pass HIV on through sex [[who-hiv]].

Read that 97.6% carefully. It counts only people who are still on treatment and were tested. People who stopped coming to the ART centre fall outside the count, and they are the ones most at risk. When treatment stops, the virus multiplies again and the immune system weakens [[who-hiv]]. That is where AIDS takes hold, in a gap no percentage shows.

## How families and friends can help

Much of what keeps someone with HIV alive happens outside the hospital.

- **Suggest a test without blame.** If someone close to you has been unwell for weeks, offer to go with them for an HIV test at a government testing centre. NACO's helpline 1097 can point you to the nearest one [[naco]].
- **Get tested yourself** if you are their partner or child. Family testing is voluntary and needs the consent of the person with HIV.
- **Help with the routine**: a daily reminder, a ride to the ART centre, a hand with paperwork.
- **Keep their secret.** Under the HIV Act, no one can be compelled to disclose their HIV status except by court order [[naco-hiv-aids-act-2017-gazette]]. Their status is theirs to share.
- **Watch for despair.** A diagnosis can bring depression. Tele-MANAS, 14416, offers free mental-health support [[tele-manas]], and NACO's helpline 1097 offers confidential HIV counselling round the clock [[naco-sankalak-2025]].

In March 2025, about 80,000 children were on treatment at government ART centres [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. For them, every link in the chain is in adult hands.

The medicine that prevents these deaths exists, and government centres give it free. What the 32,160 deaths measure is how far it still has to reach, and reach is something families, friends and the health system can change.
aids-deaths-india-care-chain-gaps.hg:
Socho Ludhiana ka ek 35 saal ka aadmi, jiska weight mahino se gir raha hai. Ek local practitioner use "kamzori" aur kabhi na jaane wali khaansi ki dawai deta rehta hai. District hospital mein admit hone tak koi HIV test ki baat nahi karta, aur tab tak uska immune system bahut kamzor ho chuka hota hai. Yeh ek hypothetical hai, lekin ek aise desh mein AIDS se maut aise ho sakti hai, jahan use rokne wali dawai government centres par free hai.

2024 mein India mein estimated 32,160 logon ki AIDS-related causes se maut hui [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Yeh ek modelled estimate hai, aur NACO ki uncertainty range 21.47 thousand se 49.95 thousand tak hai. Inhe samajhne ke liye care ki chain ko follow karo aur dekho ki woh kahan tootti hai.

## 32,160 maut: 1.73 lakh se neeche, phir bhi bahut zyada

2010 mein India mein estimated 1.73 lakh AIDS-related maut hui thi [[pib-world-aids-day-backgrounder-2025]]. 2024 tak yeh 81.4% gir gayi [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. HIV ko AIDS tak pahunchne se antiretroviral therapy (ART) hi rokti hai [[who-hiv]]. March 2025 mein 18.60 lakh HIV wale log ART par the: 17.54 lakh 800 government ART centres par, jahan yeh free hai, aur lagbhag 1.06 lakh private sector mein [[naco-sankalak-2025]].

Lekin India mein estimated 25.61 lakh log HIV ke saath jee rahe hain [[naco-sankalak-2025]], yaani har chaar mein se teen se bhi kam treatment par hain. NACO is gap ko UN ke 95-95-95 targets se naapta hai: HIV wale 95% logon ko apna status pata ho, unmein se 95% treatment par hon, aur unmein se 95% ka virus suppressed ho.

| Chain ki kadi | 2020-21 | 2024-25 |
|---|---|---|
| Pata hai ki HIV hai | 70.7% | 83.9% |
| Diagnosed aur treatment par | 82.5% | 86.6% |
| Treatment par, virus suppressed | 84.9% | 97.6% |

India har step par aage badha hai [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Aakhri kadi ab sabse mazboot hai: dawai kaam karti hai. Chain usse pehle tootti hai.

## Pehla gap: diagnosis bahut der se

2024-25 mein India mein HIV wale lagbhag har chhe mein se ek insaan ko pata hi nahi tha ki use HIV hai [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. HIV saalon tak chupchaap immune system ko kamzor kar sakta hai. AIDS, iski sabse advanced stage, zyada tar tab hota hai jab HIV ka diagnosis ya ilaaj nahi hota, aur yeh un serious infections ka darwaza khol deta hai jinse ek healthy body khud lad leti [[who-hiv]]. Jiska test beemar padne ke baad hota hai, woh treatment bahut peeche se shuru karta hai.

Testing tab logon ko dhoondhti hai jab sahi jagah ho. 2024-25 mein NACO ne at-risk logon ke 4.13 crore HIV tests kiye, aur 0.40% positive nikle. Khud walk-in karne wale log in tests ka sirf 14% the, lekin unmein positivity sabse zyada thi, 1.1% [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Family doosra mazboot signal hai. HIV wale logon ke 6.6 lakh spouses, partners aur bachchon ka test hua, aur unmein se 4.1% positive nikle, yaani overall rate se lagbhag dus guna [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Family mein ek insaan ka diagnosis doosre ko jaldi dhoondhne ka mauka hota hai.

## Doosra gap: diagnosis hua, par treatment nahi

2024-25 mein jinhe apna status pata tha, unmein se 86.6% treatment par the [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Free dawai ke bawajood har aath mein se ek se zyada log treatment par nahi the.

Sirf figures se iski wajah pata nahi chalti. India mein 800 government ART centres hain [[naco-sankalak-2025]], aur kisi chhote shehar ya gaon mein rehne wale ke liye sabse paas wala centre bhi kaafi door ho sakta hai. Wahan ke ek hypothetical dihaadi mazdoor ke baare mein socho: har visit ka matlab ho sakta hai bus ka kiraya, ek din ki dihaadi ka nuksaan, aur kisi jaan-pehchaan wale ke dekh lene ka darr. Kuch log theek feel kar sakte hain aur shuru karne ki wajah nahi dekhte, ya abhi diagnosis ko maan hi nahi paaye hote.

Law utna nahi deta jitna log sochte hain. HIV Act 2017 sarkaron ko ART sirf "as far as possible", yaani jahan tak mumkin ho, dene ke liye bolta hai (Section 14), isliye free treatment ek policy hai, absolute legal right nahi [[naco-hiv-aids-act-2017-gazette]]. Act jo pakka deta hai woh hai discrimination se protection: Section 3 healthcare, naukri, education aur ghar ke maamle mein bhedbhaav ko mana karta hai [[naco-hiv-aids-act-2017-gazette]]. Har state ko complaints sunne ke liye ek HIV Ombudsman appoint karna hota hai [[naco-hiv-aids-act-2017-gazette]]; March 2025 tak 34 States/UTs mein Ombudsman tha [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## Treatment par bane rehne ke liye kya chahiye

ART HIV ko cure nahi karti. Yeh roz li jaane wali dawai hai, zindagi bhar ke liye [[who-hiv]]. Regularly li jaaye toh kaam karti hai: 2024-25 mein treatment par jin logon ka viral load test hua, unmein se 97.6% ka virus suppressed tha [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Jo insaan undetectable bana rehta hai, woh sex ke through HIV aage nahi deta [[who-hiv]].

Is 97.6% ko dhyaan se padho. Isme sirf woh log gine jaate hain jo abhi bhi treatment par hain aur jinka test hua. Jo log ART centre aana chhod chuke hain, woh is count se bahar hain, aur sabse zyada risk unhi ko hai. Treatment rukte hi virus phir badhne lagta hai aur immune system kamzor hota hai [[who-hiv]]. AIDS wahin pair jamata hai, us gap mein jo koi percentage nahi dikhata.

## Family aur dost kaise help kar sakte hain

HIV wale insaan ko zinda rakhne wala bahut kuch hospital ke bahar hota hai.

- **Bina blame ke test ka suggestion do.** Agar tumhara koi apna hafton se beemar hai, toh uske saath kisi government testing centre par HIV test ke liye chalne ki offer karo. NACO ki helpline 1097 sabse paas wala centre bata sakti hai [[naco]].
- **Khud bhi test karwao** agar tum unke partner ya bachche ho. Family testing voluntary hai aur HIV wale insaan ki consent se hi hoti hai.
- **Routine mein saath do**: roz ka reminder, ART centre tak ki ride, paperwork mein madad.
- **Unka raaz rakho.** HIV Act ke under court order ke bina kisi ko apna HIV status batane ke liye majboor nahi kiya ja sakta [[naco-hiv-aids-act-2017-gazette]]. Status unka hai, batana unka faisla hai.
- **Mayusi par nazar rakho.** Diagnosis ke baad depression aa sakta hai. Tele-MANAS, 14416, free mental-health support deta hai [[tele-manas]], aur NACO ki helpline 1097 din-raat confidential HIV counselling deti hai [[naco-sankalak-2025]].

March 2025 mein government ART centres par lagbhag 80,000 bachche treatment par the [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Unke liye chain ki har kadi badon ke haath mein hai.

In maut ko rokne wali dawai maujood hai, aur government centres ise free dete hain. Yeh 32,160 maut dikhati hain ki use abhi kitni door tak pahunchna baaki hai, aur pahunch woh cheez hai jise family, dost aur health system badal sakte hain.

bihar-punjab-new-hiv-infections-migratio.en:
Picture India's HIV epidemic and you may picture Mumbai, the southern states or the North-East. For people already living with the virus, that picture fits: Maharashtra had an estimated 3,99,023 in 2024, more than any other state, and the North-East has the highest rates [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. But a different list shows where HIV is spreading now. In 2024 Bihar had an estimated 7,694 new infections, the most in India, and Punjab and Uttar Pradesh also had more than Maharashtra [[naco-sankalak-2025]].

## The second map: where new infections happen

India has two HIV maps. One counts everyone living with the virus, including people infected decades ago; our by-the-numbers story on HIV in 2024 covers it. The other counts new infections in a year, and shows where the virus is moving now [[naco-sankalak-2025]].

| Most people living with HIV (2024) | Most new infections (2024) |
|---|---|
| Maharashtra: 3,99,023 | Bihar: 7,694 |
| Andhra Pradesh: 3,10,451 | Punjab: 6,785 |
| Karnataka: 2,91,348 | Uttar Pradesh: 6,373 |
| Uttar Pradesh: 1,95,427 | Maharashtra: 5,334 |
| Tamil Nadu: 1,65,971 | Karnataka: 4,618 |

Bihar's estimated 1,54,296 people living with HIV are fewer than half Maharashtra's total [[naco-sankalak-2025]], yet Bihar had more new infections in 2024. Bihar and Uttar Pradesh together accounted for more than a fifth of India's estimated new infections, though both have adult HIV rates below the national average [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. In Punjab, new infections were 29% higher in 2024 than in 2010, while across India they fell by 48.7% [[naco-sankalak-2025]].

These are modelled estimates with wide error ranges; Bihar's true figure could be well above or below 7,694. The big southern and western states have many people living with HIV but relatively low rates of new infection [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. The first map shows where HIV has been. The second shows where prevention has to go.

## In Punjab, needles lead. In Bihar and UP, they do not

In Punjab, 56% of people newly diagnosed in 2024-25 said they got HIV from shared needles or syringes, against 11.5% nationally [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. That puts Punjab with Arunachal Pradesh, Tripura and Assam, the states where NACO says injecting drug use is the main route [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Our story on the North-East covers that pattern.

Bihar and Uttar Pradesh are not on that list. Across India, most people newly diagnosed report sex as the route: nearly 74% named heterosexual sex in 2024-25 [[naco-sankalak-2025]].

Public-health programmes speak of "bridge populations": people who may have sex with partners at higher risk of HIV, and then with a wife or regular partner at home. In 2024, NACO put HIV prevalence at 0.81% among truckers and 0.45% among migrant workers, about four times and more than twice the 0.20% among all adults [[naco-sankalak-2025]].

Consider a hypothetical: a 26-year-old from a Bihar village spends eleven months a year on building sites in another state. There are no condoms on site, and a clinic visit costs a day's wages. If he gets HIV, he may feel fine for years [[who-hiv]]. When he goes home for Chhath, he may carry it to a wife who has only ever had one partner.

That is no reason to blame migrants. In a story like his, the risk comes from long separation and from having no condoms, tests or information at work, not from who he is.

## Paid sex, regular partners and what the answers hide

Of 1,63,306 people newly diagnosed in 2024-25, 15.1% named a commercial sex partner as the route, about one in seven [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Self-reported answers like these can be shaped by shame. Female sex workers had an HIV prevalence of 1.13% in 2024, more than five times the adult average [[naco-sankalak-2025]].

That does not make sex workers the source of HIV. They face a higher risk themselves, and blaming them ignores the clients and partners in the same chain. Another number matters as much: 26.5% of people newly diagnosed named a regular partner, such as a spouse, as the route [[naco-sankalak-2025]].

## Bihar and UP: the knowledge gap

Bihar, with the most new infections, also had one of the lowest levels of HIV knowledge among young women. In 2019-21, only 10% of young women aged 15-24 in Bihar and 12% in Uttar Pradesh had comprehensive knowledge of HIV, against 69% in Mizoram [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

The gap runs through protection too. Nationally, only 54.4% of young women aged 15-24 knew where to get a condom in 2019-21, against 87.3% of young men [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. And 35.1% of men aged 15-49 agreed that "contraception is women's business and a man should not have to worry about it" [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Put together: more than a third of men see contraception as women's business, and nearly half of young women do not know where to get a condom.

That is why the second map matters. Services for sex workers and people who inject drugs remain vital, and Punjab needs needle-focused services most of all. But in populous states with low HIV rates, such as Bihar and Uttar Pradesh, much of the risk can sit with people who would never call themselves high-risk: men working far from home, and the partners they return to.

## Prevention that reaches men at work and couples at home

Prevention has to go where men work and travel: building sites, factories, truck stops and railway stations. Free tests and condoms at both ends of the festival journey home could reach men who rarely visit clinics.

It also has to reach couples. NACO offers people living with HIV the chance to have their spouse, partners and children tested, with their consent. In 2024-25, 6.6 lakh such contacts were tested and 4.1% were positive, about ten times the 0.40% among all at-risk people tested [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. One positive test can be the first warning for a whole household.

Treatment protects families too: a person whose treatment keeps HIV undetectable does not pass it on through sex [[who-hiv]]. After a risky encounter, PEP, a 28-day course started as soon as possible and no later than 72 hours, can stop HIV taking hold [[who-pep]]. Our guide to free, confidential HIV testing explains where to go.

None of this needs blame. It needs a test at the right time, a condom in the right pocket, and NACO's toll-free helpline, 1097, which gives confidential advice round the clock in 16 languages [[naco-sankalak-2025]].
bihar-punjab-new-hiv-infections-migratio.hg:
India ki HIV epidemic ke baare mein socho, toh shayad dimaag mein Mumbai, South ke states ya North-East aayenge. HIV ke saath jee rahe logon ki baat karo toh yeh tasveer sahi bhi hai: 2024 mein Maharashtra mein estimated 3,99,023 aise log the, kisi bhi state se zyada, aur sabse ooncha rate North-East mein hai [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Lekin ek doosri list batati hai ki HIV abhi kahan phail raha hai. 2024 mein Bihar mein estimated 7,694 naye infections hue, poore India mein sabse zyada, aur Punjab aur Uttar Pradesh mein bhi Maharashtra se zyada naye infections the [[naco-sankalak-2025]].

## Doosra map: naye infections kahan ho rahe hain

India ke paas HIV ke do maps hain. Pehla un sab logon ko ginta hai jo HIV ke saath jee rahe hain, unko bhi jinhe decades pehle infection hua tha; HIV in 2024 par hamari by-the-numbers story yahi map dikhati hai. Doosra map ek saal ke naye infections ginta hai, aur batata hai ki virus abhi kis taraf badh raha hai [[naco-sankalak-2025]].

| HIV ke saath jee rahe sabse zyada log (2024) | Sabse zyada naye infections (2024) |
|---|---|
| Maharashtra: 3,99,023 | Bihar: 7,694 |
| Andhra Pradesh: 3,10,451 | Punjab: 6,785 |
| Karnataka: 2,91,348 | Uttar Pradesh: 6,373 |
| Uttar Pradesh: 1,95,427 | Maharashtra: 5,334 |
| Tamil Nadu: 1,65,971 | Karnataka: 4,618 |

Bihar mein HIV ke saath jee rahe estimated 1,54,296 log Maharashtra ke aadhe se bhi kam hain [[naco-sankalak-2025]], phir bhi 2024 mein Bihar mein naye infections zyada the. Bihar aur Uttar Pradesh milkar India ke estimated naye infections ke paanchwe hisse se zyada the, jabki dono ka adult HIV rate national average se kam hai [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Punjab mein 2024 ke naye infections 2010 se 29% zyada the, jabki inhi saalon mein poore India mein yeh 48.7% gire [[naco-sankalak-2025]].

Yeh modelled estimates hain aur inme error ki range kaafi badi hai; Bihar ka asli figure 7,694 se kaafi upar ya neeche ho sakta hai. South aur West ke bade states mein HIV ke saath jee rahe log bahut hain, lekin wahan naye infections ka rate kaafi kam hai [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Pehla map dikhata hai ki HIV kahan raha hai. Doosra dikhata hai ki prevention ko kahan jaana hai.

## Punjab mein needles aage hain, Bihar aur UP mein nahi

Punjab mein 2024-25 mein naye diagnose hue logon mein se 56% ne bataya ki HIV shared needles ya syringes se hua, jabki poore India mein yeh 11.5% hai [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Isse Punjab un states ke saath aa jaata hai jahan NACO ke hisaab se injecting drug use sabse bada route hai: Arunachal Pradesh, Tripura aur Assam [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. North-East par hamari story is pattern ko cover karti hai.

Bihar aur Uttar Pradesh is list mein nahi hain. Poore India mein naye diagnose hue zyada tar log sex ko route batate hain: 2024-25 mein lagbhag 74% ne heterosexual sex bataya [[naco-sankalak-2025]].

Public health programmes "bridge populations" ki baat karte hain: aise log jo kabhi un partners ke saath sex karte hain jinhe HIV ka risk zyada hai, aur phir ghar par wife ya regular partner ke saath. 2024 mein NACO ke hisaab se truckers mein HIV prevalence 0.81% aur migrant workers mein 0.45% thi, yaani sab adults ke 0.20% ka lagbhag chaar guna aur do guna se zyada [[naco-sankalak-2025]].

Ek hypothetical socho: Bihar ke ek gaon ka 26 saal ka ladka saal ke gyarah mahine kisi doosre state mein building sites par kaam karta hai. Site par condoms nahi milte, aur clinic jaane ka matlab hai ek din ki dihadi chhodna. Agar use HIV ho jaye, toh ho sakta hai saalon tak use kuch feel hi na ho [[who-hiv]]. Chhath par jab woh ghar lautega, ho sakta hai woh virus apni wife tak pahuncha de, jiski zindagi mein sirf ek hi partner raha hai.

Iska matlab yeh nahi ki migrants ko blame kiya jaye. Aisi kahani mein risk lambe time tak ghar se door rehne se aata hai, aur is baat se ki kaam ki jagah par na condoms hain, na tests, na sahi jaankari. Risk is baat se nahi aata ki woh kaun hai.

## Paid sex, regular partners aur jawabon ke peeche kya chhupa hai

2024-25 mein naye diagnose hue 1,63,306 logon mein se 15.1% ne commercial sex partner ko route bataya, yaani lagbhag har saat mein se ek [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Log jo khud batate hain, un jawabon par sharm ka asar ho sakta hai. 2024 mein female sex workers mein HIV prevalence 1.13% thi, adult average se paanch guna se bhi zyada [[naco-sankalak-2025]].

Iska matlab yeh nahi ki sex workers HIV ka source hain. Unhe khud zyada risk hai, aur unhe blame karne se usi chain ke clients aur partners nazar se chhoot jaate hain. Ek aur number utna hi zaroori hai: naye diagnose hue logon mein se 26.5% ne regular partner ko route bataya, jaise spouse [[naco-sankalak-2025]].

## Bihar aur UP: jaankari ki kami

Sabse zyada naye infections wale Bihar mein young women ke beech HIV ki jaankari bhi sabse kam levels mein se ek thi. 2019-21 mein Bihar ki 15-24 saal ki sirf 10% young women ko HIV ki comprehensive knowledge thi, Uttar Pradesh mein 12%, jabki Mizoram mein 69% [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Protection mein bhi yahi gap hai. 2019-21 mein poore India mein 15-24 saal ki sirf 54.4% young women jaanti thi ki condom kahan milta hai, jabki young men mein yeh 87.3% tha [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Aur 15-49 saal ke 35.1% men ne maana ki "contraception auraton ka kaam hai, aadmi ko iski fikar karne ki zaroorat nahi" [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Dono baaton ko saath rakho: ek-tihai se zyada aadmi contraception ko auraton ka kaam maante hain, aur lagbhag aadhi young women ko pata hi nahi ki condom kahan milta hai.

Isiliye doosra map maayne rakhta hai. Sex workers aur drugs inject karne walon ke liye services aaj bhi bahut zaroori hain, aur Punjab ko sabse zyada needles par focus karne wali services chahiye. Lekin Bihar aur Uttar Pradesh jaise badi abaadi aur kam HIV rate wale states mein bahut sa risk aise logon ke paas ho sakta hai jo khud ko kabhi "high-risk" nahi maanenge: ghar se door kaam karne wale aadmi, aur ghar par unke partners.

## Prevention jo kaam ki jagah par aadmiyon tak aur ghar par couples tak pahunche

Prevention ko wahan jaana hoga jahan aadmi kaam aur safar karte hain: building sites, factories, truck stops aur railway stations. Festival season mein ghar lautne ke safar ke dono siron par free tests aur condoms milein, toh woh aadmi bhi pahunch mein aa sakte hain jo kam hi clinic jaate hain.

Prevention ko couples tak bhi pahunchna hoga. NACO HIV ke saath jee rahe logon ko yeh option deta hai ki unki consent se unke spouse, partners aur bachchon ka test ho. 2024-25 mein aise 6.6 lakh contacts ka test hua aur 4.1% positive nikle, jo test hue sabhi at-risk logon ke 0.40% ka lagbhag das guna hai [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Ek positive test poore ghar ke liye pehli warning ban sakta hai.

Treatment bhi families ko bachata hai: jiska treatment HIV ko undetectable rakhta hai, woh sex ke zariye HIV aage pass nahi karta [[who-hiv]]. Kisi risky encounter ke baad PEP, yaani 28 din ka course jo jitna jaldi ho sake aur 72 ghante ke andar start ho, HIV ko jamne se rok sakta hai [[who-pep]]. Free aur confidential HIV test par hamari guide batati hai ki kahan jaana hai.

Isme kisi ko blame karne ki zaroorat nahi. Zaroorat hai sahi time par test ki, sahi jeb mein condom ki, aur NACO ki toll-free helpline 1097 ki, jo din-raat 16 languages mein confidential advice deti hai [[naco-sankalak-2025]].

breast-cancer-india-screening-gap.en:
Imagine a 44-year-old in Indore who notices a small hard lump in her breast while bathing. It does not hurt. Her daughter has board exams, her mother-in-law needs a knee operation, and a painless lump goes to the bottom of the list. She tells no one for eight months. She is hypothetical. The numbers around her are not. GLOBOCAN 2022 ranked breast cancer the most common cancer in India [[iarc-globocan-india-factsheet-2022]]. The latest edition estimates 2,37,231 new cases and 96,100 deaths in 2024 [[iarc-globocan-india-factsheet-2024]]. Yet when the national health survey asked women aged 15-49 whether they had ever had a breast screening test, 0.6% said yes [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

## India's most common cancer, in numbers

| GLOBOCAN edition | New cases | Deaths | Share of all cancers in Indian women |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2022 | 1,92,020 | 98,337 | 26.6% |
| 2024 | 2,37,231 | 96,100 | 30.4% |

The two rows are not a two-year trend. The inputs and methods changed between editions, so the figures are not directly comparable [[iarc-globocan-india-factsheet-2024]]. Each row says the same thing: breast cancer is the largest single cancer among Indian women, 30.4% of all their cancers in the latest estimate.

These are modelled estimates. But the death figure deserves a second look, because medicine is not helpless against this cancer. WHO says deaths fall when breast cancer is detected and treated early, and that cancerous lumps are more likely to be treated successfully when they are small and have not spread [[who-breast-cancer]]. A toll of 96,100 in a disease where timing decides so much raises one question: how early do Indian women reach a doctor? The screening data is the closest clue we have.

## 0.6% screened

NFHS-5, the national health survey of 2019-21, asked about three cancers. Among women aged 15-49, 0.6% had ever had a screening test for breast cancer, 1.2% for cervical cancer and 0.7% for oral cancer [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

The figure has limits. It is self-reported, and it includes teenagers, whom no one would screen. It also stops at 49, although breast cancer becomes more common in later life [[who-breast-cancer]], so it says nothing about women in their fifties and sixties. Even so, 0.6% does not describe a screening programme with gaps. It describes a country where, for almost every woman, the first breast check comes after she has found something herself.

We have no verified national figure for how many Indian women are diagnosed late. The likely barriers are not hard to picture, though. The lump does not hurt, so it does not feel urgent. A breast is hard to mention to a father-in-law who controls the money, or to a male doctor in a crowded OPD. A day at the hospital is a day's wages. And fear of the word "cancer" keeps women away from the one room where they might hear "it is nothing".

## Changes that need a doctor, and what is usually harmless

WHO lists the changes to act on [[who-breast-cancer]]:

- a lump or thickening in the breast, often without pain
- a change in the size, shape or appearance of the breast
- dimpling, redness, pitting or other changes in the skin
- a change in the nipple or the skin around it
- abnormal or bloody fluid from the nipple

Its instruction is plain: an abnormal breast lump needs medical care, even if it does not hurt [[who-breast-cancer]].

Most breast lumps are not cancer [[who-breast-cancer]]. In teenagers and women in their twenties, the usual causes are fibroadenomas (smooth, rubbery lumps that move under the fingers), fluid-filled cysts, and the lumpiness and tenderness that arrive before a period. Pain alone is rarely the sign.

But "usually harmless" describes a crowd, not your lump, and nobody can tell by touch. If a lump is still there after your next period, see a doctor; at a young age the usual first test is an ultrasound, which is painless. After menopause, do not wait at all.

Two more corrections. Most women diagnosed with breast cancer have no known family history of it [[who-breast-cancer]], so "nobody in our family had it" is no reason to ignore a lump. And a small share of breast cancers occur in men [[who-breast-cancer]]. A lump behind a man's nipple, or in a trans person's chest, needs the same visit.

## Clinical breast exams and mammograms: who needs what

Three tools do three different jobs.

**Breast awareness** means knowing how your breasts normally look and feel, so that a change stands out. It costs nothing and diagnoses nothing. Its job is to shorten the time between a change and a doctor.

**A clinical breast examination** is a trained doctor or nurse looking at and feeling both breasts and armpits. It takes minutes and needs no machine. It can find a lump you missed and show whether you need a scan. It cannot say whether a lump is cancer; that takes imaging and usually a tissue sample.

**A mammogram** is a low-dose X-ray that can show changes before anyone can feel them. WHO describes mammography screening as meant for apparently healthy women, usually aged 50 to 69, and calls it impractical in many countries at present [[who-breast-cancer]].

That matters for India. WHO says early diagnosis is possible even without mass mammography, if people know the signs and are examined and referred quickly [[who-breast-cancer]]. A country at 0.6% can afford that: every woman knows the five changes, every health visit includes the offer of a breast examination, and no lump waits months for a scan.

## Getting checked without waiting for pain

At a government health centre or hospital, or with a private gynaecologist or general surgeon, ask for a breast examination. You can ask for a woman to examine you and for a companion to stay. If a scan is advised, ask which one and why, and keep the report.

If you find a lump, note the date. Do not massage it, and do not wait for it to dissolve or to start hurting. A skin or nipple change with it means go now.

The woman in Indore may well have a harmless lump; most are. Eight months of silence did not change those odds, only the cost of being wrong. One examination would have told her.
breast-cancer-india-screening-gap.hg:
Socho, Indore ki ek 44 saal ki woman ko nahate waqt apne breast mein ek chhoti, sakht gaanth mehsoos hoti hai. Dard nahi hai. Beti ke board exams hain, saas ke ghutne ka operation hona hai, aur bina dard wali gaanth list mein sabse neeche chali jaati hai. Aath mahine tak woh kisi ko nahi batati. Yeh woman hypothetical hai. Uske aas-paas ke numbers asli hain. GLOBOCAN 2022 ne breast cancer ko India ka sabse common cancer rank kiya tha [[iarc-globocan-india-factsheet-2022]]. Latest edition ka estimate 2024 ke liye 2,37,231 naye cases aur 96,100 deaths ka hai [[iarc-globocan-india-factsheet-2024]]. Phir bhi jab national health survey ne 15-49 saal ki women se poocha ki kya unka kabhi breast screening test hua hai, toh sirf 0.6% ne haan kaha [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

## India ka sabse common cancer, numbers mein

| GLOBOCAN edition | Naye cases | Deaths | Indian women ke saare cancers mein hissa |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2022 | 1,92,020 | 98,337 | 26.6% |
| 2024 | 2,37,231 | 96,100 | 30.4% |

Yeh do rows do saal ka trend nahi hain. Dono editions ke beech inputs aur methods badal gaye, isliye figures seedhe compare nahi kiye ja sakte [[iarc-globocan-india-factsheet-2024]]. Har row ek hi baat kehti hai: breast cancer Indian women ka sabse bada single cancer hai, latest estimate mein unke saare cancers ka 30.4%.

Yeh modelled estimates hain. Par deaths wale figure ko dobara dekhna banta hai, kyunki is cancer ke saamne medicine bebas nahi hai. WHO kehta hai ki jab breast cancer jaldi pakda jaaye aur jaldi treat ho, toh deaths kam hoti hain, aur cancer wali gaanth ka treatment tab zyada kaamyaab hota hai jab woh chhoti ho aur faili na ho [[who-breast-cancer]]. Jis bimari mein timing itna kuch tay karti hai, usme 96,100 ka aankda ek sawaal uthata hai: Indian women doctor tak kitni jaldi pahunchti hain? Iska sabse kareebi ishaara screening ke data mein hai.

## Sirf 0.6% ki screening

NFHS-5, yaani 2019-21 ke national health survey ne teen cancers ke baare mein poocha. 15-49 saal ki women mein 0.6% ka kabhi breast cancer ka screening test hua tha, 1.2% ka cervical cancer ka aur 0.7% ka oral cancer ka [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Is figure ki limits hain. Yeh self-reported hai, aur isme teenagers bhi shaamil hain, jinki screening koi karta hi nahi. Yeh 49 par ruk bhi jaata hai, jabki breast cancer badhti umar ke saath zyada common hota hai [[who-breast-cancer]], toh fifties aur sixties ki women ke baare mein yeh kuch nahi batata. Phir bhi 0.6% kisi aise screening programme ki tasveer nahi hai jisme bas kuch gaps hon. Yeh us desh ki tasveer hai jahan lagbhag har woman ka pehla breast check tab hota hai jab use khud kuch mil chuka hota hai.

Kitni Indian women ka diagnosis late hota hai, iska koi verified national figure humare paas nahi hai. Par mumkin rukawatein samajhna mushkil nahi hai. Gaanth mein dard nahi hota, toh woh urgent nahi lagti. Breast ki baat us sasur se karna mushkil hai jiske haath mein paisa hai, ya bheed bhari OPD mein kisi male doctor se. Hospital mein ek din matlab ek din ki mazdoori. Aur "cancer" shabd ka darr women ko usi ek kamre se door rakhta hai jahan shayad unhe sunne ko milta, "kuch nahi hai".

## Kaun se badlaav doctor ko dikhane hain, aur kya aksar harmless hota hai

WHO un badlaavon ki list deta hai jin par action lena hai [[who-breast-cancer]]:

- breast mein gaanth ya thickening, aksar bina dard ke
- breast ke size, shape ya look mein badlaav
- skin mein dimpling, redness, gaddhe ya koi aur badlaav
- nipple ya uske aas-paas ki skin mein badlaav
- nipple se abnormal ya khoon wala fluid

Uski hidayat seedhi hai: breast ki abnormal gaanth ko medical care chahiye, chahe usme dard na ho [[who-breast-cancer]].

Zyadatar breast lumps cancer nahi hote [[who-breast-cancer]]. Teenagers aur twenties ki women mein aam wajahein hoti hain fibroadenoma (chikni, rubber jaisi gaanth jo ungliyon ke neeche hilti hai), fluid se bhare cysts, aur woh lumpiness aur tenderness jo periods se pehle aati hai. Sirf dard hona shayad hi kabhi iska sign hota hai.

Par "aksar harmless" ek bheed ke baare mein kaha jaata hai, tumhari gaanth ke baare mein nahi, aur chhoo kar koi nahi bata sakta. Agar gaanth agle period ke baad bhi wahin hai, toh doctor ko dikhao; kam umar mein aam taur par pehla test ultrasound hota hai, jisme dard nahi hota. Menopause ke baad bilkul wait mat karo.

Do aur galatfehmiyan. Jin women ko breast cancer diagnose hota hai, unmein se zyadatar ki family mein iski koi known history nahi hoti [[who-breast-cancer]], toh "humare ghar mein kisi ko nahi hua" gaanth ko ignore karne ki wajah nahi hai. Aur breast cancers ka ek chhota hissa men mein hota hai [[who-breast-cancer]]. Kisi man ke nipple ke peeche ki gaanth, ya kisi trans person ke chest ki gaanth, ke liye bhi wahi visit zaroori hai.

## Clinical breast exam aur mammogram: kise kya chahiye

Teen tools hain, aur teeno ka kaam alag hai.

**Breast awareness** ka matlab hai jaanna ki tumhare breasts normally kaise dikhte aur mehsoos hote hain, taaki badlaav alag se dikhe. Isme paisa nahi lagta, aur isse koi diagnosis bhi nahi hota. Iska kaam hai badlaav aur doctor ke beech ka time kam karna.

**Clinical breast examination** mein ek trained doctor ya nurse dono breasts aur armpits ko dekhta aur chhoo kar check karta hai. Isme kuch minute lagte hain aur koi machine nahi chahiye. Yeh woh gaanth pakad sakta hai jo tumse chhoot gayi, aur bata sakta hai ki scan chahiye ya nahi. Yeh nahi bata sakta ki gaanth cancer hai ya nahi; uske liye imaging aur aksar tissue ka sample chahiye.

**Mammogram** ek low-dose X-ray hai jo badlaav tab dikha sakta hai jab woh kisi ko mehsoos bhi nahi hote. WHO ke mutabik mammography screening apparently healthy women ke liye hai, aam taur par 50 se 69 saal ki, aur philhaal kai countries mein yeh practical nahi hai [[who-breast-cancer]].

India ke liye yeh baat maayne rakhti hai. WHO kehta hai ki mass mammography ke bina bhi early diagnosis possible hai, agar log signs jaante hon aur unki jaanch aur referral jaldi ho [[who-breast-cancer]]. 0.6% wala desh itna toh kar sakta hai: har woman ko paanchon badlaav pata hon, har health visit mein breast examination ka offer ho, aur kisi gaanth ko scan ke liye mahinon wait na karna pade.

## Dard ka wait kiye bina jaanch karwao

Government health centre ya hospital mein, ya private gynaecologist ya general surgeon ke paas, breast examination maango. Tum keh sakti ho ki jaanch koi woman kare aur koi saath wala room mein rahe. Agar scan ki salah mile, toh poocho kaun sa aur kyun, aur report sambhal kar rakho.

Gaanth mile toh date note kar lo. Uski maalish mat karo, aur uske ghulne ya dard shuru hone ka wait mat karo. Saath mein skin ya nipple mein badlaav ho, toh abhi jao.

Ho sakta hai Indore ki us woman ki gaanth harmless hi ho; zyadatar hoti hain. Aath mahine ki chuppi se yeh odds nahi badle, bas galat nikalne ki keemat badh gayi. Ek examination use bata deta.

cervavac-india-hpv-vaccine-not-used.en:
On 1 September 2022, a Union minister unveiled Cervavac, India's first indigenously developed quadrivalent vaccine against the human papillomavirus, the virus behind most cervical cancers. Its maker, the Serum Institute of India, said it might cost Rs 200-400 a dose [[tribune-cervavac-launch-2022]]. Three and a half years later, on 28 February 2026, India launched its free national HPV campaign for 14-year-old girls [[pib-hpv-campaign-launch-2026]]. The vaccine in the syringes was not Cervavac. It was Gardasil-4, procured in partnership with GAVI, the Vaccine Alliance [[pib-hpv-backgrounder-2026]]. In the government documents we reviewed, nobody explains why.

This is not a story about a dangerous vaccine. Nothing in the record suggests that either one is unsafe. It is a story about a decision affecting about 1.2 crore girls a year that was made out of public view.

## 2022: a made-in-India vaccine and a Rs 200-400 promise

On 12 July 2022, the Drugs Controller General of India granted the Serum Institute market authorisation for Cervavac, the first indigenously developed quadrivalent HPV vaccine, meaning one built against four HPV types [[theprint-cervavac-dcgi-2022]]. It was developed as a public-private partnership with the government's own Department of Biotechnology [[tribune-cervavac-launch-2022]].

At the launch, Minister of State for Science and Technology Jitendra Singh unveiled it. The company said it might be priced between Rs 200 and Rs 400 a dose, adding that "the final prices will be fixed later". The schedule then was two doses for 9-to-14-year-olds and three for ages 15 to 26 [[tribune-cervavac-launch-2022]].

The pitch was self-reliance: a vaccine developed in India, partly with public institutions, at a price that seemed within reach of a public programme. For families who had only ever seen HPV vaccines at private clinics, it sounded like the end of a long wait.

## 2026: the campaign picks Gardasil-4 through GAVI

The wait ended differently. The national programme offers one dose of Gardasil-4, a quadrivalent vaccine against HPV types 6, 11, 16 and 18, to girls aged 14, a yearly group of about 1.2 crore [[pib-hpv-campaign-launch-2026]]. The government's backgrounder says the vaccine is being procured "through a transparent mechanism in partnership with GAVI, the Vaccine Alliance" [[pib-hpv-backgrounder-2026]].

Cervavac is mentioned in the official releases in one place only: the list of vaccines a girl may already have received privately. Such girls are recorded on U-WIN, the digital vaccination register, rather than vaccinated again [[pib-hpv-update-march-2026]]. By 11 September 2026, more than 80 lakh doses had been given under the campaign [[pib-hpv-80-lakh-doses-2026]], every one of them from a programme built on Gardasil-4.

## What the public record does not explain

The record is precise about what happened. It is silent on why.

**The decision.** No published note says who chose Gardasil-4 over Cervavac, when, or on what grounds. If an expert advisory body advised on the choice, its reasoning has not been made public in the documents reviewed.

**The price.** The Rs 200-400 figure was indicative at launch, and the price at which Cervavac is actually sold could not be confirmed [[tribune-cervavac-launch-2022]]. What India pays per dose of Gardasil-4, and how much of that GAVI covers, is not stated either.

**WHO prequalification.** The World Health Organization runs a quality assessment of vaccines, called prequalification. Whether Cervavac holds it, and whether that played any part in the choice, the government documents do not say.

**One dose or two.** Cervavac was launched with a two-dose schedule for 9-to-14-year-olds [[tribune-cervavac-launch-2022]]. The campaign is built on a single dose [[pib-hpv-campaign-launch-2026]]. Whether there is evidence for Cervavac as a single dose is another question the record leaves open.

There may be good reasons behind the choice: price, guaranteed supply, the strength of the evidence for one product over another. But "may" is not an explanation, and a programme for about 1.2 crore girls a year should publish its reasons.

## Two quadrivalent vaccines: what the choice means for parents

For a parent standing in an Ayushman Arogya Mandir today, the answer is simple. The vaccine on offer is free and licensed, and it targets types 16 and 18, which cause more than 80% of cervical cancer cases in India [[pib-hpv-backgrounder-2026]]. Waiting for a different brand means waiting without protection, while the girl gets older.

If your daughter already received Cervavac privately, she does not need a second vaccine; the dose is recorded on U-WIN [[pib-hpv-update-march-2026]]. Vaccination stays voluntary, with parental consent [[pib-hpv-update-march-2026]].

The choice matters more for the country than for any one child. It decides how public money is spent, whether a national programme uses a home-grown product, and whether India's own investment in vaccine research ever reaches its own public clinics.

## The questions that need answers

Parliament has already asked about the campaign. On 21 July 2026, according to a news report of a written reply, the health ministry told it that 52,10,302 girls had been vaccinated by 15 July [[etvbharat-hpv-parliament-2026]]. The same route can be used to ask:

- Why was Gardasil-4 chosen over Cervavac, and will the expert advice behind the decision be published?
- What price per dose does India pay, and who pays it: GAVI, the Centre or both?
- Does Cervavac hold WHO prequalification, and was that a factor?
- Is there evidence for Cervavac as a single dose, and is any study under way?
- Will Cervavac be considered for future years, and at what price?

Any citizen can put the same questions to the Union Health Ministry through an RTI application. Ask them as questions of public accountability. A vaccine choice made in silence feeds rumours, and in a country where too many girls still miss the dose, rumours cost more than any brand.
cervavac-india-hpv-vaccine-not-used.hg:
1 September 2022 ko ek Union minister ne Cervavac unveil ki. Yeh human papillomavirus ke khilaaf India ki pehli indigenously developed quadrivalent vaccine thi, yaani us virus ke khilaaf jo zyadatar cervical cancers ke peeche hai. Ise banane wali company, Serum Institute of India, ne kaha ki iska price Rs 200-400 per dose ho sakta hai [[tribune-cervavac-launch-2022]]. Saadhe teen saal baad, 28 February 2026 ko, India ne 14 saal ki ladkiyon ke liye apna free national HPV campaign launch kiya [[pib-hpv-campaign-launch-2026]]. Syringes mein jo vaccine thi, woh Cervavac nahi thi. Woh Gardasil-4 thi, jo GAVI, the Vaccine Alliance ke saath partnership mein procure hui [[pib-hpv-backgrounder-2026]]. Jo government documents humne dekhe, unmein koi nahi batata kyun.

Yeh kisi khatarnaak vaccine ki story nahi hai. Record mein aisa kuch nahi hai jo kahe ki dono mein se koi bhi unsafe hai. Yeh ek aise faisle ki story hai jo har saal lagbhag 1.2 crore ladkiyon par asar daalta hai aur jo public ki nazar se door liya gaya.

## 2022: ek made-in-India vaccine aur Rs 200-400 ka promise

12 July 2022 ko Drugs Controller General of India ne Serum Institute ko Cervavac ke liye market authorisation diya. Yeh pehli indigenously developed quadrivalent HPV vaccine thi, yaani chaar HPV types ke khilaaf bani vaccine [[theprint-cervavac-dcgi-2022]]. Ise government ke apne Department of Biotechnology ke saath public-private partnership mein develop kiya gaya tha [[tribune-cervavac-launch-2022]].

Launch par Minister of State for Science and Technology Jitendra Singh ne ise unveil kiya. Company ne kaha ki iska price Rs 200 se Rs 400 per dose ke beech ho sakta hai, aur saath mein joda ki "the final prices will be fixed later". Us waqt schedule tha 9 se 14 saal walon ke liye do doses aur 15 se 26 saal walon ke liye teen [[tribune-cervavac-launch-2022]].

Pitch self-reliance ki thi: India mein bani vaccine, jismein public institutions ka bhi hissa tha, aur aisa price jo ek public programme ki pahunch mein lagta tha. Jin families ne HPV vaccines sirf private clinics mein dekhi thi, unhe laga ki lamba intezaar ab khatam hone wala hai.

## 2026: campaign ne GAVI ke zariye Gardasil-4 chuni

Intezaar khatam hua, par alag tarah se. National programme 14 saal ki ladkiyon ko Gardasil-4 ki ek dose deta hai. Yeh HPV type 6, 11, 16 aur 18 ke khilaaf ek quadrivalent vaccine hai, aur target group har saal lagbhag 1.2 crore ladkiyon ka hai [[pib-hpv-campaign-launch-2026]]. Government ka backgrounder kehta hai ki vaccine "through a transparent mechanism in partnership with GAVI, the Vaccine Alliance" procure ho rahi hai [[pib-hpv-backgrounder-2026]].

Official releases mein Cervavac ka zikr sirf ek jagah hai: un vaccines ki list mein jo kisi ladki ko private mein pehle lag chuki ho sakti hain. Aisi ladkiyon ko dobara vaccine nahi lagti; unhe U-WIN par record kiya jaata hai, jo digital vaccination register hai [[pib-hpv-update-march-2026]]. 11 September 2026 tak campaign mein 80 lakh se zyada doses lag chuki thi [[pib-hpv-80-lakh-doses-2026]], aur har ek dose us programme se aayi jo Gardasil-4 par bana hai.

## Public record kya nahi batata

Record yeh bilkul saaf batata hai ki kya hua. Kyun hua, is par woh chup hai.

**Faisla.** Koi published note nahi batata ki Gardasil-4 ko Cervavac par kisne chuna, kab, aur kis basis par. Agar kisi expert advisory body ne is choice par advice di thi, toh uski reasoning un documents mein public nahi hai jo humne dekhe.

**Price.** Rs 200-400 ka figure launch par indicative tha, aur Cervavac asal mein kis price par bikti hai, yeh confirm nahi ho saka [[tribune-cervavac-launch-2022]]. India Gardasil-4 ki ek dose ke liye kitna deta hai, aur usmein se kitna GAVI cover karta hai, yeh bhi kahin nahi likha.

**WHO prequalification.** World Health Organization vaccines ka ek quality assessment karta hai, jise prequalification kehte hain. Cervavac ke paas yeh hai ya nahi, aur kya is choice mein iska koi role tha, government documents nahi batate.

**Ek dose ya do.** Cervavac 9 se 14 saal walon ke liye do-dose schedule ke saath launch hui thi [[tribune-cervavac-launch-2022]]. Campaign single dose par bana hai [[pib-hpv-campaign-launch-2026]]. Cervavac ke single dose ke liye evidence hai ya nahi, yeh ek aur sawaal hai jo record khula chhod deta hai.

Is choice ke peeche achhe reasons ho sakte hain: price, guaranteed supply, ya ek product ke evidence ka doosre se mazboot hona. Lekin "ho sakte hain" koi explanation nahi hai, aur har saal lagbhag 1.2 crore ladkiyon ke programme ko apne reasons publish karne chahiye.

## Do quadrivalent vaccines: parents ke liye is choice ka matlab

Aaj kisi Ayushman Arogya Mandir mein khade parent ke liye jawaab simple hai. Jo vaccine mil rahi hai woh free hai, licensed hai, aur type 16 aur 18 ko target karti hai, jo India mein cervical cancer ke 80% se zyada cases ke liye zimmedar hain [[pib-hpv-backgrounder-2026]]. Kisi doosre brand ka wait karne ka matlab hai bina protection ke wait karna, jabki ladki ki umar badhti ja rahi hai.

Agar tumhari beti ko private mein Cervavac pehle hi lag chuki hai, toh use doosri vaccine ki zaroorat nahi; dose U-WIN par record ho jaati hai [[pib-hpv-update-march-2026]]. Vaccination voluntary hi hai, parents ke consent ke saath [[pib-hpv-update-march-2026]].

Yeh choice kisi ek bachche se zyada desh ke liye maayne rakhti hai. Isi se tay hota hai ki public money kaise kharch hoti hai, kya ek national programme desh mein bana product use karta hai, aur kya vaccine research mein India ka apna investment kabhi uske apne public clinics tak pahunchta hai.

## Woh sawaal jinke jawaab chahiye

Parliament campaign ke baare mein pehle hi pooch chuki hai. Ek written reply ki news report ke mutabik, 21 July 2026 ko health ministry ne use bataya ki 15 July tak 52,10,302 ladkiyon ko vaccine lag chuki thi [[etvbharat-hpv-parliament-2026]]. Isi raaste se yeh bhi poocha ja sakta hai:

- Gardasil-4 ko Cervavac par kyun chuna gaya, aur kya is faisle ke peeche ki expert advice publish hogi?
- India per dose kitna price deta hai, aur kaun deta hai: GAVI, Centre ya dono?
- Kya Cervavac ke paas WHO prequalification hai, aur kya yeh ek factor tha?
- Kya Cervavac ke single dose ke liye evidence hai, aur kya koi study chal rahi hai?
- Kya aane wale saalon mein Cervavac par vichaar hoga, aur kis price par?

Koi bhi citizen yahi sawaal RTI application ke zariye Union Health Ministry se pooch sakta hai. Inhe public accountability ke sawaalon ki tarah poocho. Chuppi mein liya gaya vaccine ka faisla rumours ko badhaata hai, aur jis desh mein ab bhi bahut saari ladkiyon ki dose chhoot rahi hai, wahan rumours kisi bhi brand se zyada mehnge padte hain.

cervical-cancer-screening-india-numbers.en:
Cervical cancer is one of the few cancers that medicine can see coming. A screening test finds abnormal cells years before they turn into cancer, and treating them at that stage is a simple procedure [[who-cervical]]. India has barely used that head start. In the National Family Health Survey of 2019-21 (NFHS-5), only 1.2% of women aged 15-49 had ever been screened [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

The numbers below measure that gap. They also show why the HPV vaccine campaign launched in 2026 cannot close it for women who are already adults.

## The second cancer of Indian women

The latest GLOBOCAN estimate gives India 79,360 new cervical cancer cases and 36,319 deaths in 2024. It is the second most common cancer among Indian women, 10.2% of their cancers, behind breast cancer at 30.4% [[iarc-globocan-india-factsheet-2024]]. India accounts for about 13% of the world's new cases (79,360 of 6,04,196) and about 13% of the deaths (36,319 of 2,79,583) [[iarc-globocan-cervix-factsheet-2024]].

If you remember bigger numbers, you are not wrong. The previous edition, GLOBOCAN 2022, estimated 1,27,526 cases and 79,906 deaths [[iarc-globocan-india-factsheet-2022]]. The two cannot be compared. The 2024 edition uses different registry inputs and methods, so the drop is mostly a change in estimation, not proof that the disease fell by a third in two years.

GLOBOCAN's India figures are models, not counts; in 2022 even the deaths were modelled, as India had no national mortality data. That uncertainty is a finding in itself.

## 1.2% against 70%: the screening gap

| Measure | Number |
|---|---|
| Women aged 15-49 ever screened for cervical cancer, 2019-21 | 1.2% |
| Women aged 35-49 ever screened | 2% |
| Women aged 15-49 ever screened for breast cancer | 0.6% |
| Best state for cervical screening: Tamil Nadu | 7% |
| WHO target: women screened by 35 and again by 45 | 70% |

The survey figures are from NFHS-5 [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. After Tamil Nadu came Puducherry at 5% and Mizoram at 4%. The best-performing state in the country stood at one-tenth of the WHO target.

A fair reading needs one correction. WHO's 70% is about women by the ages of 35 and 45, while the 15-49 group includes teenagers who are not due for a test. The closer comparison is women aged 35-49, and there the figure is 2%. The correction changes almost nothing.

The data is old and self-reported. A newer round, NFHS-6 (2023-24), came out as provisional fact sheets in May 2026 [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]]. Its screening figure is not yet in our verified data, so NFHS-5 remains the number we can stand behind.

## WHO's 90-70-90 and where India stands

On 17 November 2020, 194 countries committed to WHO's cervical cancer elimination strategy. It sets three targets for 2030: 90% of girls fully vaccinated against HPV by 15, 70% of women screened with a high-performance test by 35 and again by 45, and 90% of women with cervical disease treated [[who-cervical-elimination-launch-2020]]. Elimination means 4 or fewer cases per 100,000 women [[who-cervical-cancer-factsheet-2026]].

India's position on each:

- Vaccination: the nationwide free campaign for girls aged 14 began on 28 February 2026, with a single dose for an annual cohort of about 1.2 crore girls [[pib-hpv-campaign-launch-2026]]. By 11 September 2026, more than 80 lakh doses had been given, roughly two-thirds of one year's cohort [[pib-hpv-80-lakh-doses-2026]]. No national coverage percentage has been published.
- Screening: 1.2% of women aged 15-49, and 2% of those aged 35-49, in 2019-21 [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. The deadline is four years away.
- Treatment: we found no verified national figure to report.

> India began vaccinating its daughters in 2026. For adult women, the 2019-21 survey found screening at 1.2%.

## Vaccines protect daughters, screening protects mothers

The campaign vaccinates 14-year-olds. A woman who is 35 today is outside it. This is a slow disease: abnormal cells usually take many years to become cancer [[who-cervical]].

The slow clock cuts both ways. On that timeline, many of the cancers diagnosed in the coming years will grow from infections that adult women already carry, and a dose given to a schoolgirl in 2026 cannot reach them. But the same years are the window in which a screening test can find abnormal cells and a doctor can remove them. For adult women, screening is the protection on offer. Vaccinated girls will need it too when they grow up [[who-cervical]].

Imagine a 38-year-old woman in Sitapur who takes her daughter to the health centre for the free dose. The girl's vaccination is recorded. Nobody asks the mother whether she has ever been screened. In one visit, the system protects the daughter and walks past the woman standing next to her.

Some women have less time. Women living with HIV are 6 times more likely to develop cervical cancer than women without HIV [[who-cervical-cancer-factsheet-2026]]. With untreated HIV the process can be much faster, and WHO advises women living with HIV to start screening earlier and repeat it more often [[who-cervical]].

## What an adult woman should do this year

WHO recommends regular screening with a high-performance test, and its target is that every woman is screened by 35 and again by 45 [[who-cervical-elimination-launch-2020]]. Ask a government health centre which test it offers: an HPV test, a Pap smear, or VIA, a visual check of the cervix.

- If you are 35 or older and have never been screened, go this year; if you are younger, ask a doctor when to start. Do not wait for symptoms: precancers rarely cause any [[who-cervical]].
- A positive screening result is not a cancer diagnosis. If precancerous changes are confirmed, treatment is usually quick and effective [[who-cervical]].
- Bleeding between periods, after sex or after menopause needs a doctor at any age, screened or not [[who-cervical]].
- HPV is a very common virus. A positive test says nothing about your character or your marriage.

A country where 1.2% of women had been screened has no shortage of women who are due. If you are one of them, the test is something you can ask for.
cervical-cancer-screening-india-numbers.hg:
Cervical cancer un gine-chune cancers mein se hai jinhe medicine aate hue dekh sakti hai. Screening test abnormal cells ko cancer banne se saalon pehle pakad leta hai, aur us stage pe unka ilaaj ek simple procedure hai [[who-cervical]]. India ne is badhat ka faayda lagbhag uthaya hi nahi. 2019-21 ke National Family Health Survey (NFHS-5) mein 15-49 saal ki sirf 1.2% women ki kabhi bhi screening hui thi [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Neeche ke numbers isi gap ko naapte hain. Ye bhi dikhate hain ki 2026 mein shuru hua HPV vaccine campaign un women ke liye ye gap kyun nahi bhar sakta jo pehle se adult hain.

## Indian women ka doosra sabse common cancer

Latest GLOBOCAN estimate ke hisaab se India mein 2024 mein cervical cancer ke 79,360 naye cases aaye aur 36,319 mautein hui. Ye Indian women mein doosra sabse common cancer hai, unke cancers ka 10.2%, breast cancer ke baad jo 30.4% hai [[iarc-globocan-india-factsheet-2024]]. Duniya ke naye cases mein India ka hissa lagbhag 13% hai (6,04,196 mein se 79,360), aur mauton mein bhi lagbhag 13% (2,79,583 mein se 36,319) [[iarc-globocan-cervix-factsheet-2024]].

Agar tumhe isse bade numbers yaad hain, toh tum galat nahi ho. Pichhle edition, GLOBOCAN 2022, ne 1,27,526 cases aur 79,906 mauton ka estimate diya tha [[iarc-globocan-india-factsheet-2022]]. In dono ko compare nahi kiya ja sakta. 2024 wala edition alag registry inputs aur methods use karta hai, isliye ye giraavat zyada tar estimate karne ke tareeke ka badlaav hai, is baat ka saboot nahi ki do saal mein bimaari ek tihaai ghat gayi.

GLOBOCAN ke India figures models hain, ginti nahi; 2022 mein mautein bhi model se nikaali gayi thi, kyunki India ke paas national mortality data nahi tha. Ye uncertainty apne aap mein ek finding hai.

## 1.2% banaam 70%: screening ka gap

| Kya naapa gaya | Number |
|---|---|
| 15-49 saal ki women jinki kabhi cervical cancer screening hui, 2019-21 | 1.2% |
| 35-49 saal ki women jinki kabhi screening hui | 2% |
| 15-49 saal ki women jinki kabhi breast cancer screening hui | 0.6% |
| Cervical screening mein sabse aage state: Tamil Nadu | 7% |
| WHO target: women ki screening 35 tak aur phir 45 tak | 70% |

Survey ke figures NFHS-5 se hain [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Tamil Nadu ke baad Puducherry 5% pe aur Mizoram 4% pe tha. Desh ka sabse achchha perform karne wala state bhi WHO target ke dasve hisse pe khada tha.

Sahi tareeke se padhne ke liye ek correction zaroori hai. WHO ka 70% un women ke baare mein hai jinki screening 35 aur 45 ki umar tak honi chahiye, jabki 15-49 wale group mein teenagers bhi hain jinka test abhi due hi nahi. Zyada sahi comparison 35-49 saal ki women ka hai, aur wahan figure 2% hai. Is correction se tasveer lagbhag nahi badalti.

Data purana bhi hai aur self-reported bhi. Ek naya round, NFHS-6 (2023-24), May 2026 mein provisional fact sheets ke roop mein aaya [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]]. Uska screening figure abhi hamare verified data mein nahi hai, isliye NFHS-5 hi wo number hai jiske peeche hum khade ho sakte hain.

## WHO ka 90-70-90 aur India kahan khada hai

17 November 2020 ko 194 countries ne WHO ki cervical cancer elimination strategy ko commit kiya. Isme 2030 ke liye teen targets hain: 90% ladkiyon ko 15 ki umar tak HPV ka poora vaccine, 70% women ki high-performance test se screening 35 tak aur phir 45 tak, aur cervical disease wali 90% women ka ilaaj [[who-cervical-elimination-launch-2020]]. Elimination ka matlab hai har 100,000 women pe 4 ya usse kam cases [[who-cervical-cancer-factsheet-2026]].

Har target pe India ki position:

- Vaccination: 14 saal ki ladkiyon ke liye nationwide free campaign 28 February 2026 ko shuru hua, single dose ke saath, aur har saal ka cohort lagbhag 1.2 crore ladkiyon ka hai [[pib-hpv-campaign-launch-2026]]. 11 September 2026 tak 80 lakh se zyada doses lag chuki thi, yaani ek saal ke cohort ka lagbhag do-tihaai [[pib-hpv-80-lakh-doses-2026]]. Koi national coverage percentage publish nahi hua hai.
- Screening: 2019-21 mein 15-49 saal ki 1.2% women, aur 35-49 saal ki 2% women [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Deadline chaar saal door hai.
- Treatment: hume report karne layak koi verified national figure nahi mila.

> India ne 2026 mein apni betiyon ko vaccine lagana shuru kiya. Adult women ke liye 2019-21 ke survey mein screening 1.2% pe mili thi.

## Vaccine betiyon ko bachata hai, screening maaon ko

Campaign 14 saal ki ladkiyon ko vaccine lagata hai. Jo woman aaj 35 ki hai, wo iske bahar hai. Ye ek dheemi bimaari hai: abnormal cells ko cancer banne mein aam taur pe kai saal lagte hain [[who-cervical]].

Ye dheemi ghadi dono taraf kaam karti hai. Is timeline pe, aane wale saalon mein diagnose hone wale bahut se cancers un infections se banenge jo adult women mein pehle se hain, aur 2026 mein kisi schoolgirl ko lagi dose un tak nahi pahunch sakti. Lekin yahi saal wo window bhi hain jisme screening test abnormal cells ko dhoondh sakta hai aur doctor unhe hata sakta hai. Adult women ke liye jo protection maujood hai, wo screening hai. Vaccine lagwa chuki ladkiyon ko bhi bade hoke iski zaroorat padegi [[who-cervical]].

Socho, Sitapur mein 38 saal ki ek woman apni beti ko free dose ke liye health centre le jaati hai. Ladki ka vaccination record ho jaata hai. Maa se koi nahi poochhta ki uski kabhi screening hui hai ya nahi. Ek hi visit mein system beti ko bacha leta hai aur uske bagal mein khadi woman ke paas se nikal jaata hai.

Kuch women ke paas waqt aur kam hota hai. HIV ke saath jee rahi women mein cervical cancer hone ke chances, bina HIV wali women ke muqable, 6 guna zyada hote hain [[who-cervical-cancer-factsheet-2026]]. Bina ilaaj ke HIV mein ye process kaafi tez ho sakta hai, aur WHO HIV ke saath jee rahi women ko screening jaldi shuru karne aur zyada baar karane ki salaah deta hai [[who-cervical]].

## Adult woman ko is saal kya karna chahiye

WHO high-performance test se regular screening ki salaah deta hai, aur uska target hai ki har woman ki screening 35 tak aur phir 45 tak ho [[who-cervical-elimination-launch-2020]]. Sarkaari health centre se poochho ki wahan kaun sa test hota hai: HPV test, Pap smear, ya VIA, yaani cervix ki aankhon se jaanch.

- Agar tum 35 ya usse zyada ki ho aur kabhi screening nahi hui, toh isi saal jao; kam umar ho toh doctor se poochho ki kab shuru karna hai. Symptoms ka intezaar mat karo: precancers mein aksar koi symptom hota hi nahi [[who-cervical]].
- Screening ka positive result cancer ka diagnosis nahi hai. Agar precancerous changes confirm hote hain, toh ilaaj aam taur pe jaldi ho jaata hai aur effective hota hai [[who-cervical]].
- Periods ke beech, sex ke baad ya menopause ke baad bleeding ho toh kisi bhi umar mein doctor ko dikhao, screening hui ho ya nahi [[who-cervical]].
- HPV ek bahut common virus hai. Positive test tumhare character ya tumhari shaadi ke baare mein kuch nahi kehta.

Jis desh mein sirf 1.2% women ki screening hui thi, wahan aisi women ki koi kami nahi jinka test due hai. Agar tum unmein se ek ho, toh ye test tum khud maang sakti ho.

condom-failure-typical-use-myths.en:
Out of every 100 people who rely on external condoms for a year, about 13 end up with a pregnancy [[who-fp]]. That figure gets quoted as proof that condoms "don't work". It shows something else: the condom rarely fails on its own. People fail it, mostly because nobody ever showed them how to use one.

## Perfect use and typical use: where 13 comes from

Doctors measure a method twice. Perfect use is the method used correctly every single time. Typical use is a year of ordinary life, including the night the condom went on halfway through and the night it stayed in the drawer. The 13 is typical use [[who-fp]]. With perfect use, pregnancies are far fewer. The gap is human error, not weak latex. An intact condom does not let sperm through.
