The errors are few and well known: putting it on after genital contact has begun; leaving no space at the tip; using one that is expired, or heat-damaged after months in a wallet or under a bike seat; tearing the packet open with teeth; adding petroleum jelly, body lotion or cooking oil, which weaken latex; reusing one; or the wrong size, which slips or strains.

With no method at all, about 85 in 100 have a pregnancy within a year, and with withdrawal about 20 [[who-fp]]. In NFHS-5, 9.5% of currently married women reported condom use, while 10.3% relied on traditional methods such as withdrawal and counting "safe days" [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Mistakes included, the condom already beats withdrawal.

## Myth: two condoms are safer than one

The truth: two condoms rub against each other, and the friction makes both more likely to tear or slip. The same goes for wearing an external condom with an internal one, the pouch worn inside the vagina. Used alone, the internal condom is a real option, though about 21 in 100 users have a pregnancy in a year of typical use [[who-fp]].

If the fear is pregnancy, the second layer that works is a second method, not a second condom. Fewer than 1 in 100 users of an IUD or implant get pregnant in a year, and about 7 in 100 on the pill [[who-fp]]. A condom plus one of these is called dual protection: one method against pregnancy, the condom against infection.

## Myth: condoms protect against every STI

The truth: condoms are the only contraceptive that also protects against sexually transmitted infections, including HIV [[who-fp]]. They greatly reduce the risk. They do not remove it [[who-sti]].

Condoms work best against infections carried in body fluids. They protect less against infections that cause sores outside the area a condom covers, such as syphilis and genital herpes [[who-sti]]. Syphilis has not gone away: of 46.2 lakh syphilis screenings at government STI clinics in 2024-25, 43,482 were reactive [[naco-sankalak-2025]].

Many STIs cause no symptoms, so only a test can tell [[who-sti]]. Protection is three things: a condom every time, testing, and the vaccines for HPV and hepatitis B [[who-sti]]. The opposite rumour, that condoms have "tiny holes" and are useless against HIV, is just as false.

## Why young women can't get them and young men won't use them

In NFHS-5, only 54.4% of women aged 15-24 knew where to get a condom, against 87.3% of young men [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. The survey assumed that any man who had used a condom in the past year knew a source, which lifts the male figure slightly, so the real gap may be a little narrower. It is still wide.

Imagine a couple in their early twenties in Kanpur. He buys the condoms, so he decides whether one is used, when it goes on, and whether the packet that has ridden in his wallet since Diwali is good enough. She has never handled one, cannot tell whether it is on correctly, and has been taught that asking would say something about her character. Every error listed above becomes easier.

In the same survey, 35.1% of men agreed that contraception is "women's business and a man should not have to worry about it" [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Yet the condom is the one common method that a man wears. The complaint that condoms "ruin sex" is usually a complaint about fit, dryness or fumbling, and each has a fix: another size, a thinner condom, water-based lubricant, practice. Refusing one moves the whole risk of pregnancy and infection onto the partner.

## Using one correctly, and what to do if it breaks

- Check the expiry date and the packet; store condoms away from heat.
- Open the packet with fingers, not teeth. Put the condom on before any genital contact, pinching the tip.
- Use only water-based or silicone-based lubricant.
- Hold the base while withdrawing. Use a new one every time, and put the used one in a bin.

If a condom breaks or slips off, act by the clock. Emergency contraception works up to 5 days after sex, and sooner is better; it is not abortion and does not end an established pregnancy [[who-ec]]. If there is any chance of HIV exposure, see a doctor urgently: PEP must start as soon as possible, no later than 72 hours after exposure, and is taken for 28 days [[who-pep]]. NACO's toll-free helpline 1097 offers confidential counselling round the clock [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Take a pregnancy test if a period is late, and ask about STI tests at one of the 1,127 government Suraksha Clinics [[naco-sankalak-2025]].

If you are under 18, buying condoms or asking questions is not an offence. But under POCSO any sexual act with a person under 18 is an offence whatever either person agreed to, and anyone who knows of it must report it [[indiacode-pocso-act-2012]], so a doctor cannot promise secrecy. You are still entitled to care. This is general information, not legal advice. If anything happened without your agreement, call 1098 or 112.

The condom is not a weak method. It is a good method handed to people who were never taught to use it, and much of that 13 in 100 is what the silence costs.
condom-failure-typical-use-myths.hg:
Jo 100 log ek saal tak external condom ke bharose rehte hain, unmein se lagbhag 13 ke yahan pregnancy ho jaati hai [[who-fp]]. Yeh number aksar is baat ke saboot ki tarah ghumaya jaata hai ki condom "kaam nahi karte". Asal mein yeh kuch aur dikhata hai: condom apne aap kam hi fail hota hai. Use log fail karte hain, zyadatar isliye ki kisi ne kabhi sikhaya hi nahi ki ise use kaise karna hai.

## Perfect use aur typical use: yeh 13 aata kahan se hai

Doctor kisi bhi method ko do baar naapte hain. Perfect use matlab method har ek baar bilkul sahi tareeke se use hua. Typical use matlab aam zindagi ka ek saal, jismein woh raat bhi shaamil hai jab condom beech mein jaakar pehna gaya, aur woh raat bhi jab woh drawer mein hi pada reh gaya. 13 wala number typical use ka hai [[who-fp]]. Perfect use mein pregnancies kaafi kam hoti hain. Yeh gap insaani galti ka hai, kamzor latex ka nahi. Jo condom saabut hai, usmein se sperm paar nahi hota.

Galtiyan thodi si hain aur jaani-pehchaani hain: genital contact shuru hone ke baad condom pehenna; tip par jagah na chhodna; expired condom use karna, ya aisa jo mahinon wallet mein ya bike ki seat ke neeche garmi se kharab ho chuka ho; packet daanton se phaadna; petroleum jelly, body lotion ya khaane ka tel lagana, jo latex ko kamzor karte hain; ek hi condom dobara use karna; ya galat size, jo ya toh slip hota hai ya zyada khinchta hai.

Koi method na ho toh 100 mein se lagbhag 85 ke yahan ek saal ke andar pregnancy hoti hai, aur withdrawal ke saath lagbhag 20 [[who-fp]]. NFHS-5 mein 9.5% currently married women ne condom use bataya, jabki 10.3% withdrawal aur "safe days" ginne jaise traditional methods par tiki thi [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Galtiyon ke saath bhi condom withdrawal se behtar hi hai.

## Myth: do condom ek se zyada safe hain

Sach yeh hai: do condom aapas mein ragadte hain, aur is friction se dono ke phatne ya slip hone ka chance badh jaata hai. Yahi baat external condom ke saath internal condom pehenne par bhi laagu hoti hai; internal condom woh pouch hai jo vagina ke andar pehna jaata hai. Akele use ho toh internal condom ek asli option hai, haalaanki typical use ke ek saal mein 100 mein se lagbhag 21 users ke yahan pregnancy hoti hai [[who-fp]].

Agar darr pregnancy ka hai, toh kaam karne wali doosri layer doosra method hai, doosra condom nahi. IUD ya implant use karne walon mein ek saal mein 100 mein 1 se bhi kam pregnant hote hain, aur pill par lagbhag 7 [[who-fp]]. Condom ke saath inmein se koi ek method ho, toh ise dual protection kehte hain: ek method pregnancy ke khilaaf, condom infection ke khilaaf.

## Myth: condom har STI se bachata hai

Sach yeh hai: condom akela contraceptive hai jo sexually transmitted infections, HIV samet, se bhi bachata hai [[who-fp]]. Woh risk ko bahut kam karta hai. Khatm nahi karta [[who-sti]].

Condom un infections ke khilaaf sabse achha kaam karta hai jo body fluids se phailte hain. Jo infections condom se dhake hisse ke bahar ghaav (sores) karte hain, jaise syphilis aur genital herpes, unse woh kam bachata hai [[who-sti]]. Syphilis kahin gaya nahi hai: 2024-25 mein government STI clinics mein hui 46.2 lakh syphilis screenings mein se 43,482 reactive nikli [[naco-sankalak-2025]].

Kai STIs mein koi symptom nahi hota, isliye sirf test hi bata sakta hai [[who-sti]]. Protection teen cheezon se banti hai: har baar condom, testing, aur HPV aur hepatitis B ke vaccines [[who-sti]]. Ulti afwaah, ki condom mein "chhote-chhote chhed" hote hain aur woh HIV ke khilaaf bekaar hai, utni hi jhoothi hai.

## Young women ko condom milte kyun nahi, aur young men pehente kyun nahi

NFHS-5 mein 15-24 saal ki sirf 54.4% women ko pata tha ki condom kahan milta hai, jabki young men mein yeh 87.3% tha [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Survey ne yeh maan liya tha ki jis bhi man ne pichhle saal condom use kiya, use source pata hai; isse men ka figure thoda upar jaata hai, toh asli gap thoda kam ho sakta hai. Phir bhi gap bada hai.

Kanpur ke ek couple ko imagine kijiye, dono bees-baais saal ke. Condom ladka khareedta hai, isliye wahi tay karta hai ki condom use hoga ya nahi, kab pehna jaayega, aur Diwali se wallet mein pada packet chalega ya nahi. Ladki ne kabhi condom haath mein liya hi nahi, use pata nahi chalta ki sahi pehna gaya hai ya nahi, aur use yahi sikhaya gaya hai ki poochhne se uske character par sawaal uthega. Upar ginayi har galti aur aasaan ho jaati hai.

Usi survey mein 35.1% men ne maana ki contraception "aurton ka kaam hai, mard ko iski fikr karne ki zaroorat nahi" [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Phir bhi condom hi woh ek common method hai jo mard pehenta hai. "Condom se sex ka maza kharab ho jaata hai" wali shikayat aam taur par fit, dryness ya hadbadi ki shikayat hoti hai, aur har ek ka hal hai: doosra size, patla condom, water-based lubricant, practice. Condom se mana karne ka matlab hai pregnancy aur infection ka poora risk partner par daal dena.

## Sahi tareeke se use karna, aur phat jaaye toh kya karna hai

- Expiry date aur packet check kijiye; condom garmi se door rakhiye.
- Packet ungliyon se kholiye, daanton se nahi. Kisi bhi genital contact se pehle condom pehniye, tip ko chutki se dabaa kar.
- Sirf water-based ya silicone-based lubricant use kijiye.
- Bahar nikaalte waqt base ko pakde rakhiye. Har baar naya condom lijiye, aur use kiya hua dustbin mein daaliye.

Condom phat jaaye ya nikal jaaye toh ghadi dekh kar chaliye. Emergency contraception sex ke baad 5 din tak kaam karti hai, aur jitni jaldi utna behtar; yeh abortion nahi hai aur established pregnancy ko khatm nahi karti [[who-ec]]. Agar HIV exposure ka zara bhi chance hai toh turant doctor se miliye: PEP jitni jaldi ho sake shuru hona chahiye, exposure ke 72 ghante ke andar hi, aur 28 din tak liya jaata hai [[who-pep]]. NACO ki toll-free helpline 1097 chaubees ghante confidential counselling deti hai [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Period late ho toh pregnancy test kijiye, aur 1,127 government Suraksha Clinics mein se kisi ek par STI tests ke baare mein poochhiye [[naco-sankalak-2025]].

Agar aap 18 se kam umar ke hain, toh condom khareedna ya sawaal poochhna koi offence nahi hai. Lekin POCSO ke tahat 18 se kam umar ke kisi bhi insaan ke saath koi bhi sexual act offence hai, chahe dono ne kuch bhi agree kiya ho, aur jise bhi iski jaankari ho use report karna zaroori hai [[indiacode-pocso-act-2012]], isliye doctor secrecy ka vaada nahi kar sakta. Phir bhi care par aapka haq hai. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi. Agar kuch bhi aapki marzi ke bina hua hai, toh 1098 ya 112 par call kijiye.

Condom kamzor method nahi hai. Yeh ek achha method hai jo un logon ke haath mein de diya gaya jinhe kabhi use karna sikhaya hi nahi gaya, aur 100 mein 13 ka zyadatar hissa usi chuppi ki keemat hai.

congenital-syphilis-pregnancy-testing-ga.en:
A blood test at the first antenatal check-up and a course of penicillin injections are enough to stop a baby being born with syphilis. India's own programme data for 2024-25 show where that short chain breaks. Only 77% of pregnant women were tested for syphilis. Of the 10,545 found infected, treatment was recorded for 9,065. And in the whole country, just 212 babies were recorded with congenital syphilis [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. That last number looks like good news. It is more likely a measure of how little anyone is looking.

## An old, cheap injection, and the babies it never reaches

Syphilis is a bacterial infection, passed on mainly through sex, and many people who have it notice no symptoms. In pregnancy it can cross to the baby. Left untreated, it can end in stillbirth, in the death of a newborn, or in a baby born with the infection, which is called congenital syphilis [[who-syphilis]]. Such a baby can have problems with the bones, blood, eyes, hearing or brain, and some of the signs are noticed only later in life [[who-syphilis]].

The cure is neither new nor costly. Benzathine penicillin, given by injection, is the only treatment WHO recommends for pregnant women with syphilis; an early infection needs a single dose and later stages need more [[who-syphilis]]. The earlier in pregnancy it is given, the better the baby is protected.

So every baby born with syphilis marks a step somebody missed: no test, a late test, no treatment, or a partner who was never treated and passed the infection back.

## One pregnant woman in four not tested

In 2024-25, 77% of pregnant women in India were tested for syphilis, against 84% for HIV [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Both are blood tests meant to be done at the same antenatal visit. Nothing in medicine explains why one should reach fewer women than the other.

| Year | Pregnant women tested for syphilis | Tested for HIV |
|---|---|---|
| 2017-18 | 30% | not given |
| 2020-21 | 54% | 76% |
| 2024-25 | 77% | 84% |

The climb from 30% is real progress. But it still leaves roughly one pregnant woman in four untested [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Coverage is measured against an estimate of pregnancies, not a headcount. NACO itself says the 2024-25 figure dipped slightly from the year before because of reporting and supply problems.

Imagine a 21-year-old at a primary health centre two hours from the district hospital, at her first check-up. Her blood is drawn and the HIV test is done. The syphilis kits ran out last month. She is told it will be done "next time", and the next time she comes, she is in labour. She is a hypothetical. But a "supply problem" in a national report is this scene, repeated at one health centre after another.

## 10,545 mothers found, one in seven not recorded as treated

India identified 10,545 pregnant women with syphilis in 2024-25, double the 5,228 found in 2021-22 [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. The rise largely reflects more testing, not necessarily more infection. Look harder and you find more.

Of those 10,545 women, 9,065, or 86%, received treatment [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. That leaves roughly one woman in seven who carried an infection dangerous to her baby and for whom no treatment is on record. Some may have been treated at another hospital and never entered in the register. Others were lost between the test and the injection: a result that came back late, a referral to a hospital too far away, a family that did not see why a woman who felt well needed injections. The data cannot say which.

And these are only the women who were tested. How many infected mothers are among the untested, no one knows.

## 212 babies: why the count is almost certainly too low

Against 10,545 infected mothers, the programme recorded 212 babies with congenital syphilis in 2024-25. Of them, 189, or 89%, were treated [[naco-sankalak-2025]].

Treating the mother protects the baby, so nobody should expect the two numbers to match. But the mothers not recorded as treated alone outnumber the recorded babies several times over, before a single untested woman is counted. Three things suggest the figure is too low.

- **Someone has to look.** Diagnosis depends on examining the baby and following up infants exposed in the womb. A baby can seem healthy at birth and show signs only later [[who-syphilis]]. If the family has gone home and nobody calls them back, that baby is never counted.
- **It counts infants only.** It says nothing about pregnancies that ended in miscarriage or stillbirth, which are among the harms syphilis causes [[who-syphilis]].
- **Reporting is patchy.** NACO notes that Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Haryana and Chandigarh reported zero treatment of such babies despite documented cases [[naco-sankalak-2025]].

> A low count of sick babies is good news only if someone is looking for them.

## The North-East hotspots, and the test every pregnant woman should ask for

Nationally, 0.05% of pregnant and breastfeeding women tested positive for syphilis in 2024-25. In Arunachal Pradesh the figure was 1.86%, in Meghalaya 1.32% and in Mizoram 1.15% [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. In those states a missed antenatal test is a far bigger gamble than the national average suggests.

A positive test in pregnancy says nothing about a woman's character and does not show who had the infection first. It shows that a test did its job. What should follow is treatment for her, a test and treatment for her partner, and a follow-up plan for the baby.

If you are pregnant, or someone in your family is, ask at the first check-up for the syphilis test by name, along with the HIV test, and ask to see both results. If the centre has no kit, ask to be referred. India has 1,127 government STI clinics, branded Suraksha Clinics, at district hospitals and medical colleges [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. If the result is positive, the injections are a cure, and the sooner they start, the safer the baby.
congenital-syphilis-pregnancy-testing-ga.hg:
Pehle antenatal check-up par ek blood test aur penicillin ke injections ka course, bas itna kaafi hai ki koi baby syphilis ke saath paida na ho. India ka apna programme data (2024-25) dikhata hai ki yeh chhoti si chain kahan tootti hai. Sirf 77% pregnant women ka syphilis test hua. Jin 10,545 mein infection mila, unmein se 9,065 ka treatment record hua. Aur poore desh mein sirf 212 babies congenital syphilis ke saath record hue [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Yeh aakhri number achhi khabar jaisa lagta hai. Zyada chances yeh hain ki yeh bas itna batata hai ki dhoondha hi kitna kam ja raha hai.

## Ek purana, sasta injection, aur woh babies jin tak yeh pahunchta hi nahi

Syphilis ek bacterial infection hai jo zyada tar sex se failta hai, aur jinhe yeh hota hai unmein se bahut logon ko koi symptoms mehsoos hi nahi hote. Pregnancy mein yeh maa se baby tak pahunch sakta hai. Ilaaj na ho toh nateeja stillbirth ho sakta hai (yaani baby ka mara hua paida hona), newborn ki maut ho sakti hai, ya baby infection ke saath paida ho sakta hai, jise congenital syphilis kehte hain [[who-syphilis]]. Aise baby ko haddiyon, khoon, aankhon, sunne ki shakti ya dimaag se judi problems ho sakti hain, aur kuch signs zindagi mein kaafi baad mein jaakar dikhte hain [[who-syphilis]].

Ilaaj na naya hai, na mehenga. Benzathine penicillin ka injection hi woh akela treatment hai jo WHO syphilis wali pregnant women ke liye recommend karta hai; shuruaati infection mein ek dose kaafi hoti hai aur baad ke stages mein zyada lagti hain [[who-syphilis]]. Pregnancy mein yeh jitni jaldi lage, baby utna zyada safe rehta hai.

Isliye syphilis ke saath paida hua har baby kisi chhoote hue step ka nishaan hai: test hua hi nahi, test der se hua, treatment nahi mila, ya partner ka ilaaj kabhi hua hi nahi aur usne infection wapas de diya.

## Har chaar mein se ek pregnant woman ka test nahi hua

2024-25 mein India mein 77% pregnant women ka syphilis test hua, jabki HIV test 84% ka [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Dono blood tests hain aur dono ek hi antenatal visit par hone chahiye. Medicine mein aisi koi wajah nahi jo samjha sake ki ek test doosre se kam women tak kyun pahunchta hai.

| Saal | Pregnant women jinka syphilis test hua | HIV test hua |
|---|---|---|
| 2017-18 | 30% | data nahi diya |
| 2020-21 | 54% | 76% |
| 2024-25 | 77% | 84% |

30% se yahan tak pahunchna asli progress hai. Lekin ab bhi lagbhag har chaar mein se ek pregnant woman ka test nahi hota [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Coverage pregnancies ke estimate ke against naapi jaati hai, asli headcount ke against nahi. NACO khud kehta hai ki 2024-25 ka figure pichhle saal se thoda gira, reporting aur supply ki problems ki wajah se.

Socho ek 21 saal ki ladki, jo district hospital se do ghante door ke primary health centre par apne pehle check-up ke liye aayi hai. Uska blood liya jaata hai aur HIV test ho jaata hai. Syphilis ki kits pichhle mahine khatam ho gayi thin. Use kaha jaata hai ki "agli baar" ho jaayega, aur agli baar jab woh aati hai, tab woh labour mein hoti hai. Yeh ek hypothetical hai. Lekin national report mein likha "supply problem" asal mein yahi scene hai, ek ke baad ek health centre par dohraya hua.

## 10,545 maayein mili, har saat mein se ek ka treatment record mein nahi

2024-25 mein India ne 10,545 pregnant women mein syphilis pehchaana, jo 2021-22 ke 5,228 ka double hai [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Yeh badhat zyada tar zyada testing ki wajah se hai, zaroori nahi ki infection badha ho. Jitna zyada dhoondhoge, utna zyada milega.

In 10,545 women mein se 9,065 ko, yaani 86% ko, treatment mila [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Bachti hain lagbhag har saat mein se ek woman, jiske andar aisa infection tha jo uske baby ke liye khatarnaak hai aur jiske treatment ka koi record nahi. Ho sakta hai kuch ka ilaaj kisi doosre hospital mein hua ho aur register mein chadha hi na ho. Baaki test aur injection ke beech kahin chhoot gayin: result der se aaya, referral itne door ke hospital ka mila ki jaana mushkil tha, ya family ko samajh nahi aaya ki jo aurat theek mehsoos kar rahi hai use injections kyun chahiye. Data yeh nahi bata sakta ki kiske saath kya hua.

Aur yeh sirf woh women hain jinka test hua. Jinka test nahi hua, unmein kitni infected maayein hain, yeh kisi ko nahi pata.

## 212 babies: yeh ginti almost pakka kam kyun hai

10,545 infected maaon ke saamne, programme ne 2024-25 mein congenital syphilis wale 212 babies record kiye. Unmein se 189 ka, yaani 89% ka, treatment hua [[naco-sankalak-2025]].

Maa ka ilaaj baby ko bachata hai, isliye kisi ko yeh umeed nahi karni chahiye ki dono numbers barabar honge. Lekin sirf woh maayein jinka treatment record mein nahi hai, record hue babies se kai guna zyada hain, aur abhi tak ek bhi untested woman ko gina nahi gaya. Teen baatein batati hain ki yeh figure asal se kam hai.

- **Kisi ko dhoondhna padta hai.** Diagnosis baby ki jaanch par aur pet mein exposed hue infants ke follow-up par tika hai. Baby paida hote waqt healthy lag sakta hai aur signs baad mein dikh sakte hain [[who-syphilis]]. Agar family ghar ja chuki hai aur koi unhe wapas nahi bulata, toh woh baby kabhi gina hi nahi jaata.
- **Yeh sirf infants ki ginti hai.** Yeh un pregnancies ke baare mein kuch nahi batati jo miscarriage ya stillbirth par khatam hui, jabki yeh dono syphilis se hone wale nuksaan mein shaamil hain [[who-syphilis]].
- **Reporting adhoori hai.** NACO note karta hai ki Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Haryana aur Chandigarh ne documented cases hone ke bawajood aise babies ka zero treatment report kiya [[naco-sankalak-2025]].

> Bimaar babies ki kam ginti tabhi achhi khabar hai jab koi unhe dhoondh raha ho.

## North-East ke hotspots, aur woh test jo har pregnant woman ko maangna chahiye

National level par 2024-25 mein 0.05% pregnant aur breastfeeding women ka syphilis test positive aaya. Arunachal Pradesh mein yeh figure 1.86% tha, Meghalaya mein 1.32% aur Mizoram mein 1.15% [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. In states mein antenatal test ka chhoot jaana national average se kahin bada risk hai.

Pregnancy mein positive test kisi aurat ke character ke baare mein kuch nahi kehta, aur yeh bhi nahi batata ki infection pehle kisko tha. Yeh sirf itna batata hai ki test ne apna kaam kiya. Iske baad teen cheezein honi chahiye: uska treatment, uske partner ka test aur treatment, aur baby ke follow-up ka plan.

Agar tum pregnant ho, ya tumhari family mein koi hai, toh pehle check-up par HIV test ke saath syphilis test naam lekar maango, aur dono results dekhne ko kaho. Centre par kit na ho toh referral maango. India mein 1,127 government STI clinics hain, jinhe Suraksha Clinics kehte hain, district hospitals aur medical colleges mein [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Result positive aaye toh injections se yeh infection theek ho jaata hai, aur ilaaj jitni jaldi shuru ho, baby utna safe.

contraceptive-methods-compared-effective.en:
Every contraceptive comes with one number that matters more than any rumour about it: how many pregnancies there are among 100 people relying on it during the first year of ordinary, imperfect use. For an implant or an IUD, fewer than 1. For the pill, about 7. For the external condom, about 13. For withdrawal, about 20. With no method at all, about 85 [[who-fp]]. India's choices run almost the other way round.

## The number that matters: pregnancies per 100 users a year

Doctors measure effectiveness in two ways. Perfect use is what a method achieves when it is used exactly right, every time. Typical use is real life: the pill forgotten after a late night, the condom put on halfway through, the month a couple "took a chance". Typical use is the number to choose by, because it describes ordinary people.

Here is how the main methods compare with what married women in India actually used. The effectiveness column is WHO's [[who-fp]]; the usage column comes from the National Family Health Survey, NFHS-5 [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

| Method | Pregnancies per 100 users in a year, typical use | Married women using it, 2019-21 |
|---|---|---|
| Sterilisation, female or male | permanent, among the most effective | 37.9% female, 0.3% male |
| IUD, such as the Copper-T | fewer than 1 | 2.1% |
| Injectable | about 4 | 0.6% |
| Pill | about 7 | 5.1% |
| External condom | about 13 | 9.5% |
| Traditional methods (withdrawal, "safe days") | about 20 for withdrawal | 10.3% |

The pattern is simple. Methods that need no action on the day, such as an implant, an IUD or sterilisation, almost never fail. Methods that depend on remembering, timing or self-control in the moment fail far more often, and the gap between their perfect and typical use is mostly human error. The internal condom fares worse still, at about 21 in 100 [[who-fp]].

## What Indian couples actually use

In NFHS-5, 66.7% of currently married women were using some method of contraception and 56.4% a modern one, up from 48% for modern methods in 2015-16 [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. That is progress, but look at the mix.

Female sterilisation alone, at 37.9%, makes up about two thirds of all modern method use. For every married woman whose husband has had a vasectomy, more than a hundred have had the operation themselves [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Part of the reason sits in men's answers to the same survey: 35.1% agreed that contraception is "women's business and a man should not have to worry about it" [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

The next biggest group is not the pill or the IUD. It is traditional methods, mostly withdrawal and counting "safe days", at 10.3%. More married women rely on them than on the pill, the IUD and the injectable put together [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Put the two columns side by side and India's family planning looks like this: rely on timing, luck or a condom until the family is complete, then sterilise the woman. The methods built to space children reliably barely register. And these figures cover only currently married women; unmarried people who have sex are not in the table at all.

## The most reliable reversible methods are the least used

An IUD such as the Copper-T is placed in the uterus by a trained provider and works for years [[who-fp]]. The copper version contains no hormones, and it can be removed whenever a woman chooses. Fitted within five days of unprotected sex, a copper IUD is also the most effective form of emergency contraception [[who-ec]]. Yet only 2.1% of married women used an IUD, and just 0.6% the injectable [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

WHO lists the usual barriers: limited choice and access, fear of side effects, and cultural or religious opposition [[who-fp]]. Consider a 24-year-old in Lucknow with a one-year-old, who wants to wait before a second child. At home the choices on offer are condoms her husband dislikes, "being careful", or nothing until the operation after the last child. The method that would cover her whole gap with no daily effort is the one nobody mentions. Some side effects are real, such as heavier periods in the first months with a copper IUD, but they are reasons to switch methods, not to go without.

The gap adds up: about 20 in 100 for every year a couple relies on withdrawal, fewer than 1 with an IUD [[who-fp]]. Across the years between two children, that is often the difference between a planned family and an unplanned one.

## Only condoms also protect against STIs

Pregnancy is only half the comparison. Condoms are the only contraceptive method that also protects against sexually transmitted infections, including HIV [[who-fp]]. Sterilisation, the IUD, the pill and the injectable do nothing against infections.

Condoms are highly effective against STIs but not complete protection: they do not fully guard against infections that cause sores outside the area they cover, such as syphilis and genital herpes [[who-sti]]. Many STIs cause no symptoms, so a partner who looks and feels well can still carry one [[who-sti]].

That is why many people use dual protection: a condom against infection plus a more reliable method against pregnancy, such as an IUD or the pill. Two condoms worn together are not dual protection; they rub and tear more easily.

## Questions to ask a doctor before choosing

No method is best for everyone, and some are unsafe with certain health conditions or medicines, so a doctor or trained health worker should assess you before you start or switch. Take these questions with you:

- How many in 100 typical users get pregnant in a year on this method?
- Which side effects are common, and how long do they usually last?
- How do I stop it, and how soon can I get pregnant afterwards?
- Does it protect against STIs, or do I need condoms as well?
- If it fails or I miss a dose, what is my backup? Emergency contraception works up to five days after sex, and sooner is better [[who-ec]].

The right method is the one that fits your body, your plans and your ability to use it correctly. Start that choice with the numbers, not the rumours.
contraceptive-methods-compared-effective.hg:
Har contraceptive ke saath ek number aata hai jo uske baare mein kisi bhi afwaah se zyada maayne rakhta hai: us par tike 100 logon mein, aam aur adhoore use ke pehle saal mein, kitni pregnancies hoti hain. Implant ya IUD ke saath 1 se kam. Pill ke saath lagbhag 7. External condom ke saath lagbhag 13. Withdrawal ke saath lagbhag 20. Koi method na ho toh lagbhag 85 [[who-fp]]. India ki choices lagbhag ulti disha mein chalti hain.

## Jo number sach mein maayne rakhta hai: har saal 100 users mein pregnancies

Doctor effectiveness do tarah se naapte hain. Perfect use matlab method ko har baar bilkul sahi tareeke se use karna. Typical use matlab real life: late night ke baad bhooli hui pill, beech mein jaakar pehna gaya condom, woh mahina jab couple ne "chance le liya". Choose karte waqt typical use wala number dekhiye, kyunki woh aam logon ki asli zindagi batata hai.

Neeche dekhiye ki main methods ek doosre se kaise compare karte hain, aur India mein shaadishuda aurtein asal mein kya use kar rahi thi. Effectiveness wala column WHO ka hai [[who-fp]]; usage wala column National Family Health Survey, NFHS-5 se hai [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

| Method | Typical use mein har saal 100 users par pregnancies | Use karne wali shaadishuda aurtein, 2019-21 |
|---|---|---|
| Sterilisation, aurat ya mard ki | permanent, sabse effective methods mein se | 37.9% female, 0.3% male |
| IUD, jaise Copper-T | 1 se kam | 2.1% |
| Injectable | lagbhag 4 | 0.6% |
| Pill | lagbhag 7 | 5.1% |
| External condom | lagbhag 13 | 9.5% |
| Traditional methods (withdrawal, "safe days") | withdrawal mein lagbhag 20 | 10.3% |

Pattern seedha hai. Jin methods mein us din kuch karna nahi padta, jaise implant, IUD ya sterilisation, woh lagbhag kabhi fail nahi hote. Jo methods yaad rakhne, timing ya us pal ke self-control par tike hain, woh kahin zyada fail hote hain, aur unke perfect aur typical use ke beech ka gap zyadatar insaani galti hai. Internal condom aur bhi peechhe hai, 100 mein lagbhag 21 par [[who-fp]].

## Indian couples asal mein kya use karte hain

NFHS-5 mein 66.7% currently married aurtein koi na koi contraceptive method use kar rahi thi aur 56.4% koi modern method; 2015-16 mein modern methods ka figure 48% tha [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Yeh progress hai, lekin mix dekhiye.

Akela female sterilisation, 37.9% par, saare modern method use ka lagbhag do-tihaai hai. Har us shaadishuda aurat ke muqable, jiske pati ne vasectomy karwayi hai, sau se zyada aurtein aisi hain jinhone khud operation karwaya hai [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Iski ek wajah usi survey mein mardon ke jawabon mein dikhti hai: 35.1% ne maana ki contraception "aurton ka kaam hai, mard ko iski fikr karne ki zaroorat nahi" [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Doosra sabse bada group pill ya IUD nahi hai. Woh hai traditional methods, zyadatar withdrawal aur "safe days" ginna, 10.3% par. Pill, IUD aur injectable ko mila kar jitni shaadishuda aurtein use karti hain, usse zyada in traditional methods par tiki hain [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Dono columns ko saath rakhiye toh India ki family planning kuch aisi dikhti hai: family poori hone tak timing, kismat ya condom ke bharose raho, phir aurat ka operation karwa do. Bachchon ke beech bharosemand gap rakhne ke liye bane methods mushkil se dikhte hain. Aur yeh figures sirf currently married aurton ke hain; jo unmarried log sex karte hain, woh is table mein hain hi nahi.

## Sabse bharosemand reversible methods sabse kam use hote hain

Copper-T jaisa IUD ek trained provider uterus mein lagata hai, aur woh saalon tak kaam karta hai [[who-fp]]. Copper wale version mein koi hormone nahi hota, aur aurat jab chahe use nikalwa sakti hai. Unprotected sex ke paanch din ke andar lagwaya jaaye toh copper IUD emergency contraception ka sabse effective tareeka bhi hai [[who-ec]]. Phir bhi sirf 2.1% shaadishuda aurtein IUD use karti thi, aur sirf 0.6% injectable [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

WHO aam rukaavatein ginata hai: kam choice aur pahunch, side effects ka darr, aur samaaj ya dharm ki taraf se virodh [[who-fp]]. Lucknow ki ek 24 saal ki aurat ko imagine kijiye, jiska ek saal ka bachcha hai aur jo doosre bachche se pehle rukna chahti hai. Ghar mein uske saamne options hain: condoms jo uske pati ko pasand nahi, "dhyaan rakhna", ya aakhri bachche ke baad operation tak kuch bhi nahi. Jo method bina roz ki mehnat ke uska poora gap cover kar deta, usi ka koi naam nahi leta. Kuch side effects asli hote hain, jaise copper IUD ke pehle kuch mahinon mein periods ka heavy hona, lekin yeh method badalne ki wajah hain, bina method ke rehne ki nahi.

Yeh gap judta jaata hai: withdrawal par tike har saal ke liye 100 mein lagbhag 20, IUD ke saath 1 se kam [[who-fp]]. Do bachchon ke beech ke saalon mein aksar yahi planned aur unplanned family ka fark ban jaata hai.

## Sirf condom STIs se bhi bachata hai

Pregnancy comparison ka sirf aadha hissa hai. Condom akela contraceptive method hai jo sexually transmitted infections, HIV samet, se bhi bachata hai [[who-fp]]. Sterilisation, IUD, pill aur injectable infections ke khilaaf kuch nahi karte.

Condom STIs ke khilaaf bahut effective hai, lekin poori suraksha nahi: jo infections condom se dhake hisse ke bahar ghaav (sores) karte hain, jaise syphilis aur genital herpes, unse woh poori tarah nahi bachata [[who-sti]]. Kai STIs mein koi symptom nahi hota, isliye jo partner dikhne aur mehsoos karne mein bilkul theek hai, woh bhi infection le kar chal sakta hai [[who-sti]].

Isiliye kai log dual protection use karte hain: infection ke khilaaf condom, aur pregnancy ke khilaaf ek zyada bharosemand method, jaise IUD ya pill. Ek saath pehne gaye do condom dual protection nahi hain; woh aapas mein ragadte hain aur aasaani se phat jaate hain.

## Method chunne se pehle doctor se poochhne wale sawaal

Koi bhi method sabke liye best nahi hota, aur kuch methods kuch health conditions ya dawaiyon ke saath safe nahi hote, isliye shuru karne ya badalne se pehle doctor ya trained health worker aapko check kare. Yeh sawaal saath le jaiye:

- Is method par typical use mein 100 mein se kitne log ek saal mein pregnant hote hain?
- Kaunse side effects common hain, aur aam taur par kitne din rehte hain?
- Ise kaise band karun, aur uske baad kitni jaldi pregnant ho sakti hoon?
- Kya yeh STIs se bachata hai, ya mujhe condom bhi chahiye?
- Agar yeh fail ho jaaye ya dose chhoot jaaye, toh mera backup kya hai? Emergency contraception sex ke baad paanch din tak kaam karti hai, aur jitni jaldi utna behtar [[who-ec]].

Sahi method woh hai jo aapke shareer, aapke plans aur use sahi tareeke se use kar paane ki aapki capacity mein fit ho. Yeh choice numbers se shuru kijiye, afwaahon se nahi.

erectile-dysfunction-heart-disease-warni.en:
Imagine a 41-year-old accountant in Nagpur. For six months his erections have been unreliable. He drinks most evenings, smokes at work and has not had his blood pressure checked in years. Instead of seeing a doctor, he orders "sex power" capsules from an ad on his phone and takes them in secret. Whether they seem to work or not, the question a doctor would have asked first goes unasked: what is causing this, and is it a sign of something like diabetes or high blood pressure?

## What erectile dysfunction is, and what it is not

Erectile dysfunction (ED), also called impotence, means being unable to get an erection, or unable to keep one long enough to have sex [[nhs-ed]]. One bad night is not ED. Most men occasionally fail to get or keep an erection, usually because of stress, tiredness or drinking too much, and that is nothing to worry about [[nhs-ed]]. Doctors start paying attention when it keeps happening.

ED is very common, particularly in men over 40, and treatment can usually help [[nhs-ed]]. It is not a "gupt rog", a shameful secret disease of the private parts. Often it is a signal about the whole body.

## The blood-pressure, cholesterol and blood-sugar link

An erection depends on blood flowing into the penis; the main ED medicines work by increasing that blood flow [[nhs-ed]]. When ED happens often, it may be caused by high blood pressure, high cholesterol, diabetes, depression, anxiety or hormone problems [[nhs-ed]]. That is why repeated erection problems deserve a doctor's visit rather than a capsule: they might be a sign of a health condition that can be treated [[nhs-ed]].

So when a man in his thirties or forties reports unreliable erections, a good doctor does not just hand him a pill. She asks about his lifestyle and relationships and checks his blood pressure [[nhs-ed]], and she may test his blood sugar and cholesterol. For some men, the visit about their sex life is the visit that finds their diabetes or high blood pressure early enough to treat.

## Alcohol, stress and medicines

Drinking too much is one of the usual reasons for an occasional failure [[nhs-ed]], and alcohol problems are common among Indian men. The National Mental Health Survey 2015-16 found that 9% of Indian men had an alcohol use disorder, against 0.5% of women [[nimhans-nmhs-summary-2016]]. It also found a treatment gap of 86% for alcohol use disorders: most people who needed help were not getting it [[nimhans-nmhs-summary-2016]]. Over the years, drinking also raises the risk of liver disease, heart disease, depression and anxiety [[who-alcohol]].

The mind matters too. Stress, anxiety and depression can all cause ED [[nhs-ed]]. The same survey found mental health conditions overall more common among men (13.9%) than women (7.5%) [[nimhans-nmhs-summary-2016]]. The fear can feed itself: a man who failed once may worry next time, and that worry can make the next failure more likely.

ED can also be a side effect of some medicines; if one of yours is the cause, the doctor may switch you to a different one [[nhs-ed]]. Do not stop a prescribed medicine on your own.

## Why the 'sex power' ad is illegal

Section 3 of the Drugs and Magic Remedies (Objectionable Advertisements) Act, 1954 bans advertising any drug for "the maintenance or improvement of the capacity of human beings for sexual pleasure" [[sc-ima-order-mar-2025]]. The Act's Schedule also lists sexual impotence. Advertising a drug that claims to treat it is a crime: up to six months in jail, a fine or both for a first conviction, and up to one year in jail, a fine or both for a repeat [[sc-ima-order-mar-2025]].

Yet the ads are everywhere. On 26 March 2025, in Indian Medical Association v. Union of India, the Supreme Court said that "there is no implementation of the 1954 Act in its true letter and spirit", and ordered states to appoint officers to enforce it and to set up ways for the public to complain, such as a toll-free number or email [[sc-ima-order-mar-2025]].

A capsule bought from an ad tells you nothing reliable about what is inside it. Even erection medicines bought online can be fake: many websites sell fakes, and ingredients can vary from one pack to another [[nhs-ed]]. And if a capsule does seem to work, it treats the symptom and hides the warning. The man in Nagpur gets his erection back for a night; his blood pressure stays unchecked.

## Which doctor, which tests, which treatments

Start with a general physician or family doctor. The specialists who treat ED are urologists; a psychiatrist or trained sex therapist helps when the cause is mainly anxiety, depression or the relationship. Check that any doctor has a recognised medical degree and state medical council registration.

Expect questions about your drinking, smoking, medicines and relationship, and whether you still get erections at other times, such as when you wake up [[nhs-ed]]. Expect basic checks, and possibly blood tests for sugar, cholesterol or hormones.

Treatment depends on the cause:

- **Lifestyle:** losing weight, exercising, eating well, stopping smoking, reducing stress and cutting down on alcohol can sometimes help [[nhs-ed]].
- **Treating the cause:** high blood pressure, high cholesterol and hormone problems can be treated with medicine, and a medicine that is causing ED may be switched [[nhs-ed]].
- **Prescription tablets:** medicines called PDE-5 inhibitors, such as sildenafil and tadalafil, increase blood flow to the penis [[nhs-ed]]. Take them only on a doctor's advice, especially if you take any heart medicine.
- **Vacuum pumps:** they work for most men and can be used when tablets are not suitable or do not work [[nhs-ed]].
- **Counselling and sex therapy:** alone or with a partner, when ED is linked to emotional or mental health problems [[nhs-ed]].

If drinking, anxiety or low mood is part of it, Tele-MANAS on 14416 is the Health Ministry's free, round-the-clock mental-health helpline [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]].

Erection trouble is not a verdict on anyone's manhood. Treated as a symptom rather than a secret, it can be an early warning worth having.
erectile-dysfunction-heart-disease-warni.hg:
Socho, Nagpur mein ek 41 saal ka accountant hai. Pichhle chhe mahine se uska erection bharose ka nahi raha. Wo lagbhag har shaam peeta hai, office mein smoke karta hai, aur saalon se usne apna blood pressure check nahi karwaya. Doctor ke paas jaane ki jagah wo phone pe ek ad dekh ke "sex power" capsules mangwa leta hai aur chhup ke khaata hai. Capsules kaam karte lagein ya nahi, dono haalat mein wo sawaal kabhi nahi poocha jaata jo doctor sabse pehle poochta: ye kyun ho raha hai, aur kahin ye diabetes ya high blood pressure jaisi kisi cheez ka sign toh nahi?

## Erectile dysfunction kya hai, aur kya nahi

Erectile dysfunction (ED), jise impotence bhi kehte hain, ka matlab hai erection na aa paana, ya sex ke liye kaafi der tak tika na reh paana [[nhs-ed]]. Ek buri raat ED nahi hai. Zyada tar aadmiyon ke saath kabhi-kabhar aisa hota hai ki erection na aaye ya na tike, aksar stress, thakaan ya zyada peene ki wajah se, aur isme chinta ki koi baat nahi [[nhs-ed]]. Doctor tab dhyaan dete hain jab ye baar-baar hone lage.

ED bahut common hai, khaaskar 40 se upar ke aadmiyon mein, aur ilaaj se aksar sudhaar hota hai [[nhs-ed]]. Ye koi "gupt rog" nahi hai, private parts ki koi sharam wali chhupi bimaari nahi. Aksar ye poore shareer ke baare mein ek signal hota hai.

## Blood pressure, cholesterol aur blood sugar ka connection

Erection is baat pe tika hai ki penis mein khoon bhare; ED ki main dawaiyan isi blood flow ko badha ke kaam karti hain [[nhs-ed]]. Jab ED baar-baar ho, toh iske peeche high blood pressure, high cholesterol, diabetes, depression, anxiety ya hormone ki problems ho sakti hain [[nhs-ed]]. Isiliye baar-baar hone wali erection ki problem capsule nahi, doctor ki visit maangti hai: ye kisi aisi health condition ka sign ho sakti hai jiska ilaaj ho sakta hai [[nhs-ed]].

Toh jab tees ya chaalees ki umar ka koi aadmi bataata hai ki uska erection bharose ka nahi raha, toh achha doctor use sirf ek goli thama ke nahi bhejta. Wo uski lifestyle aur rishton ke baare mein poochti hai aur uska blood pressure check karti hai [[nhs-ed]], aur blood sugar aur cholesterol ka test bhi karwa sakti hai. Kuch aadmiyon ke liye sex life ke baare mein ki gayi wahi visit unki diabetes ya high blood pressure itni jaldi pakad leti hai ki waqt rehte ilaaj ho sake.

## Sharaab, stress aur dawaiyan

Zyada peena kabhi-kabhar erection na aane ya na tikne ki aam wajahon mein se hai [[nhs-ed]], aur Indian men mein sharaab ki problem common hai. National Mental Health Survey 2015-16 ne paaya ki 9% Indian men ko alcohol use disorder tha, jabki women mein ye 0.5% tha [[nimhans-nmhs-summary-2016]]. Isi survey mein alcohol use disorders ka treatment gap 86% nikla: jinhe help chahiye thi, unmein se zyada tar ko mil hi nahi rahi thi [[nimhans-nmhs-summary-2016]]. Saalon tak peene se liver ki bimaari, heart disease, depression aur anxiety ka risk bhi badhta hai [[who-alcohol]].

Mann bhi maayne rakhta hai. Stress, anxiety aur depression, ye sab ED ka kaaran ban sakte hain [[nhs-ed]]. Usi survey mein mental health conditions kul milaake women (7.5%) se zyada men (13.9%) mein paayi gayi [[nimhans-nmhs-summary-2016]]. Ye darr khud ko aur badha sakta hai: jo aadmi ek baar fail hua, wo agli baar pehle se tension mein reh sakta hai, aur wahi tension agli baar fail hone ke chances badha sakti hai.

ED kuch dawaiyon ka side effect bhi ho sakta hai; agar tumhari koi dawa iski wajah hai, toh doctor use badal ke doosri de sakte hain [[nhs-ed]]. Prescribe ki hui dawa apne mann se band mat karo.

## 'Sex power' ka ad illegal kyun hai

Drugs and Magic Remedies (Objectionable Advertisements) Act, 1954 ka Section 3 kisi bhi aisi dawa ke ad pe ban lagata hai jo "the maintenance or improvement of the capacity of human beings for sexual pleasure" ke liye ho, yaani sexual pleasure ki capacity banaye rakhne ya badhane ke liye [[sc-ima-order-mar-2025]]. Act ke Schedule mein sexual impotence bhi listed hai. Iska ilaaj karne ka daawa karne wali dawa ka ad dena crime hai: pehli conviction pe chhe mahine tak jail, fine ya dono, aur dobara conviction pe ek saal tak jail, fine ya dono [[sc-ima-order-mar-2025]].

Phir bhi ye ads har jagah hain. 26 March 2025 ko, Indian Medical Association v. Union of India case mein, Supreme Court ne kaha ki "there is no implementation of the 1954 Act in its true letter and spirit", yaani 1954 ka Act sahi maayne mein laagu hi nahi hua, aur states ko order diya ki ise enforce karne ke liye officers appoint karein aur public ke complaint karne ke tareeke banayein, jaise toll-free number ya email [[sc-ima-order-mar-2025]].

Ad dekh ke khareeda gaya capsule tumhe bharose se ye nahi batata ki uske andar kya hai. Online khareedi gayi erection ki dawaiyan bhi nakli ho sakti hain: bahut si websites fake dawaiyan bechti hain, aur ek pack se doosre pack mein ingredients badal sakte hain [[nhs-ed]]. Aur agar capsule kaam karta hua lage, tab bhi wo sirf symptom dabata hai aur warning ko chhupa deta hai. Nagpur wale aadmi ko ek raat ke liye erection wapas mil jaata hai; uska blood pressure bina check ke reh jaata hai.

## Kaunsa doctor, kaunse tests, kaunsa ilaaj

Shuruaat general physician ya family doctor se karo. ED ka ilaaj karne wale specialist urologists hote hain; agar cause zyada tar anxiety, depression ya rishta hai, toh psychiatrist ya trained sex therapist madad karte hain. Check karo ki doctor ke paas recognised medical degree aur state medical council ka registration ho.

Doctor tumhare peene, smoking, dawaiyon aur rishte ke baare mein poochenge, aur ye bhi ki kya tumhe kabhi aur waqt pe, jaise subah uthte hue, ab bhi erection hota hai [[nhs-ed]]. Basic checks ki ummeed rakho, aur shayad sugar, cholesterol ya hormones ke blood tests ki bhi.

Ilaaj cause pe depend karta hai:

- **Lifestyle:** wazan kam karna, exercise, achha khaana, smoking chhodna, stress kam karna aur sharaab kam karna kabhi-kabhi madad kar sakta hai [[nhs-ed]].
- **Cause ka ilaaj:** high blood pressure, high cholesterol aur hormone ki problems ka dawa se ilaaj ho sakta hai, aur jo dawa ED kar rahi hai use badla ja sakta hai [[nhs-ed]].
- **Prescription ki goliyan:** PDE-5 inhibitors kehlane wali dawaiyan, jaise sildenafil aur tadalafil, penis mein blood flow badhati hain [[nhs-ed]]. Inhe sirf doctor ki salaah pe lo, khaaskar agar tum dil ki koi dawa lete ho.
- **Vacuum pumps:** ye zyada tar aadmiyon ke liye kaam karte hain, aur tab use ho sakte hain jab goliyan suit na karein ya kaam na karein [[nhs-ed]].
- **Counselling aur sex therapy:** akele ya partner ke saath, jab ED emotional ya mental health problems se juda ho [[nhs-ed]].

Agar peena, anxiety ya udaasi iska hissa hai, toh Tele-MANAS 14416 Health Ministry ki free, 24 ghante chalne wali mental-health helpline hai [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]].

Erection ki problem kisi ki mardaangi par faisla nahi hai. Ise raaz ki tarah nahi, symptom ki tarah treat karo, toh ye ek kaam ki early warning ban sakti hai.

first-cervical-screening-test-guide.en:
Cervical cancer is one of the few cancers that can be stopped before it starts: a short test finds the warning signs years in advance. Yet in 2019-21, only 2% of Indian women aged 35-49 said they had ever been screened [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. The latest GLOBOCAN estimate for India is 79,360 new cases and 36,319 deaths in 2024 [[iarc-globocan-india-factsheet-2024]].

Imagine a 36-year-old schoolteacher in Nagpur whose colleague has just been diagnosed. She wants the test but is too embarrassed to ask anyone three things: will it hurt, will they ask whether I am married, and what if they find something. Here are the answers.

## Who should be screened, and when

Screening is for adults who feel well. WHO advises starting at age 30 and repeating the test every 5 to 10 years. Women living with HIV should start at 25 and repeat it every 3 to 5 years [[who-cervical]], because WHO puts their risk at six times that of women without HIV [[who-cervical-cancer-factsheet-2026]]. The global target is for 70% of women to be screened by 35 and again by 45 [[who-cervical-elimination-launch-2020]].

Three things do not change this advice:

- **The HPV vaccine.** Vaccinated women still need screening [[who-cervical]].
- **Marriage.** The test is about your cervix, not your marital status. HPV, the virus behind this cancer, spreads through sexual contact, and almost all sexually active people get it at some point [[who-cervical]]. If you have never had any sexual contact, your risk is much lower; ask a doctor when to start.
- **Feeling fine.** Precancers rarely cause symptoms [[who-cervical]].

Symptoms are different. Bleeding between periods, after sex or after menopause, or unusual discharge, needs a doctor at any age.

## VIA, Pap and HPV tests: what each checks

All three examine the cervix, the opening of the uterus, but they look for different things.

| Test | What it looks for | When you know |
|---|---|---|
| VIA | Patches that turn white when dilute acetic acid (vinegar) is put on the cervix | In the same visit |
| Pap smear | Changed cells, in a sample brushed from the cervix and read under a microscope | When the lab report comes |
| HPV test | The high-risk virus itself, in a swab | When the lab report comes |

VIA needs no laboratory, so the result can be read in the same visit. The HPV test looks for the cause, not the damage. For it, WHO says a sample a woman collects herself is as reliable as one collected by a health worker [[who-cervical]], so ask about self-collection.

None of these is a "virginity test", a pregnancy test or surgery. And none is perfect, which is why screening is repeated.

## What happens during the test

Book a day when you are not on your period. You do not need to fast, shave or bring anyone's permission.

1. The health worker asks about your age, your last period, pregnancies and any unusual bleeding. Say it is your first test.
2. You lie on your back on the examination table with your knees bent, covered by a sheet.
3. A speculum, a smooth plastic or metal instrument, is gently placed in the vagina so that the cervix can be seen. Expect pressure and some discomfort, not sharp pain. If it hurts, say so and ask for a pause or a smaller speculum.
4. For a Pap or HPV test, a soft brush is turned against the cervix for a few seconds. For VIA, the cervix is dabbed with dilute acetic acid, which can sting mildly, and then looked at.
5. The speculum is removed. It is over in a few minutes.

A little spotting afterwards can happen. Heavy bleeding or strong pain should not; go back if either does.

You can ask for a woman to do the test, bring a companion, and stop at any point. Nothing may be done without your consent, as our guide for unmarried women at the gynaecologist explains.

## Where to go

- **Government:** start with the nearest primary health centre or Ayushman Arogya Mandir. Ask the nurse, ANM or ASHA whether cervical screening is done there, and if not, where. District hospitals and medical colleges have a gynaecology OPD.
- **Private:** gynaecologists and labs offer Pap and HPV tests for a fee. Ask the price, and which test it is, before you book.
- **If you are living with HIV:** ask your ART centre for a referral.

In NFHS-5, even the state with the highest coverage, Tamil Nadu, was at 7%; the national figure for women aged 15-49 was 1.2% [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. If the first centre says "not here", ask where, and go.

Before you leave, ask which test this was, how and when you will get the result, and when the next one is due.

## An abnormal result is not a cancer diagnosis

Screening is built to catch problems early. A positive HPV test means the virus is present. It does not mean cancer, and in most cases the immune system clears the virus by itself [[who-cervical]]. A positive VIA or an abnormal Pap means some cells look changed and need a closer look.

That closer look is an examination of the cervix with the naked eye or with a magnifier called a colposcope. If a precancer is found, WHO describes the treatment as simple and effective: a heated probe (thermal ablation) or a cold probe (cryotherapy) destroys the abnormal cells, or a thin wire loop removes them (LEEP). Sometimes this is done in the same visit as the screening [[who-cervical]].

Time is usually on your side: abnormal cells typically take 15 to 20 years to become cancer [[who-cervical]]. The dangerous response to an abnormal result is not panic. It is disappearing. Go to the follow-up visit. Even if cancer is found, it can be cured when it is diagnosed and treated early [[who-cervical]].

So the teacher in Nagpur has her answers. The test is uncomfortable but brief. Her marital status does not decide whether she gets the test. And if they find something, they have most likely found it in time.
first-cervical-screening-test-guide.hg:
Cervical cancer un gine-chune cancers mein se hai jinhe shuru hone se pehle hi roka ja sakta hai: ek chhota sa test iske warning signs saalon pehle pakad leta hai. Phir bhi 2019-21 mein 35-49 saal ki sirf 2% Indian women ne kaha ki unki kabhi screening hui hai [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. GLOBOCAN ka latest estimate India ke liye 2024 mein 79,360 naye cases aur 36,319 deaths ka hai [[iarc-globocan-india-factsheet-2024]].

Socho, Nagpur ki ek 36 saal ki schoolteacher hai, jiski colleague ko abhi-abhi diagnosis mila hai. Woh test karwana chahti hai, par teen baatein kisi se poochne mein use sharam aati hai: dard hoga kya, kya woh poochenge ki meri shaadi hui hai ya nahi, aur agar kuch nikal aaya toh. Jawab yeh rahe.

## Screening kise karwani chahiye, aur kab

Screening un adults ke liye hai jo khud ko bilkul theek mehsoos karte hain. WHO ki advice hai ki 30 saal ki umar se shuru karo aur har 5 se 10 saal mein test dohrao. HIV ke saath jee rahi women ko 25 se shuru karna chahiye aur har 3 se 5 saal mein dohrana chahiye [[who-cervical]], kyunki WHO ke mutabik unka risk bina HIV wali women se chhe guna hai [[who-cervical-cancer-factsheet-2026]]. Global target hai ki 70% women ki screening 35 ki umar tak aur phir 45 tak ho jaaye [[who-cervical-elimination-launch-2020]].

Teen cheezein is advice ko nahi badalti:

- **HPV vaccine.** Vaccine lagi ho, tab bhi screening zaroori hai [[who-cervical]].
- **Shaadi.** Test tumhare cervix ke baare mein hai, tumhare marital status ke baare mein nahi. Is cancer ke peeche wala virus HPV sexual contact se failta hai, aur sex karne wale lagbhag sabhi logon ko yeh kabhi na kabhi hota hai [[who-cervical]]. Agar tumhara kabhi koi sexual contact nahi hua, toh risk kaafi kam hai; doctor se poocho ki kab shuru karna hai.
- **Theek mehsoos karna.** Precancer mein aksar koi symptom nahi hota [[who-cervical]].

Symptoms ki baat alag hai. Periods ke beech, sex ke baad ya menopause ke baad bleeding ho, ya ajeeb discharge ho, toh kisi bhi umar mein doctor ko dikhao.

## VIA, Pap aur HPV test: kaun sa kya check karta hai

Teeno cervix ko check karte hain, yaani uterus ke muh ko, par har ek alag cheez dhoondhta hai.

| Test | Kya dhoondhta hai | Result kab pata chalta hai |
|---|---|---|
| VIA | Woh patches jo cervix par dilute acetic acid (sirka) lagane se safed ho jaate hain | Usi visit mein |
| Pap smear | Badle hue cells, cervix se brush karke liye gaye sample mein, microscope ke neeche | Jab lab report aaye |
| HPV test | Khud high-risk virus, ek swab mein | Jab lab report aaye |

VIA ke liye laboratory nahi chahiye, isliye result usi visit mein padh liya jaata hai. HPV test nuksaan nahi, uski wajah dhoondhta hai. Iske liye WHO kehta hai ki jo sample woman khud leti hai, woh health worker ke liye gaye sample jitna hi reliable hai [[who-cervical]], toh self-collection ke baare mein poocho.

Inmein se koi bhi "virginity test", pregnancy test ya surgery nahi hai. Aur koi bhi perfect nahi hai, isiliye screening dohrayi jaati hai.

## Test ke dauraan kya hota hai

Aisa din chuno jab periods na chal rahe hon. Na bhookha rehna hai, na shave karna hai, na kisi ki permission laani hai.

1. Health worker tumhari umar, last period, pregnancies aur kisi ajeeb bleeding ke baare mein poochta hai. Bata do ki yeh tumhara pehla test hai.
2. Tum examination table par peeth ke bal letti ho, ghutne mude hue, upar ek chaadar.
3. Speculum, yaani plastic ya metal ka ek chikna instrument, dheere se vagina mein rakha jaata hai taaki cervix dikh sake. Pressure aur thodi discomfort hogi, tez dard nahi. Dard ho toh bol do, aur thoda rukne ya chhota speculum lene ko kaho.
4. Pap ya HPV test mein ek soft brush kuch seconds ke liye cervix par ghumaya jaata hai. VIA mein cervix par dilute acetic acid lagaya jaata hai, jisse halki si jalan ho sakti hai, aur phir use dekha jaata hai.
5. Speculum nikaal liya jaata hai. Kuch minute mein sab khatam.

Baad mein halki spotting ho sakti hai. Zyada bleeding ya tez dard nahi hona chahiye; aisa ho toh wapas jao.

Tum keh sakti ho ki test koi woman kare, kisi ko saath la sakti ho, aur kisi bhi point par rukwa sakti ho. Tumhari consent ke bina kuch nahi kiya ja sakta, jaisa unmarried women aur gynaecologist wali humari guide mein samjhaya gaya hai.

## Kahan jaayein

- **Government:** shuruaat sabse paas ke primary health centre ya Ayushman Arogya Mandir se karo. Nurse, ANM ya ASHA se poocho ki cervical screening wahan hoti hai ya nahi, aur nahi toh kahan hoti hai. District hospitals aur medical colleges mein gynaecology OPD hoti hai.
- **Private:** gynaecologists aur labs fees lekar Pap aur HPV test karte hain. Book karne se pehle price poocho, aur yeh bhi ki kaun sa test hai.
- **Agar tum HIV ke saath jee rahi ho:** apne ART centre se referral maango.

NFHS-5 mein sabse zyada coverage wala state Tamil Nadu bhi 7% par tha; 15-49 saal ki women ka national figure 1.2% tha [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Agar pehla centre kahe "yahan nahi hota", toh poocho kahan hota hai, aur wahan jao.

Nikalne se pehle poocho ki yeh kaun sa test tha, result kaise aur kab milega, aur agla test kab due hai.

## Abnormal result cancer ka diagnosis nahi hai

Screening bani hi isliye hai ki problem jaldi pakdi jaaye. HPV test positive aane ka matlab hai ki virus maujood hai. Iska matlab cancer nahi hai, aur zyadatar cases mein immune system virus ko khud clear kar deta hai [[who-cervical]]. VIA positive ya Pap abnormal aane ka matlab hai ki kuch cells badle hue dikh rahe hain aur unhe closer se dekhna hai.

Closer jaanch mein cervix ko seedhe aankhon se ya colposcope naam ke magnifier se dekha jaata hai. Agar precancer mile, toh WHO iske treatment ko simple aur effective batata hai: ek garam probe (thermal ablation) ya thanda probe (cryotherapy) abnormal cells ko khatam kar deta hai, ya ek patla wire loop unhe nikaal deta hai (LEEP). Kabhi-kabhi yeh screening wali visit mein hi ho jaata hai [[who-cervical]].

Time aksar tumhari side hota hai: abnormal cells ko cancer banne mein aam taur par 15 se 20 saal lagte hain [[who-cervical]]. Abnormal result ka khatarnaak response ghabrahat nahi hai. Khatarnaak hai gayab ho jaana. Follow-up visit par jao. Cancer nikle bhi, toh jaldi diagnosis aur treatment hone par woh theek ho sakta hai [[who-cervical]].

Toh Nagpur ki teacher ko uske jawab mil gaye. Test mein discomfort hoti hai, par woh jaldi khatam ho jaata hai. Use test milega ya nahi, yeh uske marital status se tay nahi hota. Aur agar kuch nikla, toh zyada chance yahi hai ki time rehte nikla.

free-confidential-hiv-test-guide.en:
Somewhere in India today, a person with HIV is living an ordinary week: working, studying, maybe planning a wedding. They feel fine, and they have no idea. India had an estimated 25.61 lakh people living with HIV in 2024 [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. In 2024-25, only 83.9% of people living with HIV knew their status, so roughly one in six did not [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. The fix is a blood test that is free at government centres, needs your consent and is confidential by law. This guide takes you from the counter to the result.

## Why 1 in 6 people with HIV are still undiagnosed

HIV can stay silent. In the first weeks after infection, some people get a flu-like illness and others feel nothing at all, and many do not find out they have HIV until the later stages [[who-hiv]]. Accurate knowledge is thin, too. In 2019-21, only 22% of women and 31% of men aged 15-49 had comprehensive knowledge of HIV [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Then there is the fear of being seen. The health system knows it well: national guidance says adolescent health centres should not be placed near HIV or STI testing centres, so that young people can walk in without hesitation [[nhm-afhc-page-2026]].

NACO's data show that people who decide to test on their own have good reason to. In 2024-25 the programme ran 4.13 crore HIV tests among at-risk people, and 0.40% were positive. People who walked in on their own made up only 14% of those tests but had the highest positivity among them, 1.1%, nearly three times the average [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Your own sense that something risky happened is one of the best reasons to test.

Not knowing has a cost. Untreated, HIV can progress to AIDS, often after many years. And someone who does not know their status cannot start the treatment that, once it makes the virus undetectable, also stops it passing to partners through sex [[who-hiv]].

## Where to get tested free, and what to say at the counter

HIV counselling and testing is free at government Integrated Counselling and Testing Centres (ICTCs) [[naco]]. At a district hospital or medical college, ask at the registration desk for the HIV testing centre. If you would rather ask first, call 1097. NACO's toll-free helpline works round the clock in 16 languages and took 4,32,474 calls in 2024-25 [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. It can point you to the nearest centre [[naco]].

At the counter, "I want an HIV test" is enough. You do not need a reason or a referral. A counsellor will explain the test and ask about possible exposures. Answer honestly: your answers decide when you should test, whether you will need a repeat test and whether you need PEP. Rapid tests can give a result the same day [[who-hiv]].

If you are under 18, ask the counsellor how consent works at your age. Doctors also cannot promise complete secrecy about sexual activity or abuse: under POCSO, anyone who knows of a sexual offence against a child must report it to the police [[indiacode-pocso-act-2012]]. Go anyway. Your health comes first, and if someone is hurting you, the Child Helpline 1098 can help.

## Window periods: when a negative really means negative

Every HIV test has a window period: the gap between infection and the point when the test can detect it. Many tests look for antibodies, which most people develop within a few weeks of infection. Inside that window, a test can be negative even though the virus is present, and the virus can still be passed on [[who-hiv]].

Imagine a 22-year-old in Jaipur whose condom broke ten days ago. A test today may come back negative and still be too early to count for that night. The counsellor will tell him when to come back, based on the test the centre uses. Until then: condoms every time, and no shared needles.

If the exposure was in the last 72 hours, do not wait for a test result. PEP, a 28-day course of medicine, must start as soon as possible and no later than 72 hours after exposure [[who-pep]]. Our explainer on PEP covers how to ask for it.

## Your rights: consent, confidentiality, no forced disclosure

The HIV and AIDS (Prevention and Control) Act, 2017 came into force on 10 September 2018 [[mohfw-hiv-act-commencement-2018]]. Here is what it promises you. This is general information, not legal advice.

- **No test without your informed consent** (Section 5). Someone must explain the test before you agree [[naco-hiv-aids-act-2017-gazette]].
- **No forced disclosure.** No one can be compelled to disclose their HIV status except by court order (Section 8).
- **Hidden identity in court.** In HIV-related cases, courts can replace a person's name with a pseudonym (Section 34).
- **No test as a condition.** An employer, school or hospital cannot make an HIV test a condition for a job, education or healthcare (Section 3) [[naco-hiv-aids-act-2017-gazette]].

If these rights are broken, you can complain: every state must appoint an HIV Ombudsman [[naco-hiv-aids-act-2017-gazette]]. By March 2025, 34 States/UTs had one [[naco-sankalak-2025]].

## If the result is positive: free treatment and next steps

A single positive rapid test is not a diagnosis. It has to be confirmed with further tests [[who-hiv]]. If it is confirmed, you will be referred to an ART centre. In March 2025, 800 government ART centres were treating 17.54 lakh people free of charge, and an estimated 1.06 lakh more were on treatment in the private sector [[naco-sankalak-2025]].

Not everyone who is diagnosed gets onto treatment, or stays on it. In 2024-25, 86.6% of people who knew their status were on treatment [[naco-sankalak-2025]], which means more than one in eight were not. Daily antiretroviral therapy (ART) can bring the virus down to undetectable levels, and a person who stays undetectable does not pass HIV on through sex [[who-hiv]]. Our explainer on "undetectable = untransmittable" covers what that means.

With your consent, the centre can also offer tests to your partner and children. In 2024-25, 6.6 lakh spouses, partners and children of people with HIV were tested this way, and 4.1% were positive, about ten times the rate among all at-risk people tested [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Counsellors at the centre can help you plan how to tell a partner.

A positive result is a diagnosis, not a verdict. With treatment, people with HIV can lead long and healthy lives [[who-hiv]]. The hardest step is the first one: walking up to the counter.
free-confidential-hiv-test-guide.hg:
Aaj India mein kahin koi insaan HIV ke saath ek normal hafta jee raha hai: kaam par ja raha hai, padh raha hai, shayad shaadi plan kar raha hai. Woh bilkul theek feel karta hai, aur use koi idea nahi. 2024 mein India mein estimated 25.61 lakh log HIV ke saath jee rahe the [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. 2024-25 mein HIV ke saath jee rahe sirf 83.9% logon ko apna status pata tha, yaani lagbhag har chhe mein se ek ko nahi [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Iska solution ek blood test hai jo government centres par free hai, tumhari consent se hota hai aur law ke hisaab se confidential rehta hai. Yeh guide tumhe counter se result tak le jaati hai.

## HIV wale har 6 mein se 1 ka diagnosis ab tak kyun nahi hua

HIV chupchaap reh sakta hai. Infection ke pehle kuch hafton mein kuch logon ko flu jaisi illness hoti hai aur kuch ko bilkul kuch feel nahi hota, aur bahut log baad ki stages tak jaan hi nahi paate ki unhe HIV hai [[who-hiv]]. Sahi jaankari bhi kam hai. 2019-21 mein 15-49 saal ki sirf 22% women aur 31% men ko HIV ki comprehensive knowledge thi [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Phir dekhe jaane ka darr bhi hai. Health system khud yeh baat achhi tarah jaanta hai: national guidance kehti hai ki adolescent health centres HIV ya STI testing centres ke paas nahi hone chahiye, taaki young log bina jhijhak andar ja sakein [[nhm-afhc-page-2026]].

NACO ka data dikhata hai ki jo log khud test karwane ka decision lete hain, unke paas iski achhi wajah hoti hai. 2024-25 mein programme ne at-risk logon ke 4.13 crore HIV tests kiye, aur 0.40% positive nikle. Khud walk-in karne wale log in tests ka sirf 14% the, lekin unmein positivity sabse zyada thi: 1.1%, yaani average se lagbhag teen guna [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Agar tumhe lagta hai ki kuch risky hua hai, toh yeh test karwane ki sabse achhi wajahon mein se ek hai.

Na jaanne ki keemat hoti hai. Bina treatment ke HIV AIDS tak pahunch sakta hai, aksar kai saalon baad. Aur jise apna status pata hi nahi, woh treatment bhi shuru nahi kar sakta. Yahi treatment virus ko undetectable karke sex ke through partners tak HIV jaane se bhi rokta hai [[who-hiv]].

## Free test kahan karwayein, aur counter par kya bolein

Government Integrated Counselling and Testing Centres (ICTCs) mein HIV counselling aur testing free hoti hai [[naco]]. District hospital ya medical college mein registration counter par HIV testing centre ka poocho. Agar pehle phone par poochna ho, toh 1097 par call karo. NACO ki yeh toll-free helpline din-raat 16 languages mein chalti hai, aur 2024-25 mein ispar 4,32,474 calls aayi [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Yeh tumhe nearest centre bata sakti hai [[naco]].

Counter par bas "Mujhe HIV test karwana hai" bolna kaafi hai. Koi reason ya referral nahi chahiye. Ek counsellor test samjhayenge aur possible exposures ke baare mein poochenge. Sach batao: tumhare jawab se hi tay hota hai ki test kab karwana hai, dobara test chahiye ya nahi, aur PEP ki zaroorat hai ya nahi. Rapid test se usi din result mil sakta hai [[who-hiv]].

Agar tum 18 se kam ho, toh counsellor se poocho ki tumhari umar mein consent kaise kaam karti hai. Doctors sexual activity ya abuse ke baare mein complete secrecy ka promise bhi nahi kar sakte: POCSO ke under, jise bhi kisi bachche ke khilaaf sexual offence ka pata ho, use police ko report karna hota hai [[indiacode-pocso-act-2012]]. Phir bhi zaroor jao. Tumhari health sabse pehle hai, aur agar koi tumhe hurt kar raha hai, toh Child Helpline 1098 madad kar sakti hai.

## Window period: negative result par kab bharosa karein

Har HIV test ka ek window period hota hai: infection hone aur test mein pakde jaane ke beech ka time. Kai tests antibodies dhoondhte hain, jo zyada tar logon mein infection ke kuch hafton ke andar ban jaati hain. Is window ke andar virus hone par bhi test negative aa sakta hai, aur tab bhi virus aage pass ho sakta hai [[who-hiv]].

Ek hypothetical socho: Jaipur ke ek 22 saal ke ladke ka condom das din pehle phata tha. Aaj uska test negative aa sakta hai, phir bhi us raat ke liye yeh result abhi bahut jaldi ka hai. Counsellor batayenge ki centre ke test ke hisaab se use dobara kab aana hai. Tab tak: har baar condom, aur needles kabhi share nahi.

Agar exposure pichhle 72 ghanton mein hua hai, toh test result ka wait mat karo. PEP, yaani 28 din ka medicine course, jitna jaldi ho sake aur exposure ke 72 ghante ke andar start hona chahiye [[who-pep]]. Hamara PEP explainer batata hai ki ise kaise maangna hai.

## Tumhare rights: consent, confidentiality, forced disclosure nahi

HIV and AIDS (Prevention and Control) Act, 2017, 10 September 2018 se lagu hai [[mohfw-hiv-act-commencement-2018]]. Yeh law tumse yeh promises karta hai. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

- **Tumhari informed consent ke bina test nahi** (Section 5). Haan kehne se pehle koi tumhe test samjhaye [[naco-hiv-aids-act-2017-gazette]].
- **Forced disclosure nahi.** Court order ke bina kisi ko apna HIV status batane ke liye force nahi kiya ja sakta (Section 8).
- **Court mein pehchaan chhupi rahe.** HIV se jude cases mein court insaan ke asli naam ki jagah pseudonym use kar sakta hai (Section 34).
- **Test koi condition nahi.** Employer, school ya hospital job, education ya healthcare ke liye HIV test ki condition nahi rakh sakte (Section 3) [[naco-hiv-aids-act-2017-gazette]].

Agar yeh rights tode jaayein, toh tum complaint kar sakte ho: har state ko ek HIV Ombudsman appoint karna zaroori hai [[naco-hiv-aids-act-2017-gazette]]. March 2025 tak 34 States/UTs mein Ombudsman tha [[naco-sankalak-2025]].

## Result positive aaye toh: free treatment aur next steps

Ek akela positive rapid test diagnosis nahi hai. Ise aur tests se confirm karna padta hai [[who-hiv]]. Confirm hone par tumhe ART centre refer kiya jayega. March 2025 mein 800 government ART centres par 17.54 lakh logon ka free treatment chal raha tha, aur estimated 1.06 lakh aur log private sector mein treatment par the [[naco-sankalak-2025]].

Diagnosis ke baad har koi treatment tak nahi pahunchta, ya treatment par tika nahi rehta. 2024-25 mein jinhe apna status pata tha, unme se 86.6% treatment par the [[naco-sankalak-2025]], yaani har aath mein se ek se zyada log treatment par nahi the. Roz ki antiretroviral therapy (ART) virus ko undetectable level tak la sakti hai, aur jo undetectable bana rehta hai woh sex ke through HIV pass nahi karta [[who-hiv]]. "Undetectable = untransmittable" par hamara explainer ise detail mein samjhata hai.

Tumhari consent se centre tumhare partner aur bachchon ko bhi test offer kar sakta hai. 2024-25 mein HIV wale logon ke 6.6 lakh spouses, partners aur bachchon ka is tarah test hua, aur 4.1% positive nikle, jo sabhi at-risk logon ke rate se lagbhag das guna hai [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Partner ko kaise batana hai, iski planning mein centre ke counsellors help kar sakte hain.

Positive result ek diagnosis hai, verdict nahi. Treatment ke saath HIV wale log lambi aur healthy life jee sakte hain [[who-hiv]]. Sabse mushkil step pehla hai: counter tak chal kar jaana.

globocan-cervical-cancer-estimate-change.en:
On 28 February 2026, the day India launched its national HPV vaccination campaign, the government's release measured the disease it was fighting: "over 1 lakh 20 thousand new cases and nearly 80 thousand deaths" from cervical cancer [[pib-hpv-campaign-launch-2026]]. Those figures came from GLOBOCAN 2022, the global cancer database run by IARC, the World Health Organization's cancer research agency. Open the same agency's India fact sheet today and it says 79,360 new cases and 36,319 deaths [[iarc-globocan-india-factsheet-2024]].

On paper, the death toll has more than halved. No vaccine, screening drive or new treatment did that. The estimate was rebuilt, and the size of the correction says something uncomfortable about how India counts its dead.

## Two editions, two very different numbers

GLOBOCAN 2022 estimated 1,27,526 new cervical cancer cases and 79,906 deaths in India in 2022, making it the second most common cancer among Indian women, at 17.7% of their cancers [[iarc-globocan-india-factsheet-2022]]. The edition now online, GLOBOCAN 2024, estimates 79,360 new cases and 36,319 deaths. Cervical cancer is still second, but at 10.2% [[iarc-globocan-india-factsheet-2024]].

| Estimate | GLOBOCAN 2022 | GLOBOCAN 2024 |
|---|---|---|
| New cases, India | 1,27,526 | 79,360 |
| Deaths, India | 79,906 | 36,319 |
| Share of Indian women's cancers | 17.7% | 10.2% |
| New cases, world | 6,62,301 | 6,04,196 |
| Deaths, world | 3,48,874 | 2,79,583 |
| India's share of world deaths | about 23% | about 13% |

India's place in the world moves too: from about 19% of the world's new cases and about 23% of its deaths in the 2022 edition [[iarc-globocan-cervix-factsheet-2022]] to about 13% of both in the 2024 edition [[iarc-globocan-cervix-factsheet-2024]]. Set the editions side by side and most of the drop in the world total, for cases and for deaths, is the change in India's line alone.

## Why this is not a real fall

Cervical cancer develops slowly, over years, after a persistent infection with a high-risk type of HPV [[who-cervical]]. A death toll like this cannot halve in two years unless something enormous happens to screening or treatment, and there is no sign that it did. In 2019-21, only 1.2% of Indian women aged 15-49 had ever been screened for cervical cancer [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. The free vaccination campaign began only on 28 February 2026, after the year the new estimate describes, and it vaccinates 14-year-olds, so its effect on cancer figures lies decades ahead [[pib-hpv-campaign-launch-2026]].

What changed is the arithmetic. The 2024 edition uses different registry inputs and methods from the 2022 one [[iarc-globocan-india-factsheet-2024]]. The numbers carry a clue: between editions, estimated cases drop by more than a third, but estimated deaths drop by more than half. In the 2022 edition, deaths were well over half the number of new cases; in the 2024 edition they are under half. That points to a change in the model's assumption about how many patients die, not only in its inputs.

Breast cancer shows the same thing in reverse. The 2022 edition estimated 1,92,020 new cases and 98,337 deaths in India [[iarc-globocan-india-factsheet-2022]]; the 2024 edition says 2,37,231 new cases and 96,100 deaths [[iarc-globocan-india-factsheet-2024]]. Nobody should headline that as a two-year surge either.

## A country that does not count its cancer deaths

GLOBOCAN is not a count. It is a model built on whatever data each country can supply.
