For India, the 2022 edition drew cancer cases from 20 sub-national registries, and against national mortality data it recorded "No data" [[iarc-globocan-india-factsheet-2022]]. Rates from the areas that registries cover are applied to the whole population. Deaths are then calculated from those estimated cases, using a modelled ratio of deaths to cases [[iarc-globocan-india-factsheet-2024]].

Imagine a 50-year-old woman in a village far from any cancer registry. She has been unwell for months, is taken once to a district hospital, and dies at home. Her family may register the death, but if no doctor certifies the cause, the words "cervical cancer" never reach a database. She enters the national statistics only as a fraction in a formula.

That is how tens of thousands of women can appear or vanish on paper when a model is revised.

> The gap between the two estimates of India's cervical cancer deaths is bigger than the newer estimate itself.

## How to read a modelled estimate

**Check the edition.** A GLOBOCAN figure without its edition year is unusable. The government's February release quoted the edition that was current then; the older figure was not a lie, only the best estimate available. Anyone repeating "nearly 80 thousand deaths" today is quoting a superseded number.

**Ask whether it was counted or modelled.** Registered cases and surveyed households are counts. India's cancer deaths are modelled.

**Never subtract across editions.** Compare within one edition: India against the world, or cervix against breast. The honest sentence is "the latest estimate is 36,319 deaths", not "deaths fell to 36,319".

**Distrust headlines that credit a policy.** Consider a reporter who remembers the launch-day figure, finds the new one and files "Cervical cancer deaths halve after vaccine drive". The fall is not real, and the drive began after the year being estimated. By evening it would be a WhatsApp forward telling parents the job is done.

## What stays true either way

Even on the lower estimate, an estimated 36,319 Indian women died of cervical cancer in one year, from a disease that vaccination and screening can largely prevent [[who-cervical]]. Worldwide, WHO puts the toll at around 6,04,000 new cases and around 2,80,000 deaths in 2024, and says women living with HIV are six times more likely to develop it [[who-cervical-cancer-factsheet-2026]].

The case for prevention has not moved. HPV types 16 and 18 account for more than 80% of cervical cancer cases in India [[pib-hpv-backgrounder-2026]], and more than 80 lakh vaccine doses had been given under the national campaign by 11 September 2026 [[pib-hpv-80-lakh-doses-2026]]. Screening is where India fails adult women: 1.2% ever screened [[nfhs5-india-2021]], against a WHO target of 70% of women screened by 35 and again by 45 [[who-cervical-elimination-launch-2020]].

A programme for about 1.2 crore girls a year [[pib-hpv-campaign-launch-2026]] will one day have to show that it saved lives. It cannot do that against a baseline that swings by half when a model changes. The smaller number is not good news. It is a measure of how much India still does not know about how its women die.
globocan-cervical-cancer-estimate-change.hg:
28 February 2026 ko, jis din India ne apna national HPV vaccination campaign launch kiya, government ke release ne us bimari ko numbers mein naapa jisse woh lad rahi thi: cervical cancer ke "over 1 lakh 20 thousand new cases and nearly 80 thousand deaths" [[pib-hpv-campaign-launch-2026]]. Yeh figures GLOBOCAN 2022 se aaye the. GLOBOCAN ek global cancer database hai jise IARC chalati hai, yaani World Health Organization ki cancer research agency. Aaj usi agency ki India fact sheet kholo toh usmein likha hai 79,360 new cases aur 36,319 deaths [[iarc-globocan-india-factsheet-2024]].

Kaagaz par deaths aadhi se bhi kam ho gayi hain. Yeh kisi vaccine, screening drive ya naye treatment ne nahi kiya. Estimate dobara banaya gaya, aur correction kitna bada hai, yeh ek uncomfortable baat batata hai ki India apne marne walon ko kaise ginta hai.

## Do editions, do bahut alag numbers

GLOBOCAN 2022 ka estimate tha ki 2022 mein India mein cervical cancer ke 1,27,526 new cases aur 79,906 deaths hui. Is hisaab se yeh Indian women mein doosra sabse common cancer tha, unke cancers ka 17.7% [[iarc-globocan-india-factsheet-2022]]. Jo edition ab online hai, GLOBOCAN 2024, woh 79,360 new cases aur 36,319 deaths ka estimate deta hai. Cervical cancer ab bhi doosre number par hai, lekin 10.2% par [[iarc-globocan-india-factsheet-2024]].

| Estimate | GLOBOCAN 2022 | GLOBOCAN 2024 |
|---|---|---|
| New cases, India | 1,27,526 | 79,360 |
| Deaths, India | 79,906 | 36,319 |
| Indian women ke cancers mein hissa | 17.7% | 10.2% |
| New cases, duniya | 6,62,301 | 6,04,196 |
| Deaths, duniya | 3,48,874 | 2,79,583 |
| Duniya ki deaths mein India ka hissa | lagbhag 23% | lagbhag 13% |

Duniya mein India ki jagah bhi badal jaati hai: 2022 edition mein duniya ke new cases ka lagbhag 19% aur deaths ka lagbhag 23% [[iarc-globocan-cervix-factsheet-2022]], aur 2024 edition mein dono ka lagbhag 13% [[iarc-globocan-cervix-factsheet-2024]]. Dono editions ko saath rakho toh duniya ke total mein jo giravat dikhti hai, cases mein bhi aur deaths mein bhi, uska zyadatar hissa sirf India ki line ka badlav hai.

## Yeh asli giravat kyun nahi hai

Cervical cancer dheere-dheere banta hai, saalon mein, jab high-risk type ke HPV ka infection body mein tika rehta hai [[who-cervical]]. Aisa death toll do saal mein aadha tabhi ho sakta hai jab screening ya treatment mein kuch bahut bada badle, aur aisa hone ka koi sign nahi hai. 2019-21 mein 15-49 saal ki sirf 1.2% Indian women ne kabhi cervical cancer screening karwayi thi [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Free vaccination campaign toh 28 February 2026 ko hi shuru hua, yaani us saal ke baad jiska naya estimate hai. Usmein 14 saal ki ladkiyon ko vaccine lagti hai, isliye cancer figures par uska asar dashakon baad dikhega [[pib-hpv-campaign-launch-2026]].

Jo badla hai, woh hisaab hai. 2024 edition ke registry inputs aur methods 2022 wale se alag hain [[iarc-globocan-india-factsheet-2024]]. Numbers khud ek clue dete hain: dono editions ke beech estimated cases ek-tihai se zyada girte hain, lekin estimated deaths aadhi se zyada. 2022 edition mein deaths new cases ke aadhe se kaafi zyada thi; 2024 edition mein woh aadhe se kam hain. Yeh is taraf ishaara karta hai ki sirf inputs nahi badle, model ka yeh assumption bhi badla ki kitne patients ki death hoti hai.

Breast cancer yahi cheez ulti disha mein dikhata hai. 2022 edition ne India mein 1,92,020 new cases aur 98,337 deaths ka estimate diya tha [[iarc-globocan-india-factsheet-2022]]; 2024 edition 2,37,231 new cases aur 96,100 deaths kehta hai [[iarc-globocan-india-factsheet-2024]]. Ise bhi kisi ko "do saal mein surge" wali headline nahi banana chahiye.

## Ek desh jo apni cancer deaths ginta hi nahi

GLOBOCAN ginti nahi hai. Yeh ek model hai, jo us data par banta hai jo har country de paati hai. India ke liye 2022 edition ne cancer cases 20 sub-national registries se liye, aur national mortality data ke saamne likha "No data" [[iarc-globocan-india-factsheet-2022]]. Jin ilaakon ko registries cover karti hain, wahan ke rates poori population par laga diye jaate hain. Phir deaths unhi estimated cases se nikali jaati hain, deaths aur cases ke ek modelled ratio se [[iarc-globocan-india-factsheet-2024]].

Imagine karo ek 50 saal ki woman, kisi aise gaon mein jo har cancer registry se door hai. Woh mahinon se beemar hai, ek baar district hospital le jaayi jaati hai, aur ghar par uski death ho jaati hai. Parivaar shayad death register karwa de, lekin agar koi doctor cause certify nahi karta, toh "cervical cancer" shabd kisi database tak kabhi nahi pahunchte. National statistics mein woh sirf ek formula ke fraction ki tarah aati hai.

Isi tarah ek model revise hone par dasiyon hazaar women kaagaz par aa sakti hain ya gayab ho sakti hain.

> India ki cervical cancer deaths ke dono estimates ke beech ka gap naye estimate se bhi bada hai.

## Modelled estimate ko kaise padhein

**Edition check karo.** Edition ke saal ke bina GLOBOCAN ka koi figure kaam ka nahi. Government ke February release ne wahi edition quote kiya tha jo us waqt current tha; purana figure jhooth nahi tha, bas us waqt ka best available estimate tha. Jo aaj bhi "nearly 80 thousand deaths" dohra raha hai, woh ek purana, replace ho chuka number quote kar raha hai.

**Poocho ki yeh gina gaya tha ya model se nikla.** Registered cases aur survey kiye gaye households ginti hain. India ki cancer deaths modelled hain.

**Editions ke aar-paar kabhi minus mat karo.** Ek hi edition ke andar compare karo: India banaam duniya, ya cervix banaam breast. Imaandaar sentence yeh hai: "latest estimate 36,319 deaths ka hai". Yeh nahi: "deaths girkar 36,319 ho gayi".

**Jo headline kisi policy ko credit de, us par shak karo.** Socho ek reporter ko launch wale din ka figure yaad hai, use naya figure milta hai aur woh file kar deta hai: "Vaccine drive ke baad cervical cancer deaths aadhi". Giravat asli nahi hai, aur drive us saal ke baad shuru hui jiska estimate hai. Shaam tak yeh ek WhatsApp forward ban chuka hoga jo parents ko bata raha hoga ki kaam ho gaya.

## Jo dono surat mein sach rehta hai

Kam wale estimate par bhi ek saal mein andaazan 36,319 Indian women cervical cancer se mari, ek aisi bimari se jise vaccination aur screening kaafi had tak rok sakte hain [[who-cervical]]. Duniya bhar mein WHO ke mutabik 2024 mein lagbhag 6,04,000 new cases aur lagbhag 2,80,000 deaths hui, aur HIV ke saath jee rahi women mein yeh cancer hone ki sambhavna chheh guna zyada hai [[who-cervical-cancer-factsheet-2026]].

Prevention ka case wahin ka wahin hai. India mein cervical cancer ke 80% se zyada cases HPV type 16 aur 18 se hote hain [[pib-hpv-backgrounder-2026]], aur 11 September 2026 tak national campaign mein 80 lakh se zyada vaccine doses lag chuki thi [[pib-hpv-80-lakh-doses-2026]]. India adult women ko screening mein fail karta hai: sirf 1.2% ne kabhi screening karwayi [[nfhs5-india-2021]], jabki WHO ka target hai ki 70% women ki screening 35 ki umar tak aur phir 45 tak ho [[who-cervical-elimination-launch-2020]].

Har saal lagbhag 1.2 crore ladkiyon ke programme [[pib-hpv-campaign-launch-2026]] ko ek din dikhana hoga ki usne jaanein bachayi. Yeh us baseline ke saamne nahi dikhaya ja sakta jo ek model badalne par aadha idhar-udhar ho jaata hai. Chhota number good news nahi hai. Yeh is baat ka naap hai ki India ab bhi kitna kam jaanta hai ki uski women kaise marti hain.

gonorrhoea-drug-resistance-self-medicati.en:
Consider this situation. A 24-year-old in Kanpur notices a discharge and a burning feeling when he urinates. A doctor feels impossible: the waiting room, the questions, the neighbour who might see him there. So he walks to a chemist two lanes away, lowers his voice, and leaves with a strip of antibiotics. In three days the burning stops. The rest of the strip goes into a drawer.

He believes he is cured. He may only have silenced the infection. And if it was gonorrhoea, he has helped a germ that, according to the World Health Organization (WHO), is steadily leaving doctors with fewer medicines that can kill it.

## The warning from WHO

Gonorrhoea is a bacterial infection. It is on WHO's short list of curable sexually transmitted infections (STIs), along with syphilis, chlamydia and trichomoniasis [[who-sti]]. "Curable" comes with a condition: the right antibiotic, in the right dose.

That condition is getting harder to meet. WHO says antimicrobial resistance in STIs, gonorrhoea in particular, has increased in recent years and has reduced treatment options, and that its global surveillance programme has found high rates of resistance to many antibiotics [[who-sti]]. It calls drug resistance a major threat to reducing the burden of STIs worldwide [[who-sti]].

There is no vaccine to fall back on: WHO lists vaccine candidates against gonorrhoea as still in early clinical development [[who-sti]].

## How a half-course breeds resistance

The bacteria in one infection are not identical. A few are, by chance, slightly harder to kill. The right drug at the right dose kills all of them. The wrong drug, too small a dose, or a course dropped on day three kills the easy bacteria first and leaves the tougher ones to multiply. Those are the ones the next partner receives.

One strip in one drawer changes little. Repeat it across a country, year after year, and the tough strain becomes the ordinary one.

Two more traps sit inside that strip. The first is that symptoms are a poor guide. WHO notes that STIs are often asymptomatic [[who-sti]], and a symptom that stops is not proof that the infection has gone.

The second is that "discharge" has many causes, and several are not STIs at all; they need different medicines, or none. A strip bought on a guess may treat nothing, and it still exposes the body's bacteria to the drug.

## India's blind spot: STIs treated outside the system

India's AIDS programme managed about 1.12 crore (111.8 lakh) STI/RTI cases in 2024-25, including 71.95 lakh visits at its Suraksha Clinics [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. The National AIDS Control Organisation (NACO) runs 1,127 of these clinics, at district hospitals and medical colleges [[naco-sankalak-2025]].

Most of these cases are managed by symptoms, without a laboratory naming the germ. WHO calls the method simple and fast where tests are expensive or unavailable. It also states the price: substantial overtreatment, while infections without symptoms are not covered at all. It recommends that countries add laboratory testing step by step [[who-sti]].

Then there is what the figure leaves out. It counts episodes, not people, and only those inside the government programme. Infections treated by private doctors, chemists and unqualified practitioners are not counted. The programme's data cannot say how many people treat a suspected STI with a strip bought without a test, which drug they were given, or whether it worked.

> India counts the STI cases its clinics treat. It does not count the strips sold across the counter.

Resistance grows best exactly where nobody is measuring: no test before treatment, no check after it, no partner informed.

## Why 'venereal disease' cure ads are illegal

Under the Drugs and Magic Remedies (Objectionable Advertisements) Act, 1954, advertising a drug that claims to treat conditions listed in the Act's Schedule is a crime, and the Schedule covers venereal diseases, including syphilis and gonorrhoea, as well as sexual impotence. A first conviction carries up to six months in jail, a fine, or both; a repeat conviction, up to one year [[sc-ima-order-mar-2025]]. This is general information, not legal advice.

A wall poster or reel promising a "guaranteed cure" sells treatment without diagnosis, the same shortcut as the counter strip.

Enforcement is another matter. On 26 March 2025 the Supreme Court said that although the Act was more than 70 years old, "there is no implementation of the 1954 Act in its true letter and spirit". It ordered states to appoint enforcement officers within one month and to set up public complaint mechanisms within two months [[sc-ima-order-mar-2025]].

## Test, finish the course, treat partners

Here is what the 24-year-old needed instead of the strip.

- Get examined, and tested where a test is available: at a Suraksha Clinic or with any qualified doctor. Say plainly what kind of sex you had; it helps the doctor decide what to check.
- Take exactly what is prescribed, all of it. WHO notes that the curable STIs are generally cured with single-dose regimens of the right antibiotic [[who-sti]], so proper treatment is often shorter than the chemist's strip.
- Get partners treated. WHO calls treating sexual partners an important part of STI care, to interrupt transmission and prevent re-infection [[who-sti]].
- Go back if symptoms continue. A treatment that fails is exactly what a doctor needs to hear about; it is how a resistant infection gets caught.
- Never keep, share or reuse leftover antibiotics.

Used correctly and every time, condoms are among the most effective ways to prevent STIs [[who-sti]]. For confidential questions, NACO's helpline 1097 offers counselling round the clock in 16 languages [[naco-sankalak-2025]].

Gonorrhoea is still curable. Whether it stays that way depends partly on what happens at the chemist's counter.
gonorrhoea-drug-resistance-self-medicati.hg:
Ek situation socho. Kanpur mein 24 saal ke ek ladke ko discharge dikhta hai aur peshaab karte waqt jalan hoti hai. Doctor ke paas jaana use namumkin lagta hai: waiting room, sawaal, aur wo padosi jo use wahan dekh sakta hai. Toh wo do gali door ke chemist ke paas jaata hai, awaaz dheemi karta hai, aur antibiotics ki ek strip le ke nikal aata hai. Teen din mein jalan band ho jaati hai. Baaki strip drawer mein chali jaati hai.

Use lagta hai wo theek ho gaya. Ho sakta hai usne infection ko sirf chup karaya ho. Aur agar wo gonorrhoea tha, toh usne ek aise germ ki madad ki hai jiske baare mein World Health Organization (WHO) kehta hai ki use maarne wali dawaein doctors ke paas lagataar kam hoti ja rahi hain.

## WHO ki warning

Gonorrhoea ek bacterial infection hai. Ye WHO ki us chhoti si list mein hai jisme theek ho sakne wale sexually transmitted infections (STIs) aate hain, syphilis, chlamydia aur trichomoniasis ke saath [[who-sti]]. Lekin "theek ho sakta hai" ke saath ek shart judi hai: sahi antibiotic, sahi dose mein.

Ye shart poori karna mushkil hota ja raha hai. WHO kehta hai ki STIs mein, khaas kar gonorrhoea mein, antimicrobial resistance haal ke saalon mein badha hai aur isne ilaaj ke options kam kar diye hain, aur uske global surveillance programme ne kai antibiotics ke against resistance ki oonchi rates paayi hain [[who-sti]]. WHO drug resistance ko duniya bhar mein STIs ka bojh kam karne ke raaste ka ek bada khatra maanta hai [[who-sti]].

Peeche koi vaccine bhi nahi khadi hai: WHO ke mutaabik gonorrhoea ke vaccine candidates abhi early clinical development mein hi hain [[who-sti]].

## Aadha course resistance kaise paida karta hai

Ek infection ke saare bacteria ek jaise nahi hote. Kuch, bas chance se, thode zyada mushkil se marte hain. Sahi dawa sahi dose mein un sabko maar deti hai. Galat dawa, kam dose, ya teesre din chhoda hua course pehle aasaan bacteria ko maarta hai aur zyada tough walon ko badhne ke liye chhod deta hai. Agle partner tak wahi pahunchte hain.

Ek drawer mein padi ek strip se zyada kuch nahi badalta. Lekin yahi cheez poore desh mein, saal dar saal dohrao, toh tough strain hi aam strain ban jaata hai.

Us strip ke andar do aur jaal hain. Pehla ye ki symptoms bharosemand guide nahi hain. WHO kehta hai ki STIs mein aksar koi symptom hota hi nahi [[who-sti]], aur symptom ka ruk jaana is baat ka saboot nahi ki infection chala gaya.

Doosra ye ki "discharge" ki kai wajah hoti hain, aur unmein se kai STI hain hi nahi; unki dawaein alag hoti hain, ya dawa ki zaroorat hi nahi hoti. Andaaze pe kharidi gayi strip ho sakta hai kisi cheez ka ilaaj na kare, phir bhi wo body ke bacteria ko us dawa ke saamne la deti hai.

## India ka blind spot: system ke bahar hone wala STI ka ilaaj

India ke AIDS programme ne 2024-25 mein lagbhag 1.12 crore (111.8 lakh) STI/RTI cases manage kiye, jinmein uske Suraksha Clinics ki 71.95 lakh visits shaamil hain [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. National AIDS Control Organisation (NACO) aise 1,127 clinics chalata hai, district hospitals aur medical colleges mein [[naco-sankalak-2025]].

Inmein se zyada tar cases symptoms dekh ke manage hote hain, bina is ke ki koi lab germ ka naam bataye. WHO is tareeke ko simple aur tez batata hai, un jagahon ke liye jahan tests mehenge hain ya milte nahi. Saath hi wo iski keemat bhi batata hai: kaafi zyada overtreatment, jabki bina symptoms wale infections isme cover hi nahi hote. WHO ki salaah hai ki countries dheere-dheere laboratory testing jodte jaayein [[who-sti]].

Phir aata hai wo hissa jo is figure mein hai hi nahi. Ye episodes ginta hai, log nahi, aur sirf unhe jo sarkaari programme ke andar aaye. Private doctors, chemists aur unqualified practitioners ke haathon jin infections ka ilaaj hota hai, wo gine hi nahi jaate. Programme ka data ye nahi bata sakta ki kitne log apne suspected STI ka ilaaj bina test ke kharidi strip se karte hain, unhe kaun si dawa di gayi, ya wo kaam aayi ya nahi.

> India un STI cases ko ginta hai jinka ilaaj uske clinics karte hain. Counter pe biki strips ko wo nahi ginta.

Resistance sabse achchhe se wahin badhta hai jahan koi naap hi nahi raha: ilaaj se pehle test nahi, ilaaj ke baad check nahi, partner ko khabar nahi.

## 'Venereal disease' ke ilaaj wale ads illegal kyun hain

Drugs and Magic Remedies (Objectionable Advertisements) Act, 1954 ke under kisi aisi dawa ko advertise karna crime hai jo Act ke Schedule mein listed conditions ke ilaaj ka daawa kare, aur us Schedule mein venereal diseases aati hain, jinmein syphilis aur gonorrhoea shaamil hain, aur sexual impotence bhi. Pehli conviction pe chhe mahine tak jail, fine, ya dono ho sakte hain; dobara conviction pe ek saal tak [[sc-ima-order-mar-2025]]. Ye general information hai, legal advice nahi.

Deewar ka poster ya reel jo "guaranteed ilaaj" ka waada karta hai, wo bina diagnosis ka ilaaj bechta hai, wahi shortcut jo counter wali strip hai.

Law laagu hona alag kahaani hai. 26 March 2025 ko Supreme Court ne kaha ki Act 70 saal se zyada purana hone ke bawajood "there is no implementation of the 1954 Act in its true letter and spirit", yaani wo sahi maayne mein laagu hi nahi hua. Court ne states ko order diya ki ek mahine ke andar enforcement officers appoint karein aur do mahine ke andar public ke liye complaint mechanism banayein [[sc-ima-order-mar-2025]].

## Test karao, course poora karo, partners ka ilaaj karao

Us 24 saal ke ladke ko strip ki jagah ye chahiye tha.

- Jaanch karao, aur jahan test available ho wahan test bhi: Suraksha Clinic mein ya kisi bhi qualified doctor ke paas. Saaf batao ki kis tarah ka sex hua tha; isse doctor ko tay karne mein madad milti hai ki kya check karna hai.
- Jo prescribe hua hai bilkul wahi lo, poora lo. WHO kehta hai ki theek ho sakne wale STIs aam taur pe sahi antibiotic ke single-dose regimen se theek ho jaate hain [[who-sti]], yaani sahi ilaaj aksar chemist ki strip se chhota hi hota hai.
- Partners ka ilaaj karao. WHO sexual partners ke ilaaj ko STI care ka ek zaroori hissa kehta hai, taaki transmission ruke aur re-infection na ho [[who-sti]].
- Symptoms rahein toh wapas jao. Ilaaj ka fail hona wahi cheez hai jo doctor ko pata chalni chahiye; resistant infection aise hi pakda jaata hai.
- Bachi hui antibiotics kabhi mat rakho, kisi ko mat do, aur dobara mat lo.

Sahi tareeke se aur har baar use kiye jaayein toh condoms STIs se bachaav ke sabse effective tareekon mein se hain [[who-sti]]. Confidential sawaalon ke liye NACO ki helpline 1097 pe 16 bhashaon mein 24 ghante counselling milti hai [[naco-sankalak-2025]].

Gonorrhoea ab bhi theek ho sakta hai. Aage bhi aisa rahega ya nahi, ye kuch had tak is pe depend karta hai ki chemist ke counter pe kya hota hai.

gupt-rog-clinics-magic-remedies-act.en:
Take a train into many Indian cities and look at the boundary walls along the tracks. The same promises are painted there in huge letters, with a phone number: "gupt rog" (secret disease), "shighrapatan" (premature ejaculation), "night fall", "napunsakta" (impotence), "nisantan" (childlessness), all cured, often in "ek mulaqat", a single visit. They now arrive as reels and sponsored posts too. Most of these ads are illegal under a law passed in 1954. Why are they still everywhere, and what do they cost the people who answer them?

## The walls, the reels and the promise

The business runs on shame. A teenager worried about wet dreams, a married man worried about his erections, a couple who have not conceived: each is told the problem is secret, serious and curable only by a "specialist" who asks no awkward questions. What the ads sell is a "course" of powders, oils or capsules. What they do not offer is a diagnosis.

Many of the "diseases" on the wall are not diseases. Night fall (wet dreams) is a normal body event. Masturbation does not weaken anyone. Other items are real conditions with real treatments, which makes the trade more dangerous: erection problems that keep happening can be a sign of diabetes, high blood pressure or high cholesterol [[nhs-ed]], and a genital sore or discharge can be a sexually transmitted infection (STI) that needs a test and proper treatment, not a powder [[who-sti]].

## What the 1954 law bans

Section 3 of the Drugs and Magic Remedies (Objectionable Advertisements) Act, 1954 says no person shall take part in publishing an advertisement suggesting a drug can be used for "the procurement of miscarriage in women or prevention of conception in women", "the maintenance or improvement of the capacity of human beings for sexual pleasure", "the correction of menstrual disorder in women", or the diagnosis, cure, mitigation, treatment or prevention of any disease or condition listed in the Act's Schedule [[sc-ima-order-mar-2025]]. The Schedule includes sexual impotence and venereal diseases, including syphilis and gonorrhoea [[sc-ima-order-mar-2025]]. Section 5 stretches the ban to "magic remedies" such as talismans, mantras and amulets sold for the same purposes [[sc-ima-order-mar-2025]].

That covers most lines on the wall, from "sex power" to "periods regular" pills. The penalty under Section 7 is up to six months in jail, a fine or both for a first conviction, and up to a year in jail, a fine or both for a repeat [[sc-ima-order-mar-2025]]. Section 9A makes the offence cognizable, so police must register an FIR on a complaint [[sc-ima-order-mar-2025]]. This is general information, not legal advice.

## The Supreme Court's 2025 finding

On 26 March 2025, hearing an Indian Medical Association petition about misleading health advertisements, a bench of Justices Abhay S. Oka and Ujjal Bhuyan wrote: "Though the 1954 Act is more than 70 years old, unfortunately, there is no implementation of the 1954 Act in its true letter and spirit" [[sc-ima-order-mar-2025]]. The amicus curiae told the court that many states only issued warnings instead of prosecuting [[sc-ima-order-mar-2025]].

The court ordered states to appoint enough gazetted officers to enforce the Act under Section 8(1) within one month, and to set up a grievance mechanism, through a toll-free number or email, within two months [[sc-ima-order-mar-2025]].

How did a cognizable offence, painted in giant letters, survive for decades? Part of the answer is in the court record: warnings instead of prosecutions. Part of it is likely shame. The people cheated by a "gupt rog" clinic are among the least likely to complain, because complaining means saying aloud what they went there for. Without complaints, and without officers whose job is to look, little happens. The court's order targets exactly those two gaps.

## The cost of a fake cure

Imagine a 19-year-old in Patna with a painless sore. Too embarrassed to see the family doctor, he calls the number on the wall and pays for weeks of powders. The sore heals on its own, as an early syphilis sore usually does, and he believes he is cured. The infection is still there, and untreated syphilis can last for years and, in its late stage, lead to brain and cardiovascular disease [[who-syphilis]].

Government data shows the risk is real. Of 46.2 lakh syphilis screenings at India's government STI clinics in 2024-25, 43,482 (0.94%) were reactive, rising to 1.54% among men and 4.12% among transgender clients [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. These are people who came to a clinic, not the general population. In the same year India identified 10,545 syphilis-infected pregnant women [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Syphilis in pregnancy can pass to the baby; diagnosing and treating the mother with penicillin is what prevents it [[who-syphilis]].

Many STIs have no symptoms at all; only a test tells. Bacterial STIs such as syphilis, gonorrhoea and chlamydia are curable [[who-sti]]. A powder sold without a test cannot tell which infection a man has, and does nothing for a partner who may also need treatment. The fake cure costs money, then health: his, his partner's, sometimes a child's.

## How to report an ad, and where to get real care

To report an ad:

- Photograph it with the place and date, or screenshot the post with the account name.
- Send it to your state's drug control or health department, using the toll-free number or email the Supreme Court ordered, if your state has set one up.
- Because the offence is cognizable, you can also give a written complaint at a police station.
- Report sponsored posts to the platform as misleading health claims.

For real care, NACO runs 1,127 Designated STI/RTI Clinics, branded Suraksha Clinics, at district hospitals and medical colleges; Uttar Pradesh has the most, 115 [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. They are already in heavy use: 71.95 lakh visits in 2024-25, 60.9% of them by women [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. For erection, ejaculation or fertility worries, see a doctor at a government hospital. For confidential HIV information and counselling, NACO's helpline 1097 works round the clock in 16 languages [[naco-sankalak-2025]].

The wall promises secrecy. A government clinic offers privacy, plus a diagnosis.
gupt-rog-clinics-magic-remedies-act.hg:
Kai Indian shehron mein train se aate hue patriyon ke saath wali boundary walls dekho. Wahan bade-bade akshar mein, phone number ke saath, wahi waade likhe milte hain: "gupt rog", "shighrapatan" (premature ejaculation), "night fall", "napunsakta" (impotence), "nisantan" (be-aulaadi), sab ka ilaaj, aksar "ek mulaqat" mein. Ab yahi waade reels aur sponsored posts ban ke bhi aate hain. Inmein se zyada tar ads 1954 mein bane ek law ke under illegal hain. Toh ye ab bhi har jagah kyun hain, aur jo log in numbers pe call karte hain unhe iski kya keemat chukani padti hai?

## Deewarein, reels aur waada

Ye dhandha sharam pe chalta hai. Wet dreams se pareshaan ek teenager, erection ko le ke pareshaan ek shaadishuda aadmi, ek couple jinke bachcha nahi ho raha: sabko bataya jaata hai ki problem secret hai, serious hai, aur sirf ek "specialist" hi ise theek kar sakta hai jo koi awkward sawaal nahi poochta. Ads powders, tel ya capsules ka ek "course" bechte hain. Jo wo nahi dete, wo hai diagnosis.

Deewar pe likhi bahut si "bimaariyan" bimaari hain hi nahi. Night fall, yaani wet dreams, shareer ka ek normal kaam hai. Masturbation kisi ko kamzor nahi karta. Baaki cheezein real conditions hain jinka real ilaaj hai, aur yahi is dhandhe ko aur khatarnaak banata hai: baar-baar hone wali erection ki problem diabetes, high blood pressure ya high cholesterol ka sign ho sakti hai [[nhs-ed]], aur genitals pe zakhm ya discharge ek sexually transmitted infection (STI) ho sakta hai jise test aur sahi ilaaj chahiye, powder nahi [[who-sti]].

## 1954 ka law kis cheez pe ban lagata hai

Drugs and Magic Remedies (Objectionable Advertisements) Act, 1954 ka Section 3 kehta hai ki koi bhi insaan aisa ad chhapne mein hissa nahi lega jo ye suggest kare ki koi dawa "the procurement of miscarriage in women or prevention of conception in women" (miscarriage karwane ya pregnancy rokne), "the maintenance or improvement of the capacity of human beings for sexual pleasure" (sexual pleasure ki capacity banaye rakhne ya badhane), "the correction of menstrual disorder in women" (periods ki gadbad theek karne) ke liye, ya Act ke Schedule mein listed kisi bimaari ya condition ke diagnosis, ilaaj, raahat ya bachaav ke liye use ho sakti hai [[sc-ima-order-mar-2025]]. Schedule mein sexual impotence aur venereal diseases shaamil hain, jinmein syphilis aur gonorrhoea bhi hain [[sc-ima-order-mar-2025]]. Section 5 yahi ban "magic remedies" tak badhata hai, jaise taaveez, mantra aur amulets jo inhi kaamon ke liye beche jaate hain [[sc-ima-order-mar-2025]].

Deewar ki zyada tar lines isme aa jaati hain, "sex power" se le ke "periods regular" wali goliyon tak. Section 7 ke under pehli conviction pe chhe mahine tak jail, fine ya dono, aur dobara conviction pe ek saal tak jail, fine ya dono ki saza hai [[sc-ima-order-mar-2025]]. Section 9A is offence ko cognizable banata hai, yaani complaint milne pe police ko FIR darj karni padegi [[sc-ima-order-mar-2025]]. Ye general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## Supreme Court ki 2025 ki finding

26 March 2025 ko, misleading health ads ke baare mein Indian Medical Association ki ek petition sunte hue, Justices Abhay S. Oka aur Ujjal Bhuyan ki bench ne likha: "Though the 1954 Act is more than 70 years old, unfortunately, there is no implementation of the 1954 Act in its true letter and spirit", yaani Act 70 saal se zyada purana hai, par afsos, wo sahi maayne mein laagu hi nahi hua [[sc-ima-order-mar-2025]]. Amicus curiae ne court ko bataya ki kai states ne prosecute karne ki jagah sirf warnings di thi [[sc-ima-order-mar-2025]].

Court ne states ko order diya ki ek mahine ke andar Section 8(1) ke under Act laagu karne ke liye kaafi gazetted officers appoint karein, aur do mahine ke andar toll-free number ya email ke through ek grievance mechanism banayein [[sc-ima-order-mar-2025]].

Ek cognizable offence, jo bade-bade aksharon mein deewar pe likha hai, dashakon tak kaise bacha raha? Jawab ka ek hissa court record mein hai: prosecution ki jagah warnings. Doosra hissa shayad sharam hai. Jo log "gupt rog" clinic ke haathon thage jaate hain, unke complaint karne ke chances sabse kam hote hain, kyunki complaint ka matlab hai zor se bolna ki wo wahan kis liye gaye the. Na complaint, na aise officers jinka kaam dhoondhna ho, toh zyada kuch nahi hota. Court ka order thik inhi do kamiyon pe nishana lagata hai.

## Nakli ilaaj ki keemat

Socho, Patna mein ek 19 saal ke ladke ko ek zakhm hai jisme dard nahi hota. Family doctor ke paas jaane mein sharam aati hai, toh wo deewar wale number pe call karta hai aur hafton ke powders ke paise bharta hai. Zakhm apne aap bhar jaata hai, jaisa syphilis ka shuruaati zakhm aksar karta hai, aur use lagta hai ki wo theek ho gaya. Infection ab bhi wahin hai, aur bina ilaaj ka syphilis saalon tak reh sakta hai aur aakhri stage mein dimaag aur dil va khoon ki naliyon ki bimaariyon tak le ja sakta hai [[who-syphilis]].

Sarkaari data dikhata hai ki ye khatra real hai. 2024-25 mein India ke sarkaari STI clinics mein 46.2 lakh syphilis screenings hui, jinmein se 43,482 (0.94%) reactive aayi; men mein ye 1.54% aur transgender clients mein 4.12% thi [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Ye wo log hain jo clinic tak aaye, poori aabaadi nahi. Usi saal India ne 10,545 syphilis-infected pregnant women ki pehchaan ki [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Pregnancy mein syphilis bachche tak pahunch sakta hai; maa ka diagnosis aur penicillin se ilaaj hi ise rokta hai [[who-syphilis]].

Bahut se STIs mein koi symptom hota hi nahi; sirf test se pata chalta hai. Syphilis, gonorrhoea aur chlamydia jaise bacterial STIs theek ho sakte hain [[who-sti]]. Bina test ke becha gaya powder ye nahi bata sakta ki aadmi ko kaunsa infection hai, aur us partner ke liye kuch nahi karta jise shayad ilaaj ki zaroorat ho. Nakli ilaaj pehle paise khaata hai, phir sehat: uski, uske partner ki, aur kabhi-kabhi ek bachche ki.

## Ad ki report kaise karein, aur asli ilaaj kahan milega

Ad report karne ke liye:

- Jagah aur tareekh ke saath uski photo lo, ya account ke naam ke saath post ka screenshot lo.
- Ise apne state ke drug control ya health department ko bhejo, us toll-free number ya email pe jo Supreme Court ne banwane ka order diya tha, agar tumhare state ne banaya hai.
- Kyunki ye offence cognizable hai, tum police station mein likhit complaint bhi de sakte ho.
- Sponsored posts ko platform pe misleading health claim ke roop mein report karo.

Asli ilaaj ke liye, NACO district hospitals aur medical colleges mein 1,127 Designated STI/RTI Clinics chalata hai, jinka brand naam Suraksha Clinics hai; sabse zyada, 115, Uttar Pradesh mein hain [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Inka pehle se khoob use hota hai: 2024-25 mein 71.95 lakh visits, jinmein se 60.9% women ki thi [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Erection, ejaculation ya fertility ki chinta ho toh sarkaari hospital mein doctor ko dikhao. HIV ki confidential jaankaari aur counselling ke liye NACO ki helpline 1097 pe 16 bhashaon mein 24 ghante madad milti hai [[naco-sankalak-2025]].

Deewar raaz rakhne ka waada karti hai. Sarkaari clinic privacy deta hai, aur saath mein sahi diagnosis bhi.

hiv-act-2017-rights-complaint-guide.en:
Consider a 29-year-old accounts assistant in Nagpur. Blood taken at an office health camp is tested for HIV without anyone telling her. The result reaches her manager before it reaches her. Within a week her desk is in a storeroom and HR is hinting that she should resign. She is hypothetical. The test without her consent, the separate room and the push out of her job are each barred by a law that has been in force since 10 September 2018 [[mohfw-hiv-act-commencement-2018]].

India had an estimated 25.61 lakh people living with HIV in 2024 [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. The HIV and AIDS (Prevention and Control) Act, 2017 protects them and the people who share their homes. This is general information, not legal advice.

## What the law protects, in plain words

Section 3 bars discrimination against a "protected person": anyone who is HIV-positive, and anyone who ordinarily lives or has lived with a person who is [[naco-hiv-aids-act-2017-gazette]]. An HIV-negative wife, child or flatmate is covered too.

The section names 12 forms of discrimination, and the list is not closed. Because of HIV, nobody may:

- deny you a job, sack you or treat you unfairly at work;
- refuse you healthcare or treat you unfairly in it;
- keep you or your child out of a school or college;
- refuse to rent you a home;
- deny you insurance, unless the difference is backed by actuarial studies;
- isolate or segregate you;
- make an HIV test a condition for a job, healthcare or education [[naco-hiv-aids-act-2017-gazette]].

Work is where many cases begin. Sacking someone or treating them unfairly at work because of HIV is listed discrimination [[naco-hiv-aids-act-2017-gazette]], and the usual excuse does not hold: HIV does not spread through everyday contact such as shaking hands or sharing food and water [[who-hiv]]. If an employer claims your status makes you a risk, ask for that claim in writing. It becomes part of your complaint.

## Consent and the right not to disclose

No HIV test may be done on you without your informed consent (Section 5). No one can compel you to disclose your HIV status except by a court order (Section 8) [[naco-hiv-aids-act-2017-gazette]]. An employer, a hospital or a school that demands your status, or tests you without explaining the test and asking you, is on the wrong side of the law.

If your case reaches a court, the court can replace your name with a pseudonym in the record (Section 34). Anyone who discloses a protected person's HIV status learnt through court proceedings can be fined up to Rs 1 lakh, unless a court ordered the disclosure (Section 39) [[naco-hiv-aids-act-2017-gazette]].

## Step by step: Complaints Officer, then Ombudsman

**1. Build the record the same day.** Write down dates, places, names, the exact words used and who was present. Keep letters, messages, the test report and any form you signed. Ask for every dismissal, refusal or demand for a test in writing, because paper is harder to deny.

**2. Complain inside the institution.** The Act provides for Complaints Officers to deal with violations; by March 2025, 33 States/UTs had designated them [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Ask the hospital, school or employer who its Complaints Officer is, hand in a written complaint and keep an acknowledged copy.

**3. Go to the Ombudsman.** Every state government must appoint one or more HIV Ombudsman [[naco-hiv-aids-act-2017-gazette]]. Send a written complaint with copies of your record, keep a dated acknowledgement and ask for a written order. A counsellor at your ART centre or a support group of people living with HIV can help you draft it.

**4. Hold them to the order.** Anyone who ignores an Ombudsman's order can be fined up to Rs 10,000, plus up to Rs 5,000 for every day the failure continues [[naco-hiv-aids-act-2017-gazette]]. If an order is ignored, tell the Ombudsman's office in writing, with dates.

Expect gaps. By March 2025 only 29 States/UTs had notified rules under the Act, though 34 had an Ombudsman and 33 had designated Complaints Officers [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. If you cannot find your Ombudsman, ask your ART centre's counsellor, the State AIDS Control Society or the helpline below.

## Hate speech against people with HIV is a crime

Section 4 bans publishing, propagating or advocating hatred against protected persons, whether in words, signs or any other communication. A notice in a housing society or a message in a WhatsApp group could fall within it. The punishment under Section 37 is 3 months to 2 years in prison, a fine of up to Rs 1 lakh, or both [[naco-hiv-aids-act-2017-gazette]].

Screenshot the message, date and sender before anything is deleted, and take that record to the police or the Ombudsman.

## Free legal help and the NACO helpline

NACO's toll-free helpline 1097 gives confidential counselling round the clock in 16 languages [[naco-sankalak-2025]], and can point you to services near you [[naco]]. For a lawyer, the National Legal Services Authority and its district offices provide free legal aid to those who qualify [[nalsa]].

The accounts assistant in Nagpur has three violations to report. What turns them into a case is the record she starts today and the complaint she files. The Act does nothing until someone uses it.
hiv-act-2017-rights-complaint-guide.hg:
Ek hypothetical socho: Nagpur ki ek 29 saal ki accounts assistant. Office ke health camp mein uska blood liya jaata hai aur use bataye bina HIV test kar diya jaata hai. Result us tak pahunchne se pehle uske manager tak pahunch jaata hai. Ek hafte ke andar uski desk storeroom mein shift ho jaati hai, aur HR ishaaron mein keh raha hai ki woh resign kar de. Yeh ladki hypothetical hai. Bina consent ka test, alag kamra aur job se dhakelna, in teeno par ek aise law ke tahat rok hai jo 10 September 2018 se lagu hai [[mohfw-hiv-act-commencement-2018]].

2024 mein India mein estimated 25.61 lakh log HIV ke saath jee rahe the [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. HIV and AIDS (Prevention and Control) Act, 2017 unhe protect karta hai, aur unke saath ek ghar mein rehne walon ko bhi. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## Law kya protect karta hai, seedhe shabdon mein

Section 3 "protected person" ke saath discrimination ko rokta hai. Protected person matlab jo HIV-positive hai, aur woh bhi jo kisi HIV-positive insaan ke saath aam taur par rehta hai ya reh chuka hai [[naco-hiv-aids-act-2017-gazette]]. Yaani HIV-negative wife, bachcha ya flatmate bhi cover hote hain.

Section mein 12 tarah ke discrimination likhe hain, aur list yahin band nahi hoti. HIV ki wajah se koi bhi:

- tumhe job dene se mana nahi kar sakta, job se nikal nahi sakta, na kaam par unfair treatment de sakta hai;
- tumhe healthcare se mana nahi kar sakta, na ilaaj mein unfair treatment de sakta hai;
- tumhe ya tumhare bachche ko school ya college se bahar nahi rakh sakta;
- tumhe ghar kiraye par dene se mana nahi kar sakta;
- tumhe insurance se mana nahi kar sakta, jab tak farak ke peeche actuarial studies na hon;
- tumhe isolate ya segregate nahi kar sakta;
- job, healthcare ya education ke liye HIV test ki condition nahi rakh sakta [[naco-hiv-aids-act-2017-gazette]].

Kai cases kaam ki jagah se shuru hote hain. HIV ki wajah se kisi ko job se nikalna ya kaam par unfair treatment dena list mein likha discrimination hai [[naco-hiv-aids-act-2017-gazette]], aur aam bahana tikta nahi: haath milane ya khana-paani share karne jaise roz ke contact se HIV nahi failta [[who-hiv]]. Agar employer kahe ki tumhare status se risk hai, toh yeh baat likhit mein maango. Yeh tumhari complaint ka hissa banegi.

## Consent aur status na batane ka haq

Tumhari informed consent ke bina tumhara HIV test nahi ho sakta (Section 5). Court order ke bina koi tumhe apna HIV status batane ke liye majboor nahi kar sakta (Section 8) [[naco-hiv-aids-act-2017-gazette]]. Jo employer, hospital ya school tumhara status maange, ya test samjhaye aur poochhe bina tumhara test kar de, woh law ke galat side par hai.

Agar tumhara case court tak pahunche, toh court record mein tumhare naam ki jagah pseudonym likhwa sakta hai (Section 34). Court proceedings se kisi protected person ka HIV status jaan kar use bahar batane wale par Rs 1 lakh tak fine lag sakta hai, jab tak court ne khud disclosure ka order na diya ho (Section 39) [[naco-hiv-aids-act-2017-gazette]].

## Step by step: pehle Complaints Officer, phir Ombudsman

**1. Usi din record banao.** Dates, jagah, naam, exact words aur kaun-kaun maujood tha, sab likh lo. Letters, messages, test report aur jo bhi form tumne sign kiya, sambhal kar rakho. Job se nikalna ho, kisi cheez se mana karna ho ya test ki demand ho, har baat likhit mein maango, kyunki kaagaz se mukarna mushkil hota hai.

**2. Institution ke andar complaint karo.** Act mein violations dekhne ke liye Complaints Officers ka intezaam hai; March 2025 tak 33 States/UTs ne unhe designate kiya tha [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Hospital, school ya employer se poocho ki unka Complaints Officer kaun hai, likhit complaint do aur acknowledge ki hui copy apne paas rakho.

**3. Ombudsman ke paas jao.** Har state government ko ek ya zyada HIV Ombudsman appoint karne hi hote hain [[naco-hiv-aids-act-2017-gazette]]. Apne record ki copies ke saath likhit complaint bhejo, date wala acknowledgement rakho aur likhit order maango. ART centre ka counsellor ya HIV ke saath jee rahe logon ka koi support group complaint likhne mein madad kar sakta hai.

**4. Order par amal karwao.** Jo Ombudsman ka order na maane, us par Rs 10,000 tak ka fine lag sakta hai, aur jab tak woh na maane, har din Rs 5,000 tak aur [[naco-hiv-aids-act-2017-gazette]]. Agar order nahi maana gaya, toh Ombudsman ke office ko dates ke saath likhit mein batao.

Gaps ke liye taiyaar raho. March 2025 tak sirf 29 States/UTs ne Act ke rules notify kiye the, jabki 34 mein Ombudsman tha aur 33 mein Complaints Officers designate ho chuke the [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Apna Ombudsman na mile, toh ART centre ke counsellor se, State AIDS Control Society se ya neeche di gayi helpline se poocho.

## HIV wale logon ke khilaaf hate speech crime hai

Section 4 protected persons ke khilaaf nafrat publish, propagate ya advocate karne ko ban karta hai, chahe shabdon se ho, signs se, ya kisi aur tarah ke communication se. Housing society ka notice ya WhatsApp group ka message bhi iske daayre mein aa sakta hai. Section 37 ke under saza hai 3 mahine se 2 saal tak ki jail, Rs 1 lakh tak fine, ya dono [[naco-hiv-aids-act-2017-gazette]].

Kuch bhi delete hone se pehle message, date aur bhejne wale ka screenshot le lo, aur woh record police ya Ombudsman ke paas le jao.

## Free legal help aur NACO helpline

NACO ki toll-free helpline 1097 din-raat 16 languages mein confidential counselling deti hai [[naco-sankalak-2025]], aur tumhe paas ki services tak pahuncha sakti hai [[naco]]. Lawyer ke liye, National Legal Services Authority aur uske district offices un logon ko free legal aid dete hain jo iske liye qualify karte hain [[nalsa]].

Nagpur ki us accounts assistant ke paas report karne ke liye teen violations hain. Unhe case wahi record banayega jo woh aaj se likhna shuru karegi, aur wahi complaint jo woh file karegi. Jab tak koi ise use nahi karta, Act khud kuch nahi karta.

hiv-act-implementation-gaps-audit.en:
Imagine a 34-year-old hotel cook in Vijayawada who is dismissed in January 2018, after his employer learns he has HIV. A law banning exactly that had received the President's assent nine months earlier [[naco-hiv-aids-act-2017-gazette]]. He could not use a word of it. The Act existed on paper and was not yet in force.

That gap is the first entry in an audit of India's HIV law. Read against the government's own records, the HIV and AIDS (Prevention and Control) Act, 2017 is a set of real rights attached to machinery that is slow, incomplete and very hard to see into. This is general information, not legal advice.

## From Parliament to paper: the 17-month wait

The Act, No. 16 of 2017, received assent on 20 April 2017 and was published in the Gazette the next day. But its Section 1(3) said it would come into force only on a date the Central Government notified [[naco-hiv-aids-act-2017-gazette]]. The notification named 10 September 2018, about 17 months later [[mohfw-hiv-act-commencement-2018]].

For those months, nothing in the Act could be enforced: not the ban on discrimination in jobs, hospitals and schools, not the rule against HIV testing without informed consent, not the penalty for spreading hatred [[naco-hiv-aids-act-2017-gazette]].

Commencement was only the first step. Every state government also had to appoint one or more Ombudsman to hear complaints [[naco-hiv-aids-act-2017-gazette]], and states had to notify rules under the Act. By March 2025, that second stage was still unfinished [[naco-sankalak-2025]].

## Rules, Ombudsmen and Complaints Officers: the gaps

NACO's own status report gives the position in March 2025, nearly eight years after the Act became law: 29 States/UTs had notified rules, 34 had an Ombudsman and 33 had designated Complaints Officers [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. India has 36 States and UTs [[pib-hpv-update-march-2026]].

| Under the Act | States/UTs that had it, March 2025 | Missing, of 36 |
|---|---|---|
| Rules notified | 29 | 7 |
| Ombudsman in place | 34 | 2 |
| Complaints Officers designated | 33 | 3 |

Two problems sit inside that table. First, 34 Ombudsmen against 29 sets of rules means at least five States/UTs had an Ombudsman in place without notified rules under the Act.

Second, the report counts States/UTs that have designated Complaints Officers, not hospitals, schools or companies, so it cannot tell you whether the institution in front of you has one. Nor does it say whether any of these offices has heard a single complaint.

## 'As far as possible': the clause that weakens the right to treatment

On discrimination the Act speaks in commands. On treatment it hedges. Section 14 says government measures shall include providing diagnostic facilities, antiretroviral therapy (ART) and management of opportunistic infections "as far as possible" [[naco-hiv-aids-act-2017-gazette]].

In practice the medicine is there. In March 2025, 18.60 lakh people were on ART: 17.54 lakh at 800 government centres, where it is free, and an estimated 1.06 lakh in the private sector [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. But what delivers it is a programme, not a legal guarantee. The fifth phase of the National AIDS and STD Control Programme ran as a fully funded central scheme from 1 April 2021 to 31 March 2026 [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. A scheme has a budget and an end date. A right has neither.

The difference matters most to the people the system has not reached. India had an estimated 25.61 lakh people living with HIV in 2024, and in 2024-25 only 86.6% of those diagnosed were on treatment [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. If a centre is too far away or runs short of medicine, "as far as possible" is the state's answer, written into the law in advance.

## What nobody publishes: complaints, orders, penalties

The Act did build in transparency. Section 28 requires every Ombudsman to report every six months on the number and nature of complaints received, and to publish that report online [[naco-hiv-aids-act-2017-gazette]].

Our researchers found no national compilation of those complaints or their outcomes. Nor did they find national data on prosecutions under Section 37, which punishes spreading hatred against people with HIV with 3 months to 2 years in prison, a fine of up to Rs 1 lakh, or both [[naco-hiv-aids-act-2017-gazette]].

The contrast is in NACO's own report. It counts calls to the 1097 helpline to the last digit: 4,32,474 in 2024-25 [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. For the Act, it counts offices. That an Ombudsman exists says nothing about how many complaints were filed, heard or resolved.

The penalty is modest too. Anyone who ignores an Ombudsman's order can be fined up to Rs 10,000, plus up to Rs 5,000 for every day the failure continues [[naco-hiv-aids-act-2017-gazette]]. With no national record of outcomes, nobody outside the system can say whether that fine has ever been imposed.

> India counts every call to its HIV helpline. No national count of complaints under its HIV law could be found.

## What would make the Act real

Three fixes need no new law. The States/UTs still without rules or an Ombudsman can notify and appoint them. Every Ombudsman can publish a name, an address and the six-monthly report the Act already demands. NACO can add one table to its annual report: complaints received, orders passed and fines imposed, state by state.

The fourth fix belongs to Parliament: removing "as far as possible" from Section 14, so that treatment becomes something a patient can demand.

Until then, the Act depends on people using it. Our guide to the HIV Act and its Ombudsman explains how to complain. NACO's helpline 1097 gives confidential counselling round the clock in 16 languages [[naco-sankalak-2025]].

The cook in Vijayawada would have a law in force today. Whether he would also have rules, an Ombudsman who answers and a record anyone can check still depends on the state he lives in.
hiv-act-implementation-gaps-audit.hg:
Ek hypothetical socho: Vijayawada ka ek 34 saal ka hotel cook, jise January 2018 mein job se nikal diya jaata hai, jab uske employer ko pata chalta hai ki use HIV hai. Theek isi cheez ko ban karne wale law ko nau mahine pehle President ki assent mil chuki thi [[naco-hiv-aids-act-2017-gazette]]. Phir bhi woh us law ka ek shabd use nahi kar sakta tha. Act kaagaz par tha, lagu nahi hua tha.

India ke HIV law ke audit mein yeh gap pehli entry hai. Government ke apne records ke saamne rakh kar padho, toh HIV and AIDS (Prevention and Control) Act, 2017 asli rights ka ek set hai, jo aisi machinery se juda hai jo slow hai, adhoori hai, aur jiske andar jhaankna bahut mushkil hai. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## Parliament se kaagaz tak: 17 mahine ka intezaar

Act, No. 16 of 2017, ko 20 April 2017 ko assent mili aur agle din yeh Gazette mein publish hua. Lekin iske Section 1(3) mein likha tha ki yeh tabhi lagu hoga jab Central Government date notify karegi [[naco-hiv-aids-act-2017-gazette]]. Notification mein date aayi 10 September 2018, yaani lagbhag 17 mahine baad [[mohfw-hiv-act-commencement-2018]].

Un mahino mein Act ki koi bhi baat enforce nahi ho sakti thi: na jobs, hospitals aur schools mein discrimination par ban, na informed consent ke bina HIV test par rok, na nafrat failane ki saza [[naco-hiv-aids-act-2017-gazette]].

Lagu hona sirf pehla step tha. Har state government ko complaints sunne ke liye ek ya zyada Ombudsman bhi appoint karne the [[naco-hiv-aids-act-2017-gazette]], aur states ko Act ke rules notify karne the. March 2025 tak bhi yeh doosra stage adhoora tha [[naco-sankalak-2025]].

## Rules, Ombudsman aur Complaints Officers: gaps kahan hain

NACO ki apni status report March 2025 ki position batati hai, yaani Act ke law banne ke lagbhag aath saal baad: 29 States/UTs ne rules notify kiye the, 34 mein Ombudsman tha aur 33 mein Complaints Officers designate hue the [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. India mein 36 States aur UTs hain [[pib-hpv-update-march-2026]].

| Act ke under | March 2025 mein kitne States/UTs mein tha | 36 mein se kitno mein nahi |
|---|---|---|
| Rules notify hue | 29 | 7 |
| Ombudsman maujood | 34 | 2 |
| Complaints Officers designate hue | 33 | 3 |

Is table ke andar do problems chhupi hain. Pehli: 34 Ombudsman aur sirf 29 sets of rules ka matlab hai ki kam se kam paanch States/UTs mein Ombudsman toh tha, par Act ke notified rules nahi the.

Doosri: report un States/UTs ko ginti hai jinhone Complaints Officers designate kiye, hospitals, schools ya companies ko nahi. Isliye woh yeh nahi bata sakti ki tumhare saamne wale institution mein Complaints Officer hai ya nahi. Na hi yeh batati hai ki in mein se kisi office ne ek bhi complaint suni hai ya nahi.

## 'As far as possible': woh clause jo treatment ke right ko kamzor karta hai

Discrimination par Act hukm ki bhasha mein bolta hai. Treatment par woh bach kar bolta hai. Section 14 kehta hai ki government ke measures mein diagnostic facilities, antiretroviral therapy (ART) aur opportunistic infections ka management dena shaamil hoga, "as far as possible" [[naco-hiv-aids-act-2017-gazette]].

Practice mein medicine mil rahi hai. March 2025 mein 18.60 lakh log ART par the: 17.54 lakh 800 government centres par, jahan yeh free hai, aur estimated 1.06 lakh private sector mein [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Lekin ise pahunchane wali cheez ek programme hai, legal guarantee nahi. National AIDS and STD Control Programme ka fifth phase 1 April 2021 se 31 March 2026 tak ek fully funded central scheme ke roop mein chala [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Scheme ka ek budget hota hai aur ek end date. Right ka dono mein se kuch nahi hota.

Yeh farak sabse zyada un logon ke liye maayne rakhta hai jin tak system pahuncha hi nahi. 2024 mein India mein estimated 25.61 lakh log HIV ke saath jee rahe the, aur 2024-25 mein diagnose hue logon mein se sirf 86.6% treatment par the [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Agar centre bahut door ho ya medicine kam pad jaaye, toh "as far as possible" state ka jawab hai, jo law mein pehle se likha hua hai.

## Jo koi publish nahi karta: complaints, orders, penalties

Act ne transparency ka intezaam kiya tha. Section 28 ke hisaab se har Ombudsman ko har chhe mahine mein report deni hoti hai ki kitni aur kis tarah ki complaints aayi, aur yeh report online publish karni hoti hai [[naco-hiv-aids-act-2017-gazette]].

Hamare researchers ko in complaints ya unke outcomes ka koi national compilation nahi mila. Section 37 ke under prosecutions ka national data bhi nahi mila. Yeh section HIV wale logon ke khilaaf nafrat failane par 3 mahine se 2 saal tak ki jail, Rs 1 lakh tak fine, ya dono ki saza deta hai [[naco-hiv-aids-act-2017-gazette]].

Farak NACO ki apni report mein dikhta hai. Woh 1097 helpline par aayi calls aakhri digit tak ginti hai: 2024-25 mein 4,32,474 [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Act ke liye woh sirf offices ginti hai. Ombudsman ka hona yeh nahi batata ki kitni complaints file hui, suni gayi ya resolve hui.

Penalty bhi chhoti hai. Ombudsman ka order na maanne wale par Rs 10,000 tak ka fine lag sakta hai, aur jab tak woh na maane, har din Rs 5,000 tak aur [[naco-hiv-aids-act-2017-gazette]]. Outcomes ka koi national record nahi hai, isliye system ke bahar ka koi nahi keh sakta ki yeh fine kabhi laga bhi hai ya nahi.

> India apni HIV helpline par aayi har call ginta hai. Apne HIV law ke under hui complaints ki koi national ginti nahi mili.

## Act asli kaise banega

Teen fixes ke liye naya law nahi chahiye. Jin States/UTs mein abhi rules ya Ombudsman nahi hain, woh rules notify aur Ombudsman appoint kar sakte hain. Har Ombudsman apna naam, address aur woh six-monthly report publish kar sakta hai jo Act pehle se maangta hai. NACO apni annual report mein ek table jod sakta hai: state-wise kitni complaints aayi, kitne orders pass hue, kitne fines lage.

Chautha fix Parliament ke haath mein hai: Section 14 se "as far as possible" hatana, taaki treatment aisi cheez ban jaaye jise patient haq se maang sake.

Tab tak yeh Act un logon par tika hai jo ise use karte hain. HIV Act aur Ombudsman par hamari guide batati hai ki complaint kaise karni hai. NACO ki helpline 1097 din-raat 16 languages mein confidential counselling deti hai [[naco-sankalak-2025]].

Vijayawada ke us cook ke paas aaj ek lagu law hota. Lekin uske paas rules, jawab dene wala Ombudsman aur aisa record jise koi bhi check kar sake, yeh sab bhi hota ya nahi, yeh ab bhi is par depend karta hai ki woh kis state mein rehta hai.

hiv-cervical-cancer-six-times-risk.en:
Consider a 34-year-old in Guntur who has collected her HIV medicines from the same government ART centre for seven years. She has never missed a refill. Her viral load is tested and her tablets are counted. In seven years, nobody has mentioned her cervix. She is hypothetical. The gap she falls into is not: the World Health Organization says women living with HIV are six times more likely to develop cervical cancer than women without HIV [[who-cervical-cancer-factsheet-2026]].

## Why HIV and HPV are a dangerous pair

Cervical cancer starts with a virus. Human papillomavirus, or HPV, is a common infection passed on through sexual contact. Almost all sexually active people get it at some point, usually without symptoms, and in most cases the immune system clears it [[who-cervical]]. The danger begins when a high-risk type stays for years in the cervix, the opening of the uterus, and changes its cells.

HIV attacks the same immune system that is supposed to do the clearing [[who-hiv]]. With weaker defences, HPV is more likely to stay, and the damage moves faster. WHO says abnormal cells usually take 15 to 20 years to become cancer. In women with weakened immune systems, such as untreated HIV, it can take 5 to 10 [[who-cervical]].

Notice the word "untreated". Antiretroviral therapy (ART) lets the immune system grow stronger again [[who-hiv]], one more reason to take it every day. It does not cancel the need for screening: WHO's advice covers all women living with HIV, not only those off treatment.

## Six times the risk: what WHO's number means

"Six times" compares two groups. It is not a prediction about one woman, and most women living with HIV will never develop cervical cancer. It means that far more women in a group with HIV will get this cancer than in an equal group without HIV, unless something interrupts the process.

Something can. Screening finds changed cells long before they turn into cancer, and treating them is a simple procedure that prevents the disease [[who-cervical]]. So the six-fold risk is really a measure of what is lost when nobody looks.

India mostly does not look. In 2019-21, only 1.2% of women aged 15-49 had ever been screened for cervical cancer [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. The latest GLOBOCAN estimate for India is 79,360 new cases and 36,319 deaths in 2024 [[iarc-globocan-india-factsheet-2024]]. Neither figure tells us how many of those women were living with HIV.

## The missed chance at ART centres

India's general screening problem is reach: the health system has to find women who feel well and persuade them to come in. Women living with HIV are the exception. An estimated 25.61 lakh people were living with HIV in India in 2024. By March 2025, 18.60 lakh of them were on ART, including 17.54 lakh at 800 government ART centres, and about 7.98 lakh of the people at those government centres were women [[naco-sankalak-2025]].

These women are not hard to find. They return to the same centre again and again, and it already has their names, ages and phone numbers. The programme knows how to follow people for years: in 2024-25, 97.6% of people on treatment who were tested had the virus suppressed [[naco-sankalak-2025]].

> A system that can deliver a daily pill and a regular viral load test to lakhs of people can deliver one cervical test every few years to the women among them.

The verified programme figures available to us count HIV tests, treatment and viral suppression. They do not tell us how many of those 7.98 lakh women have ever had their cervix checked.

## The screening schedule for women with HIV

WHO sets a separate, tighter schedule for women living with HIV [[who-cervical]].

| | Most women | Women living with HIV |
|---|---|---|
| Start screening at | Age 30 | Age 25 |
| Repeat | Every 5 to 10 years | Every 3 to 5 years |
| After a positive screen | Treatment may be offered at the same visit | A second test before treatment is especially recommended |

The test itself is the same one other women get: an HPV test on a swab, a Pap smear, or VIA, in which a trained health worker looks at the cervix after applying dilute acetic acid. For HPV testing, WHO says a sample a woman collects herself is as reliable as one collected by a health worker [[who-cervical]].

The vaccine advice differs too. WHO says people living with HIV are a priority for HPV vaccination and should ideally get two or three doses [[who-cervical]]. India's free campaign offers a single dose to girls aged 14 [[pib-hpv-campaign-launch-2026]]. If your daughter is living with HIV, ask her ART doctor how many doses she needs.

## How to ask for a test

You do not need a symptom or anyone's permission. If you are 25 or older, tell the doctor or counsellor at your next ART visit: "I have never had a cervical screening test. Where can I get it done?" Ask for a written referral to the gynaecology OPD, and try to go the same day so that it does not cost another day's wages and another bus fare.

Elsewhere, telling the doctor your HIV status helps them choose the right schedule, but that decision is yours. The HIV Act, 2017 bars discrimination in healthcare, and no one can be compelled to disclose their HIV status except by a court order [[naco-hiv-aids-act-2017-gazette]]. If a facility turns you away, call the national AIDS helpline, 1097: toll-free, confidential and open round the clock [[naco-sankalak-2025]].

Do not wait for symptoms, because precancers rarely cause any [[who-cervical]]. But bleeding between periods, after sex or after menopause, or unusual discharge, needs a doctor now, not on the next refill date. The same schedule applies to trans men and anyone else living with HIV who has a cervix.

A positive screen is not a cancer diagnosis; it usually means changed cells that can be treated in time. The woman in Guntur has done everything the health system asked of her for seven years. The system owes her one more question.
hiv-cervical-cancer-six-times-risk.hg:
Socho, Guntur ki ek 34 saal ki woman hai jo saat saal se ek hi government ART centre se apni HIV ki dawa le rahi hai. Usne ek bhi refill miss nahi kiya. Uska viral load test hota hai, uski tablets gini jaati hain. Saat saal mein kisi ne uske cervix ka zikr tak nahi kiya. Yeh woman hypothetical hai. Jis gap mein woh girti hai, woh asli hai: World Health Organization ke mutabik HIV ke saath jee rahi women ko cervical cancer hone ka chance HIV ke bina wali women se chhe guna zyada hai [[who-cervical-cancer-factsheet-2026]].

## HIV aur HPV ki jodi itni khatarnaak kyun hai

Cervical cancer ek virus se shuru hota hai. Human papillomavirus, yaani HPV, ek common infection hai jo sexual contact se failta hai. Sex karne wale lagbhag sabhi logon ko yeh kabhi na kabhi hota hai, aksar bina kisi symptom ke, aur zyadatar cases mein immune system ise khud clear kar deta hai [[who-cervical]]. Khatra tab shuru hota hai jab koi high-risk type saalon tak cervix mein tika rahe aur uske cells ko badal de. Cervix yaani uterus ka muh.

HIV usi immune system par attack karta hai jise yeh safai karni hoti hai [[who-hiv]]. Defence kamzor ho, toh HPV ke tike rehne ka chance badh jaata hai, aur nuksaan tez chalta hai. WHO ke mutabik abnormal cells ko cancer banne mein aam taur par 15 se 20 saal lagte hain. Jin women ka immune system kamzor hai, jaise untreated HIV mein, unmein yeh 5 se 10 saal mein ho sakta hai [[who-cervical]].

"Untreated" shabd par dhyan do. Antiretroviral therapy (ART) immune system ko wapas strong hone deti hai [[who-hiv]], yaani dawa roz lene ki ek aur wajah. Par isse screening ki zaroorat khatam nahi hoti: WHO ki advice HIV ke saath jee rahi sabhi women ke liye hai, sirf unke liye nahi jo treatment par nahi hain.

## Chhe guna risk: WHO ke is number ka matlab

"Chhe guna" do groups ka comparison hai. Yeh kisi ek woman ke baare mein prediction nahi hai, aur HIV ke saath jee rahi zyadatar women ko cervical cancer kabhi nahi hoga. Matlab bas itna hai ki HIV wali women ke ek group mein yeh cancer, barabar size ke bina-HIV wale group se kahin zyada women ko hoga, agar beech mein kuch is process ko roke nahi.

Aur roka ja sakta hai. Screening badle hue cells ko cancer banne se bahut pehle pakad leti hai, aur unka treatment ek simple procedure hai jo bimari ko hone se rok deta hai [[who-cervical]]. Isliye chhe guna risk asal mein yeh naapta hai ki jab koi dekhta hi nahi, toh kitna kuch haath se nikal jaata hai.

India zyadatar dekhta hi nahi. 2019-21 mein 15-49 saal ki sirf 1.2% women ne kabhi cervical cancer screening karwayi thi [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. GLOBOCAN ka latest estimate India ke liye 2024 mein 79,360 naye cases aur 36,319 deaths ka hai [[iarc-globocan-india-factsheet-2024]]. Dono mein se koi figure yeh nahi batata ki in women mein se kitni HIV ke saath jee rahi thin.

## ART centres par haath se nikalta mauka

India mein screening ki aam problem pahunch ki hai: health system ko un women ko dhoondhna padta hai jo khud ko theek mehsoos karti hain, aur unhe test ke liye aane par raazi karna padta hai. HIV ke saath jee rahi women is mamle mein alag hain. 2024 mein India mein estimated 25.61 lakh log HIV ke saath jee rahe the. March 2025 tak inmein se 18.60 lakh ART par the, jinmein 17.54 lakh 800 government ART centres par the, aur in government centres ke logon mein lagbhag 7.98 lakh women thin [[naco-sankalak-2025]].

In women ko dhoondhna mushkil nahi hai. Yeh baar-baar usi centre par lautti hain, aur centre ke paas pehle se inke naam, umar aur phone number hain. Programme ko logon ko saalon tak follow karna aata hai: 2024-25 mein treatment par jin logon ka test hua, unmein se 97.6% mein virus suppressed tha [[naco-sankalak-2025]].

> Jo system lakhon logon tak roz ki goli aur regular viral load test pahuncha sakta hai, woh unhi mein shaamil women tak kuch saalon mein ek cervical test bhi pahuncha sakta hai.

Programme ke jo verified figures humare paas hain, woh HIV tests, treatment aur viral suppression ginte hain. Woh yeh nahi batate ki un 7.98 lakh women mein se kitnon ke cervix ki kabhi jaanch hui hai.

## HIV ke saath jee rahi women ka screening schedule

WHO ne HIV ke saath jee rahi women ke liye alag aur zyada tight schedule rakha hai [[who-cervical]].

| | Zyadatar women | HIV ke saath jee rahi women |
|---|---|---|
| Screening kab shuru ho | 30 saal ki umar se | 25 saal ki umar se |
| Kitne time mein dobara | Har 5 se 10 saal mein | Har 3 se 5 saal mein |
| Screen positive aaye toh | Treatment usi visit mein offer ho sakta hai | Treatment se pehle ek doosra test khaas taur par recommended hai |

Test wahi hai jo baaki women ka hota hai: swab par HPV test, Pap smear, ya VIA, jisme ek trained health worker cervix par dilute acetic acid lagakar use dekhta hai. HPV testing ke liye WHO kehta hai ki jo sample woman khud leti hai, woh health worker ke liye gaye sample jitna hi reliable hai [[who-cervical]].

Vaccine ki advice bhi alag hai. WHO ke mutabik HIV ke saath jee rahe log HPV vaccination ke liye priority hain aur unhe ideally do ya teen doses milni chahiye [[who-cervical]]. India ke free campaign mein 14 saal ki ladkiyon ko single dose di jaati hai [[pib-hpv-campaign-launch-2026]]. Agar tumhari beti HIV ke saath jee rahi hai, toh uske ART doctor se poocho ki use kitni doses chahiye.

## Test kaise maangein

Iske liye na symptom chahiye, na kisi ki permission. Agar tum 25 ya usse zyada umar ki ho, toh agli ART visit par doctor ya counsellor se kaho: "Meri kabhi cervical screening nahi hui. Yeh kahan ho sakti hai?" Gynaecology OPD ke liye likhit referral maango, aur koshish karo ki usi din chali jao, taaki ek aur din ki mazdoori aur ek aur bus ka kiraya na lage.

Kisi aur clinic mein doctor ko apna HIV status batane se use sahi schedule chunne mein madad milti hai, par yeh faisla tumhara hai. HIV Act, 2017 healthcare mein discrimination par rok lagata hai, aur court order ke bina kisi ko apna HIV status batane par majboor nahi kiya ja sakta [[naco-hiv-aids-act-2017-gazette]]. Agar koi facility tumhe lauta de, toh national AIDS helpline 1097 par call karo: toll-free, confidential aur chaubees ghante khuli [[naco-sankalak-2025]].

Symptoms ka wait mat karo, kyunki precancer mein aksar koi symptom hota hi nahi [[who-cervical]]. Lekin periods ke beech, sex ke baad ya menopause ke baad bleeding ho, ya ajeeb discharge ho, toh doctor ko abhi dikhao, agli refill date par nahi. Yahi schedule trans men aur HIV ke saath jee rahe har us insaan par laagu hota hai jiske paas cervix hai.

Positive screen ka matlab cancer ka diagnosis nahi hai; aksar iska matlab hota hai badle hue cells, jinka time rehte treatment ho sakta hai. Guntur ki us woman ne saat saal tak woh sab kiya jo health system ne usse maanga. Ab system par uska ek sawaal udhaar hai.

hiv-india-2024-numbers-state-burden.en:
If you were born after 2000, HIV probably reached you as history: red ribbons, old public-service ads, a disease your parents' generation worried about. The data says it never left. In 2024 an estimated 25.61 lakh people in India were living with HIV, the second-largest number in any country after South Africa [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Knowledge is thin, too. In the fifth National Family Health Survey (NFHS-5, 2019-21), only 20.1% of young women and 28.5% of young men aged 15-24 had comprehensive knowledge of HIV, the basic facts about how it spreads and how to prevent it [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Here are the numbers behind the virus, and how to read them without being fooled.

## 25.61 lakh: the world's second-largest HIV population

India's National AIDS Control Organisation (NACO) puts the number of people living with HIV at 25.61 lakh in 2024 [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. As a share of adults aged 15-49, though, India's rate is low: 0.20%, against a global average of 0.70% [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Both facts are true at once. In a country this large, a small percentage is still an enormous number of people.

Many of them are not yet on anyone's list. In 2024-25, NACO estimated that 83.9% of people living with HIV knew their status [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Roughly one in six did not. As of March 2025, 18.60 lakh people were on antiretroviral therapy (ART), the medicine that keeps the virus in check: 17.54 lakh at 800 government ART centres and an estimated 1.06 lakh in the private sector [[naco-sankalak-2025]].

## From the late-1990s peak to 0.20%: what fell

The share of Indian adults with HIV peaked at around 0.58-0.59% in 1997-98. It then fell to about 0.44% in 2005, 0.33% in 2010, 0.27% in 2015, 0.23% in 2020 and 0.20% in 2024 [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. That decline is real.

But a falling percentage is not the same as fewer people. NACO estimates that the number living with HIV dropped from about 32 lakh in 2005 to about 27 lakh in 2010, and has stayed at roughly 25-26 lakh since about 2013 [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. So the percentage can keep falling while the count barely moves. The count is stuck for one good reason and one bad one. The good reason: with ART, HIV is a manageable long-term condition, and people can live long, healthy lives [[who-hiv]]. The bad reason: new infections have not fallen fast enough. NACO's own reading is that deaths are falling faster than new infections, so the number living with HIV is still slowly growing [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. That second problem is the subject of our story on the HIV prevention target India missed.

## Five states, more than half the total

HIV is not spread evenly. NACO's 2024 state estimates rank Maharashtra first, followed by Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Uttar Pradesh and Tamil Nadu [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. These five states alone hold more than half of everyone living with HIV in India.

| State | People living with HIV (2024 estimate) |
|---|---|
| Maharashtra | 3,99,023 |
| Andhra Pradesh | 3,10,451 |
| Karnataka | 2,91,348 |
| Uttar Pradesh | 1,95,427 |
| Tamil Nadu | 1,65,971 |
| Telangana | 1,56,961 |

These are not the same kind of epidemic. The big southern and western states have high counts but relatively low rates of new infection today [[naco-sankalak-2025]], which suggests many people there were infected years ago and are living with the virus. Uttar Pradesh is on the list mainly because of its sheer population: its adult prevalence is half the national average [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. The map of new infections looks different. Bihar, with 1,54,296 people living with HIV, had the highest estimated number of new infections of any state in 2024 [[naco-sankalak-2025]]; our story on Bihar and Punjab follows that second map.

The highest rates sit elsewhere, in small north-eastern states. Mizoram's adult prevalence was 2.75% in 2024, nearly 14 times the national average [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. A national figure of 0.20% hides these concentrated epidemics; our story on the North-East, where shared needles and sex both spread HIV, looks at them closely.

## How people say they got HIV

When someone tests positive in the government programme, the programme records how the person thinks they were infected. Of 1,63,306 people newly diagnosed in 2024-25, 73.7% reported heterosexual sex: 32.1% with casual partners, 26.5% with regular partners and 15.1% with commercial partners [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Another 11.5% reported shared needles or syringes, 5.4% homosexual or bisexual sex, 3.5% mother-to-child transmission and 1.2% infected blood; 4.7% gave no route.

Look at the 26.5%. More than one in four people newly diagnosed named a regular partner as the route. "I only have one partner" is not the same as "I am safe" unless both of you have been tested.

These are also people's own answers at diagnosis. Stigma can push people to under-report sex between men and drug use, so those routes may be bigger than the record shows. The needle share has risen sharply: it was under 3% of new diagnoses in 2017-18 and 12.5% in 2023-24 [[naco-sankalak-2025]].

## How to read a modelled estimate

The big national figures, for people living with HIV, new infections and deaths, are not headcounts. India does not test every adult; these numbers come from a statistical model, not a count of diagnosed people. Three rules keep you honest:

1. **Look at the range.** The 25.61 lakh figure has an uncertainty range of 21.89 lakh to 30.67 lakh [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. The true number could be several lakh lower or higher.
2. **Never compare across rounds.** Each new round of estimates redraws the whole past. NACO's previous report gave slightly different values for the same years, so setting an old report's figure against a new one can invent a rise or a fall that never happened.
3. **Check what is being counted.** People living with HIV, new infections and deaths move differently. Between 2010 and 2024, AIDS-related deaths fell by 81.4%, but new infections by only 48.7% [[naco-sankalak-2025]].

The bottom line is not fear. HIV is treatable, and a person on effective treatment with an undetectable viral load does not pass HIV on through sex [[who-hiv]]. The danger is not knowing. If you have ever had sex without a condom or shared injecting equipment, a test is the only way to find out, and treatment at government ART centres is free [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. NACO's toll-free helpline, 1097 [[naco]], offers confidential counselling round the clock in 16 languages [[naco-sankalak-2025]].
hiv-india-2024-numbers-state-burden.hg:
Agar tum 2000 ke baad paida hue ho, toh HIV shayad tumhe ek purani kahani lagta hoga: red ribbons, purane sarkari ads, ek bimari jiski tension tumhare parents ki generation ko thi.
