Par data kehta hai ki yeh kahin gaya hi nahi. 2024 mein India mein andaazan 25.61 lakh log HIV ke saath jee rahe the. Duniya mein sirf South Africa mein isse zyada log hain [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Upar se, sahi jaankari bhi kam hai. Paanchwe National Family Health Survey (NFHS-5, 2019-21) mein 15-24 saal ki sirf 20.1% young women aur 28.5% young men ko HIV ki comprehensive knowledge thi, yaani yeh basic jaankari ki HIV kaise phailta hai aur use kaise roka ja sakta hai [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Toh chalo, in numbers ko samajhte hain, aur yeh bhi ki inhe padhte waqt dhokha kaise na khayein.

## 25.61 lakh: duniya ki doosri sabse badi HIV ginti

National AIDS Control Organisation (NACO) ke hisaab se 2024 mein 25.61 lakh log HIV ke saath jee rahe the [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Lekin 15-49 saal ke saare adults mein share dekho, toh India ka rate kam hai: sirf 0.20%, jabki global average 0.70% hai [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Dono baatein ek saath sach hain. India jaise bade desh mein chhota sa percentage bhi lakhon log hota hai.

Inmein se bahut se log abhi kisi list mein hi nahi hain. NACO ka estimate hai ki 2024-25 mein HIV wale 83.9% logon ko apna status pata tha [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Yaani lagbhag har chhe mein se ek ko pata hi nahi tha. March 2025 tak 18.60 lakh log antiretroviral therapy (ART) le rahe the, yaani woh dawai jo virus ko control mein rakhti hai. Inmein 17.54 lakh log 800 government ART centres se dawai le rahe the, aur andaazan 1.06 lakh private sector se [[naco-sankalak-2025]].

## 90s ke peak se 0.20% tak: kya gira

India mein adults mein HIV ka rate 1997-98 mein peak par tha, lagbhag 0.58-0.59%. Uske baad yeh girta gaya: 2005 mein lagbhag 0.44%, 2010 mein 0.33%, 2015 mein 0.27%, 2020 mein 0.23% aur 2024 mein 0.20% [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Yeh girawat real hai.

Lekin percentage girne ka matlab yeh nahi ki log kam ho gaye. NACO ke estimate se HIV ke saath jee rahe log 2005 mein lagbhag 32 lakh the aur 2010 mein lagbhag 27 lakh. Lagbhag 2013 se yeh ginti 25-26 lakh par hi atki hai [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Yaani ginti lagbhag wahin rehte hue bhi percentage girta reh sakta hai. Yeh ginti atki kyun hai? Iski ek achhi wajah hai aur ek buri. Achhi wajah: ART ke saath HIV ab lambe samay tak manage hone wali condition hai, aur log lambi, healthy zindagi jee sakte hain [[who-hiv]]. Buri wajah: naye infections utni tezi se nahi gire jitna girna chahiye tha. NACO khud kehta hai ki deaths naye infections se zyada tezi se gir rahi hain, isliye HIV ke saath jee rahe logon ki ginti ab bhi dheere-dheere badh rahi hai [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Isi doosri problem par hamari alag story hai, jo batati hai ki India HIV rokne ka apna target kaise miss kar gaya.

## Paanch states, total ke aadhe se zyada

HIV poore desh mein barabar nahi phaila hai. NACO ke 2024 ke state estimates mein Maharashtra sabse upar hai, uske baad Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Uttar Pradesh aur Tamil Nadu aate hain [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. India mein HIV ke saath jee rahe aadhe se zyada log inhi paanch states mein hain.

| State | HIV ke saath jee rahe log (2024 estimate) |
|---|---|
| Maharashtra | 3,99,023 |
| Andhra Pradesh | 3,10,451 |
| Karnataka | 2,91,348 |
| Uttar Pradesh | 1,95,427 |
| Tamil Nadu | 1,65,971 |
| Telangana | 1,56,961 |

Har state ki kahani ek jaisi nahi hai. South aur West ke bade states mein ginti zyada hai, par aaj wahan naye infections ka rate kam hai [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Isse lagta hai ki wahan bahut se logon ko saalon pehle infection hua tha, aur woh ab iske saath jee rahe hain. Uttar Pradesh is list mein apni bhaari population ki wajah se hai: wahan adult prevalence national average ki sirf aadhi hai [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Naye infections ka map alag dikhta hai. Bihar mein 1,54,296 log HIV ke saath jee rahe hain, par 2024 mein naye infections ka estimate kisi bhi state se zyada Bihar mein tha [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Bihar aur Punjab par hamari alag story isi doosre map ko dekhti hai.

Sabse ooncha rate kahin aur hai, North-East ke chhote states mein. 2024 mein Mizoram mein adult prevalence 2.75% thi, national average ka lagbhag 14 guna [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. 0.20% ka national average aisi jagahon ko chhupa deta hai. North-East par hamari alag story, jahan shared needles aur sex dono se HIV phail raha hai, inhe kareeb se dekhti hai.

## Log batate hain, HIV kaise hua

Jab government programme mein kisi ka test positive aata hai, toh programme record karta hai ki us insaan ke hisaab se infection kaise hua. 2024-25 mein 1,63,306 logon mein naya HIV diagnose hua. Inmein se 73.7% ne heterosexual sex bataya: 32.1% ne casual partners, 26.5% ne regular partners aur 15.1% ne commercial partners (paise ke badle sex) ki baat kahi [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. 11.5% ne bataya ki unhone kisi aur ki needle ya syringe use ki thi, 5.4% ne homosexual ya bisexual sex bataya, 3.5% mein infection maa se bachche mein aaya, aur 1.2% mein infected khoon se. 4.7% ne koi route nahi bataya.

Ab 26.5% par dhyaan do. Naye diagnose hue har chaar mein se ek se zyada logon ne regular partner ko route bataya. "Mera toh ek hi partner hai" ka matlab "main safe hoon" nahi hota, jab tak tum dono ne test na karaya ho.

Yeh bhi yaad rakho ki yeh logon ke apne jawab hain, jo diagnosis ke waqt diye gaye. Stigma ki wajah se log mardon ke beech sex aur drug use ki baat kam bata sakte hain, isliye asal mein yeh routes record se bade ho sakte hain. Needle ka hissa tezi se badha hai: 2017-18 mein yeh naye diagnoses ke 3% se bhi kam tha, aur 2023-24 mein 12.5% [[naco-sankalak-2025]].

## Modelled estimate kaise padhein

Bade national figures, yaani HIV ke saath jee rahe log, naye infections aur deaths, headcount nahi hain. India mein har adult ka test nahi hota; yeh numbers ek statistical model se nikalte hain, diagnose hue logon ki ginti se nahi. Teen rules yaad rakho:

1. **Range dekho.** 25.61 lakh ka figure asal mein 21.89 lakh se 30.67 lakh ke beech kahin bhi ho sakta hai [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Yaani asli number kuch lakh kam ya zyada ho sakta hai.
2. **Alag-alag rounds ko compare mat karo.** Har naye round mein puraane saalon ke numbers bhi dobara nikaale jaate hain. NACO ki pichhli report mein unhi saalon ke figures thode alag the, isliye purani report ka number nayi report se milaoge toh aisi badhat ya girawat dikh sakti hai jo kabhi hui hi nahi.
3. **Check karo ki gina kya ja raha hai.** HIV ke saath jee rahe log, naye infections aur deaths, teeno alag chaal chalte hain. 2010 se 2024 ke beech AIDS se judi deaths 81.4% gireen, par naye infections sirf 48.7% [[naco-sankalak-2025]].

Aakhri baat darr ki nahi hai. HIV ka treatment hai, aur jo insaan sahi treatment le raha hai aur jiska viral load undetectable hai, usse sex ke zariye HIV nahi phailta [[who-hiv]]. Asli khatra hai, pata na hona. Agar tumne kabhi bina condom sex kiya hai ya injecting equipment kisi aur ke saath share kiya hai, toh test hi jaanne ka akela tareeka hai, aur government ART centres par treatment free hai [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. NACO ki toll-free helpline 1097 [[naco]] par din-raat, 16 languages mein, confidential counselling milti hai [[naco-sankalak-2025]].

hiv-knowledge-young-indians-nfhs5.en:
Put ten young Indian women in a room, any ten between 15 and 24. Check five basic points about HIV: only how the virus spreads and how it does not. By the measure of India's national health survey, two of the ten will get all five right.

The fifth National Family Health Survey (NFHS-5), carried out in 2019-21, found that only 20.1% of young women and 28.5% of young men aged 15-24 had what it calls comprehensive knowledge of HIV. In NFHS-4, in 2015-16, the figures were 22% and 32% [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. On HIV, young Indians knew slightly less than people their age had known five years earlier.

## What "comprehensive knowledge" means

The phrase sounds demanding. It is not. NFHS counts a person as having comprehensive knowledge if they know three things and reject two. The three: condoms reduce the risk of HIV, having one faithful, uninfected partner reduces it, and a healthy-looking person can have HIV. The two are common misconceptions about how it spreads [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. All five must be right, which makes the measure strict. It does not make it advanced.

The misconceptions are where people fall. Among women aged 15-49, 46% did not know that HIV cannot be transmitted by mosquito bites, and 55% did not know it cannot spread by sharing food with a person who has AIDS. Men did better, not well: 64% knew the truth about mosquitoes and 59% about food [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

These beliefs are not harmless. Someone who thinks HIV travels on a shared plate may refuse to eat with a relative who has it. Ignorance about transmission turns into a rule about who is kept out of the kitchen.

## A small slide nobody noticed: NFHS-4 to NFHS-5

Among young women the share went from 22% to 20%; among young men, from 32% to 29%. The survey report itself calls the fall among women marginal, and for all adults aged 15-49 the figures, 22% of women and 31% of men, barely moved [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Two or three points in a sample survey is a small change.

But "no change" is the finding. Five years passed, a full school generation went from Class 8 to college, and the number did not rise. Prevention is where India is behind: an estimated 64,470 people were newly infected with HIV in 2024, a fall of 48.7% from 2010 against a national programme target of 80% by 2025-26 [[naco-sankalak-2025]].

School is where this was meant to be taught. After a backlash in 2007, somewhere between six and 12 states, depending on who counted, banned or refused to run the national adolescence education programme [[reprodhealth-plesons-jharkhand-cse-2020]]. Yet the UN's 2018 technical guidance, reviewing the evidence, says sexuality education does not increase sexual activity, risk-taking or HIV infection rates [[unesco-itgse-2018]].

## Schooling, wealth and caste: the knowledge gap

Among young women aged 15-24, NFHS-5 found [[nfhs5-india-2021]]:

| Group | Comprehensive knowledge of HIV |
|---|---|
| No schooling | 8.7% |
| 12 or more years of school | 28.0% |
| Poorest fifth of households | 11.6% |
| Richest fifth of households | 29.2% |
| Scheduled Caste | 18.2% |
| All young women | 20.1% |

A young woman who stayed in school for 12 years is more than three times as likely to know the basics as one who never went. Caste, schooling and wealth overlap, so these are not separate effects.

Twelve years in a classroom, or a home in the richest fifth, and still fewer than three in ten young women pass. Privilege buys a better score, not a good one. Schooling alone is clearly not teaching it.

Knowing that condoms work is also different from being able to get one. Only 54.4% of young women knew where to obtain a condom, against 87.3% of young men [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

## Bihar 10%, Mizoram 69%: the state divide

Only 10% of young women in Bihar, and 12% in Uttar Pradesh and Tripura, had comprehensive knowledge of HIV, against 69% in Mizoram. Among young men the range ran from 14% in West Bengal and Meghalaya to 73% in Goa [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Small-state estimates are less precise, but this gap is too wide to be noise.

Mizoram also has India's highest adult HIV prevalence, 2.75% in 2024 [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. The survey does not explain the gap. One plausible reading: where people have watched HIV arrive in their own neighbourhoods, it gets talked about, so knowledge follows the epidemic instead of arriving before it.

Bihar is the warning. The state at the bottom of the young women's table had India's highest estimated number of new HIV infections in 2024, at 7,694 [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. The two figures come from different years and methods, and Bihar is a very large state. Together they still describe a huge young population meeting a virus it was never taught about.

## The HIV facts to know by heart

Here are the answers [[who-hiv]]:

- **How it spreads.** Through specific body fluids: blood, semen, vaginal and rectal fluids, and breast milk. In practice: sex without a condom, shared needles, unscreened blood, and from mother to baby without treatment.
- **How it does not.** Not through mosquito bites, shared food or utensils, hugging, handshakes, coughing or toilets. Living, eating and studying with a person who has HIV is safe.
- **You cannot see it.** A person can look and feel healthy for years. Only a test tells.
- **Condoms work.** Used correctly every time, they greatly reduce the risk, though not to zero [[who-sti]].
- **There is an emergency medicine.** PEP can prevent infection after an exposure if it is started as soon as possible, no later than 72 hours, and taken for 28 days [[who-pep]].
- **Treatment changes everything.** On daily treatment, people with HIV live long, healthy lives, and a person whose virus is undetectable does not pass it on through sex [[who-hiv]].

To find a testing centre, call NACO's helpline, 1097: it answers confidentially at any hour, in 16 languages [[naco-sankalak-2025]].

Then do what the survey did. Ask five people this week how HIV spreads: a sibling, a friend, a parent. Correct the wrong answers without mocking anyone. That is how a number like 20.1% moves.
hiv-knowledge-young-indians-nfhs5.hg:
Das young Indian women ko ek kamre mein bithao, 15 se 24 saal ke beech ki koi bhi das. HIV ke paanch basic points check karo: bas itna ki virus kaise phailta hai aur kaise nahi. India ke national health survey ke paimane se, das mein se do ke paanchon sahi honge.

Paanchwe National Family Health Survey (NFHS-5) ne, jo 2019-21 mein hua, paaya ki 15-24 saal ki sirf 20.1% young women aur 28.5% young men ke paas woh thi jise survey HIV ki comprehensive knowledge kehta hai. NFHS-4 mein, 2015-16 mein, yeh figures 22% aur 32% the [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. HIV ke maamle mein young Indians, paanch saal pehle ke apni umar ke logon se thoda kam jaante the.

## "Comprehensive knowledge" ka matlab kya hai

Yeh phrase bhaari lagta hai. Hai nahi. NFHS kisi insaan ko comprehensive knowledge wala tab ginta hai jab use teen baatein pata hon aur woh do baatein reject kare. Teen baatein: condoms HIV ka risk kam karte hain, ek faithful, uninfected partner hone se risk kam hota hai, aur healthy dikhne wale insaan ko bhi HIV ho sakta hai. Do baatein HIV ke phailne ke baare mein common misconceptions hain [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Paanchon sahi hone chahiye, isliye yeh measure strict hai. Par isse yeh advanced nahi ho jaata.

Log misconceptions par hi girte hain. 15-49 saal ki women mein 46% ko nahi pata tha ki HIV machhar ke kaatne se transmit nahi ho sakta, aur 55% ko nahi pata tha ki yeh AIDS wale insaan ke saath khaana share karne se nahi phailta. Men ka haal behtar tha, par achha nahi: 64% ko machhar wali baat ka sach pata tha aur 59% ko khaane wali baat ka [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Yeh beliefs harmless nahi hain. Jo insaan sochta hai ki HIV ek shared plate se aa sakta hai, woh us rishtedaar ke saath khaana khane se mana kar sakta hai jise HIV hai. Transmission ke baare mein na jaanna ek rule ban jaata hai ki kise kitchen se bahar rakha jayega.

## Ek chhoti si girawat jo kisi ne notice nahi ki: NFHS-4 se NFHS-5

Young women mein share 22% se 20% hua; young men mein 32% se 29%. Survey report khud women wali girawat ko marginal kehti hai, aur 15-49 saal ke sabhi adults ke figures, 22% women aur 31% men, lagbhag wahin ke wahin rahe [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Sample survey mein do-teen points ka farak chhota change hai.

Lekin "koi change nahi" hi asli finding hai. Paanch saal guzre, school ki ek poori generation Class 8 se college pahunch gayi, aur number upar nahi gaya. Prevention mein hi India peeche hai: 2024 mein estimated 64,470 log HIV se newly infected hue, yaani 2010 se 48.7% ki girawat, jabki national programme ka target 2025-26 tak 80% ka tha [[naco-sankalak-2025]].

Yeh sab school mein sikhaya jaana tha. 2007 ke backlash ke baad, ginne wale ke hisaab se chhe se 12 states ne national adolescence education programme ko ban kar diya ya chalane se mana kar diya [[reprodhealth-plesons-jharkhand-cse-2020]]. Jabki UN ki 2018 ki technical guidance, evidence review karke, kehti hai ki sexuality education se sexual activity, risk-taking ya HIV infection rates nahi badhte [[unesco-itgse-2018]].

## Schooling, paisa aur caste: knowledge gap

15-24 saal ki young women mein NFHS-5 ne yeh paaya [[nfhs5-india-2021]]:

| Group | HIV ki comprehensive knowledge |
|---|---|
| Kabhi school nahi gayi | 8.7% |
| 12 ya zyada saal ki schooling | 28.0% |
| Sabse gareeb paanchwa hissa (households) | 11.6% |
| Sabse ameer paanchwa hissa (households) | 29.2% |
| Scheduled Caste | 18.2% |
| Sabhi young women | 20.1% |

Jo young woman 12 saal school mein rahi, uske basics jaanne ke chances us young woman se teen guna se zyada hain jo kabhi school nahi gayi. Caste, schooling aur paisa aapas mein overlap karte hain, toh yeh alag-alag effects nahi hain.

Classroom mein baarah saal, ya sabse ameer paanchwe hisse ka ghar, aur phir bhi das mein se teen se kam young women pass hoti hain. Privilege se score behtar hota hai, achha nahi. Saaf hai ki sirf schooling yeh nahi sikha rahi.

Yeh jaanna ki condoms kaam karte hain, aur condom haasil kar paana, do alag baatein hain. Sirf 54.4% young women ko pata tha ki condom kahan se milta hai, jabki young men mein 87.3% ko [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

## Bihar 10%, Mizoram 69%: states ka divide

Bihar mein sirf 10% young women ko, aur Uttar Pradesh aur Tripura mein 12% ko, HIV ki comprehensive knowledge thi, jabki Mizoram mein 69% ko. Young men mein range West Bengal aur Meghalaya ke 14% se Goa ke 73% tak thi [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Chhote states ke estimates kam precise hote hain, par yeh gap itna bada hai ki ise noise nahi keh sakte.

Mizoram mein India ka sabse zyada adult HIV prevalence bhi hai, 2024 mein 2.75% [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Survey is gap ki wajah nahi batata. Ek mumkin reading yeh hai: jahan logon ne HIV ko apne hi mohalle mein aate dekha hai, wahan uske baare mein baat hoti hai, isliye knowledge epidemic ke peeche-peeche aati hai, usse pehle nahi.

Bihar warning hai. Jo state young women ki table mein sabse neeche hai, wahin 2024 mein India ke sabse zyada estimated new HIV infections the: 7,694 [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Yeh dono figures alag saalon aur alag methods se aate hain, aur Bihar bahut bada state hai. Phir bhi saath mein yeh ek bahut badi young population dikhate hain, jo aise virus se mil rahi hai jiske baare mein use kabhi sikhaya hi nahi gaya.

## HIV ke woh facts jo zubaani yaad hone chahiye

Yeh rahe jawab [[who-hiv]]:

- **Kaise phailta hai.** Specific body fluids se: blood, semen, vaginal aur rectal fluids, aur breast milk. Practically: bina condom ke sex, shared needles, unscreened blood, aur bina treatment ke maa se bachche ko.
- **Kaise nahi phailta.** Machhar ke kaatne se nahi, khaana ya bartan share karne se nahi, gale lagne, haath milane, khaansne ya toilet se nahi. HIV wale insaan ke saath rehna, khaana aur padhna safe hai.
- **Yeh dikhta nahi.** Insaan saalon tak healthy dikh sakta hai aur healthy feel kar sakta hai. Sirf test batata hai.
- **Condoms kaam karte hain.** Har baar sahi tarah use karne par yeh risk bahut kam kar dete hain, par zero nahi [[who-sti]].
- **Ek emergency medicine hai.** PEP exposure ke baad infection rok sakta hai, agar ise jitna jaldi ho sake, 72 ghante se pehle, start kiya jaye aur 28 din liya jaye [[who-pep]].
- **Treatment sab badal deta hai.** Roz ke treatment par HIV wale log lambi, healthy life jeete hain, aur jis insaan ka virus undetectable hai, woh sex ke through ise pass nahi karta [[who-hiv]].

Testing centre dhoondhne ke liye NACO ki helpline 1097 par call karo: yeh kisi bhi waqt, 16 languages mein, confidential jawab deti hai [[naco-sankalak-2025]].

Phir wahi karo jo survey ne kiya. Is hafte paanch logon se poocho ki HIV kaise phailta hai: bhai-behen, dost, mummy-papa. Galat jawab bina mazaak udaye theek karo. 20.1% jaisa number aise hi hilta hai.

hiv-pep-72-hour-window-explained.en:
Consider three people on three different nights. They are hypothetical, but ordinary. A nurse in Lucknow pricks her finger on a used needle at the end of a double shift. A college student in Pune feels a condom tear with a new partner. A 19-year-old was sexually assaulted on Saturday and has told no one. All three face the same deadline. The medicine that can stop HIV from taking hold has to be started within 72 hours, and the sooner the better [[who-pep]].

That medicine is called PEP. National surveys do not measure how many people know about it, but they show that even a full grasp of how HIV spreads is uncommon. In the fifth National Family Health Survey (2019-21), only 20.1% of young women and 28.5% of young men aged 15-24 had what the survey calls comprehensive knowledge of HIV; among young women who had never been to school, it was 8.7% [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. That measure covers only the basics, such as condoms. PEP is not part of it.

## What PEP is, and why the clock matters

PEP stands for post-exposure prophylaxis: a short course of HIV medicines taken after a possible exposure, to stop the virus from settling into the body. It needs an urgent assessment by a clinician. It must start as soon as possible and no later than 72 hours after the exposure, and it is taken every day for 28 days [[who-pep]].

Think of the 72 hours as a closing door. Early on, the virus has not yet established itself, and medicine can still block it. After 72 hours, PEP is no longer recommended. What is left is testing and, if the virus has taken hold, treatment for life, because HIV has no cure [[who-hiv]]. So if something happened in the last 72 hours, do not wait to see whether you feel ill. Go to a hospital now.

An estimated 64,470 people in India were newly infected with HIV in 2024 [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. That is a 48.7% fall from about 1.25 lakh in 2010: real progress, but India's own national AIDS programme had aimed for an 80% cut by 2025-26 [[naco-sankalak-2025]].

## Who needs it

PEP is for a specific, recent event, not for general worry. Ask for it urgently if, in the last 72 hours:

- a condom broke or slipped, or there was no condom, with a partner whose HIV status you do not know, or who has HIV and is not on effective treatment;
- you shared needles or syringes;
- you are a health or sanitation worker and were pricked by a used needle or splashed with blood;
- you were sexually assaulted, whatever your gender.

Of 1,63,306 people newly diagnosed with HIV in 2024-25, nearly 74% reported heterosexual sex, and 26.5% of the total named a regular partner; 11.5% reported shared needles or syringes [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. HIV does not only come from strangers: a regular partner is one of the most common routes.

PEP is not needed after hugging, kissing, or sharing food or water: HIV does not spread through ordinary day-to-day contact [[who-hiv]]. And if your partner has HIV, is on treatment and has an undetectable viral load, HIV is not passed on through sex [[who-hiv]]. Tell the doctor exactly what happened. Judging the risk is their job, not yours.

## 28 days of medicine and follow-up tests

Expect an HIV test before the first dose. PEP is prevention, not treatment, so the doctor needs to know you did not already have HIV. Then comes a combination of medicines, taken every day for 28 days [[who-pep]].

If the medicine makes you feel unwell, do not stop on your own: a course abandoned halfway can leave you unprotected, so call the doctor instead. Afterwards, expect follow-up HIV tests, and use condoms until those results are clear.

PEP is not a guarantee, and it is not a plan. If you keep needing it, ask the doctor about PrEP.

## PEP, PrEP and the emergency pill are three different things

| | Prevents | When | How long |
|---|---|---|---|
| PEP | HIV | After an exposure, within 72 hours | 28 days |
| PrEP | HIV | Before exposure, for people at ongoing risk | As long as the risk lasts |
| Emergency contraceptive pill | Pregnancy | Up to five days after sex, sooner is better | Usually a single dose |

PrEP is a medicine an HIV-negative person takes, on a clinician's prescription, to prevent HIV [[who-hiv]]. The emergency contraceptive pill prevents pregnancy by delaying ovulation; it is not an abortion, and it gives no protection against HIV or any other infection [[who-ec]]. After a sexual assault, a survivor may need PEP and emergency contraception at the same time.

## Where to ask, and the NACO helpline 1097

Go to the emergency (casualty) ward of the nearest government hospital and say the words: "I need HIV PEP." If you do not know where to go, call NACO's toll-free helpline 1097. It gives confidential counselling round the clock in 16 languages, and it took 4,32,474 calls in 2024-25 [[naco-sankalak-2025]].

After a rape, or the sexual assault of a child, money cannot be a reason for delay. Section 397 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) obliges every hospital, government or private, to give these survivors immediate first aid or medical treatment free of cost, and to inform the police [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. The duty is to treat at once, not after an FIR. What happens in the examination room, and what a survivor can refuse there, is explained in our guide to the medical exam after rape. For PEP, remember one thing: the medicine is for your body, whatever you decide about the case.

There is one honest gap. The BNS defines rape as a man assaulting a woman and has no equivalent of the old Section 377, so an adult man or transgender person who is sexually assaulted is not expressly covered by that free-treatment rule [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Their 72 hours run just as fast. Go anyway, and ask for PEP by name. This is general information, not legal advice.
hiv-pep-72-hour-window-explained.hg:
Socho, teen log hain aur teen alag raatein. Ye examples hypothetical hain, par bilkul aam hain. Lucknow ki ek nurse ki double shift khatam hone wali hai, tabhi uski ungli mein ek used needle chubh jaati hai. Pune ke ek college student ka condom ek naye partner ke saath phat jaata hai. Aur ek 19 saal ke young insaan ke saath Saturday ko sexual assault hua hai, aur usne abhi tak kisi ko nahi bataya. Teeno ke saamne ek hi deadline hai. Jo dawa HIV ko body mein basne se rok sakti hai, use 72 ghante ke andar shuru karna zaroori hai, aur jitni jaldi utna better [[who-pep]].

Is dawa ka naam hai PEP. National surveys yeh nahi naapte ki kitne log iske baare mein jaante hain, lekin yeh zaroor dikhate hain ki HIV kaise phailta hai, iski poori samajh bhi kam logon ke paas hai. Paanchve National Family Health Survey (NFHS-5, 2019-21) mein 15-24 saal ki sirf 20.1% ladkiyon aur 28.5% ladkon ko HIV ki wo "comprehensive knowledge" thi jo survey check karta hai. Jo ladkiyan kabhi school nahi gayi, unmein ye sirf 8.7% tha [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Aur is measure mein sirf basics aate hain, jaise condoms. PEP iska hissa hi nahi hai.

## PEP kya hai, aur ghadi kyun matter karti hai

PEP ka full form hai post-exposure prophylaxis: HIV medicines ka ek chhota course, jo possible exposure ke baad liya jaata hai, taaki virus body mein jagah na bana paaye. Iske liye doctor ka turant assessment zaroori hai. Dawa jitni jaldi ho sake shuru honi chahiye, exposure ke 72 ghante se late nahi. Phir ye 28 din tak roz leni hoti hai [[who-pep]].

72 ghanton ko ek dheere-dheere band hote darwaaze ki tarah socho. Shuru mein virus body mein pakki jagah nahi bana paata, aur dawa use rok sakti hai. 72 ghante ke baad PEP recommend nahi ki jaati. Phir bas testing bachti hai, aur agar virus bas gaya, toh zindagi bhar ka treatment, kyunki HIV ka koi cure nahi hai [[who-hiv]]. Isliye agar pichhle 72 ghanton mein kuch hua hai, toh tabiyat bigadne ka wait mat karo. Abhi hospital jao.

Estimate hai ki 2024 mein India mein 64,470 logon ko naya HIV infection hua [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. 2010 mein ye number lagbhag 1.25 lakh tha, yaani 48.7% ki girawat. Ye real progress hai, lekin India ke apne national AIDS programme ne 2025-26 tak 80% kami ka target rakha tha [[naco-sankalak-2025]].

## Kisko PEP chahiye

PEP kisi specific, recent incident ke baad ke liye hai, general tension ke liye nahi. Agar pichhle 72 ghanton mein inmein se kuch hua hai, toh turant PEP maango:

- condom phat gaya ya slip ho gaya, ya condom tha hi nahi, aur partner ka HIV status tumhe nahi pata, ya partner ko HIV hai aur uska treatment theek se nahi chal raha;
- tumne kisi ke saath needle ya syringe share ki;
- tum health worker ya sanitation worker ho, aur tumhe used needle chubhi ya khoon ke chheente pade;
- tumhare saath sexual assault hua, chahe tumhara gender kuch bhi ho.

2024-25 mein 1,63,306 logon mein naya HIV diagnose hua. Inmein se lagbhag 74% ne heterosexual sex (aadmi-aurat ke beech sex) ko wajah bataya, aur total mein se 26.5% ne regular partner ka zikr kiya; 11.5% ne needle ya syringe share karne ki baat kahi [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Matlab HIV sirf strangers se nahi aata: regular partner sabse common routes mein se ek hai.

Gale milne, kiss karne, ya khana-paani share karne ke baad PEP ki zaroorat nahi hai: roz ke normal contact se HIV nahi phailta [[who-hiv]]. Aur agar tumhare partner ko HIV hai, uska treatment chal raha hai aur uska viral load undetectable hai, toh sex se HIV aage nahi jaata [[who-hiv]]. Doctor ko saaf-saaf batao ki kya hua. Risk kitna hai, ye judge karna unka kaam hai, tumhara nahi.

## 28 din ki dawa aur follow-up tests

Pehli dose se pehle tumhara HIV test hoga. PEP prevention hai, treatment nahi, isliye doctor ko confirm karna hota hai ki tumhe pehle se HIV nahi hai. Phir kuch medicines ka combination milta hai, jo 28 din tak roz leni hoti hain [[who-pep]].

Agar dawa se tabiyat kharab lage, toh apne mann se band mat karna: beech mein chhoda hua course tumhe bina protection ke chhod sakta hai, isliye doctor ko call karo. Course ke baad follow-up HIV tests honge, aur results clear aane tak condom use karo.

PEP koi guarantee nahi hai, aur ye koi plan bhi nahi hai. Agar tumhe baar-baar iski zaroorat pad rahi hai, toh doctor se PrEP ke baare mein pucho.

## PEP, PrEP aur emergency pill: teeno alag cheezein hain

| | Kis cheez se bachati hai | Kab | Kitne din |
|---|---|---|---|
| PEP | HIV | Exposure ke baad, 72 ghante ke andar | 28 din |
| PrEP | HIV | Exposure se pehle, jinhe lagaataar risk hai | Jab tak risk bana rahe |
| Emergency contraceptive pill | Pregnancy | Sex ke baad paanch din tak, jitni jaldi utna better | Usually ek hi dose |

PrEP ek dawa hai jo HIV-negative insaan doctor ke prescription pe leta hai, taaki use HIV na ho [[who-hiv]]. Emergency contraceptive pill ovulation ko delay karke pregnancy rokti hai; ye abortion nahi hai, aur HIV ya kisi aur infection se koi protection nahi deti [[who-ec]]. Sexual assault ke baad survivor ko PEP aur emergency contraception, dono ki ek saath zaroorat ho sakti hai.

## Kahan poochein, aur NACO helpline 1097

Sabse paas ke government hospital ke emergency (casualty) ward mein jao aur seedha bolo: "Mujhe HIV PEP chahiye." Agar nahi pata kahan jaana hai, toh NACO ki toll-free helpline 1097 pe call karo. Yahan din-raat, 16 languages mein, confidential counselling milti hai, aur 2024-25 mein ispe 4,32,474 calls aayi [[naco-sankalak-2025]].

Rape ke baad, ya kisi bachche ke saath sexual assault ke baad, paisa delay ki wajah nahi ban sakta. Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) ka Section 397 kehta hai ki har hospital, government ho ya private, aise survivors ko turant aur free first aid ya ilaaj dega, aur police ko inform karega [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Ilaaj turant karna hai, FIR ke baad nahi. Examination room mein kya hota hai, aur survivor wahan kin cheezon ke liye mana kar sakte hain, ye hamari "rape ke baad medical exam" wali guide mein explain kiya gaya hai. PEP ke liye bas ek baat yaad rakho: ye dawa tumhari body ke liye hai, case ke baare mein tum jo bhi decide karo.

Ek honest gap bhi hai. Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) mein rape ka matlab hai aadmi ka aurat pe assault, aur purane Section 377 jaisa koi provision ismein nahi hai. Isliye agar kisi adult aadmi ya transgender insaan ke saath sexual assault ho, toh free treatment wale is rule mein unka saaf taur par zikr nahi hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Par unke 72 ghante bhi utni hi tezi se beette hain. Phir bhi hospital jao, aur PEP naam leke maango. Ye general information hai, legal advice nahi.

hiv-prep-prevention-pill-questions.en:
Consider two people, both hypothetical. A 23-year-old man in Delhi who has sex with men, uses condoms mostly but not always, and has needed emergency PEP twice this year. A 31-year-old woman in Indore whose husband has just been diagnosed with HIV and started treatment; she tested negative and wants to stay that way. A pill taken before any exposure could protect them both. It is called PrEP, and in a country where an estimated 64,470 people were newly infected with HIV in 2024 [[naco-sankalak-2025]], it deserves to be far better known.

## What is PrEP, and how well does it work?

PrEP stands for pre-exposure prophylaxis. It is HIV medicine that an HIV-negative person takes, on a clinician's prescription, to prevent HIV. It can be taken as a daily pill, and WHO also lists a vaginal ring and long-acting injections [[who-hiv]].

Taken as prescribed, it gives strong protection. Protection drops when doses are missed, because there may not be enough medicine in the body when exposure happens. It is not a vaccine: protection lasts only while you keep taking it. And it is not treatment: it is for people who do not have HIV.

Do not confuse it with PEP. PEP is the emergency course after a possible exposure: it must start within 72 hours and lasts 28 days [[who-pep]]. PEP is the emergency response; PrEP is protection you put on in advance, like a seatbelt.

## Who should ask a doctor about PrEP?

Anyone whose risk of HIV is real and ongoing. That is a judgment to make with a doctor, not a label. In India the risk is concentrated. In 2024, HIV prevalence was 0.20% among all adults, but 2.12% among men who have sex with men, 2.84% among hijra and transgender people, 1.13% among female sex workers and 8.79% among people who inject drugs [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. For men who have sex with men, that is more than ten times the adult average; for people who inject drugs, more than 40 times.

These figures come from people the programme reaches, and hidden groups may differ. Shame also blurs the picture. Of 1,63,306 people newly diagnosed with HIV in 2024-25, only 5.4% named homosexual or bisexual sex as the route, and 11.5% named shared needles or syringes [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Stigma pushes people to under-report both, even to a counsellor.

A quieter group is people whose partner has HIV. A partner whose treatment keeps the virus undetectable does not pass HIV on through sex [[who-hiv]]. But a partner who has just started treatment may not be undetectable yet, and in 2024-25 only 83.9% of people living with HIV in India even knew their status [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Until tests show a partner's viral load is undetectable, or whenever you cannot be sure of a partner's status, PrEP can bridge the gap.

Ask about it, too, if you keep needing PEP, if you have recently had an STI, or if your partner injects drugs.

## PrEP, PEP or condoms: which protects against what?

| | HIV | Other STIs | Pregnancy |
|---|---|---|---|
| PrEP | Yes, when taken as prescribed | No | No |
| PEP | Yes, after one exposure, if started within 72 hours | No | No |
| Condoms | Greatly reduce the risk | Greatly reduce the risk | Yes, though not perfectly |

PrEP does nothing against syphilis, gonorrhoea or chlamydia. At government STI clinics in 2024-25, 4.12% of syphilis screenings among transgender clients and 1.54% among men were reactive, against 0.48% among women [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Many STIs cause no symptoms at all, and only testing tells [[who-sti]]. That is why regular STI checks belong with PrEP, and why condoms still matter: they greatly reduce the risk, though not to zero [[who-sti]].

## What tests come with it, and what if the pills disagree with me?

Before the first pill, you need an HIV test, and it must be negative: PrEP is only for people who do not have HIV [[who-hiv]]. If you already have HIV, you need full treatment instead. Doctors may also check how well your kidneys work.

After that, expect regular HIV and STI tests while you stay on PrEP. If the pills disagree with you, tell the doctor rather than skipping doses.

Staying on it is the hard part. Tie the pill to a daily habit and set a phone alarm. If your risk changes, ask the doctor how to stop safely. Never buy PrEP without a prescription or borrow a friend's pills: the tests are what make it safe.

## How do I bring it up with a doctor without shame?

You do not owe anyone your life story. One sentence is enough: "I'd like to know if PrEP is right for me." Then answer the doctor's questions about partners, condoms and needles honestly. The doctor needs facts, not a confession.

The law gives you some protection. Under India's HIV and AIDS (Prevention and Control) Act, 2017, no HIV test may be done without your informed consent, and no one can force you to disclose your HIV status except by court order (Sections 5 and 8) [[naco-hiv-aids-act-2017-gazette]]; our HIV testing guide covers these rights. Section 3 bars discrimination in healthcare against people living with HIV and those who live with them, which covers an HIV-negative partner who lives with someone with HIV [[naco-hiv-aids-act-2017-gazette]]. And since the Supreme Court's 2018 judgment in Navtej Singh Johar, consensual sex between adults of the same sex is not a crime [[scobserver-navtej-johar-2018]]. Being gay, bisexual or trans is not something to confess.

Where to ask: the HIV or STI services of a government hospital (in 2025 India had 1,127 Suraksha Clinics for STIs at district hospitals and medical colleges [[naco-sankalak-2025]]), a community organisation that works with your group, or a private doctor. Ask directly whether they prescribe PrEP, and if not, who does. For confidential guidance, call NACO's helpline 1097 [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. If a clinic breaks the consent or confidentiality rules above, or you live with someone who has HIV and are discriminated against, you can complain to your state's HIV Ombudsman; 34 States and UTs had one in March 2025 [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. This is general information, not legal advice.
hiv-prep-prevention-pill-questions.hg:
Socho, do log hain, dono hypothetical. Delhi ka ek 23 saal ka ladka jo men ke saath sex karta hai, zyada tar condom use karta hai par hamesha nahi, aur is saal do baar emergency PEP le chuka hai. Aur Indore ki ek 31 saal ki aurat, jiske pati ko abhi-abhi HIV diagnose hua hai aur unka treatment shuru hua hai; uska apna test negative aaya hai aur wo negative hi rehna chahti hai. Exposure se pehle li gayi ek goli in dono ko bacha sakti hai. Iska naam hai PrEP. Jis desh mein 2024 mein estimated 64,470 logon ko naya HIV infection hua [[naco-sankalak-2025]], wahan iske baare mein kahin zyada logon ko pata hona chahiye.

## PrEP kya hai, aur ye kitna kaam karti hai?

PrEP ka full form hai pre-exposure prophylaxis. Ye HIV ki dawa hai jo HIV-negative insaan doctor ke prescription pe leta hai, taaki use HIV na ho. Ise roz ki goli ki tarah liya ja sakta hai, aur WHO ek vaginal ring aur long-acting injections ko bhi list karta hai [[who-hiv]].

Prescribe kiye tareeke se li jaaye toh ye strong protection deti hai. Doses miss hone par protection ghat jaata hai, kyunki exposure ke waqt body mein kaafi dawa shayad na ho. Ye vaccine nahi hai: protection tabhi tak hai jab tak tum goli lete raho. Aur ye treatment bhi nahi hai: ye unke liye hai jinhe HIV nahi hai.

Isko PEP se confuse mat karna. PEP possible exposure ke baad ka emergency course hai: 72 ghante ke andar shuru hona chahiye aur 28 din chalta hai [[who-pep]]. PEP emergency response hai; PrEP woh protection hai jo pehle se pehna jaata hai, seatbelt ki tarah.

## Kisko doctor se PrEP ke baare mein poochna chahiye?

Har us insaan ko jiska HIV risk real hai aur baar-baar hai. Ye faisla doctor ke saath milke hota hai; ye koi label nahi hai. India mein risk kuch groups mein concentrated hai. 2024 mein sabhi adults mein HIV prevalence 0.20% thi, lekin men who have sex with men mein 2.12%, hijra aur transgender logon mein 2.84%, female sex workers mein 1.13% aur inject karke drugs lene walon mein 8.79% [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Matlab men who have sex with men mein ye adult average se das guna se bhi zyada hai; inject karke drugs lene walon mein 40 guna se bhi zyada.

Ye figures un logon ke hain jin tak programme pahunchta hai; jo groups chhupe hue hain, unki picture alag ho sakti hai. Sharam bhi picture blur karti hai. 2024-25 mein 1,63,306 logon mein naya HIV diagnose hua, aur unmein se sirf 5.4% ne homosexual ya bisexual sex ko route bataya, aur 11.5% ne needle ya syringe share karne ko [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Stigma ki wajah se log ye dono baatein kam batate hain, counsellor ke saamne bhi.

Ek quiet group aur hai: wo log jinke partner ko HIV hai. Jis partner ka treatment virus ko undetectable rakhta hai, usse sex ke through HIV nahi phailta [[who-hiv]]. Lekin jisne abhi-abhi treatment shuru kiya hai, uska virus shayad abhi undetectable na hua ho, aur 2024-25 mein India mein HIV ke saath jee rahe sirf 83.9% logon ko apna status pata tha [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Jab tak tests yeh na dikhayein ki partner ka viral load undetectable hai, ya jab bhi tum partner ke status ko lekar sure na ho, PrEP is gap ko bhar sakti hai.

Iske baare mein tab bhi pucho jab tumhe baar-baar PEP ki zaroorat pad rahi ho, haal hi mein koi STI hua ho, ya tumhara partner inject karke drugs leta ho.

## PrEP, PEP ya condom: kaun kis cheez se bachata hai?

| | HIV | Doosre STIs | Pregnancy |
|---|---|---|---|
| PrEP | Haan, agar prescribe kiye tareeke se li jaaye | Nahi | Nahi |
| PEP | Haan, ek exposure ke baad, agar 72 ghante ke andar shuru ho | Nahi | Nahi |
| Condom | Risk bahut kam karta hai | Risk bahut kam karta hai | Haan, par perfect nahi |

PrEP syphilis, gonorrhoea ya chlamydia se bilkul nahi bachati. 2024-25 mein government STI clinics mein transgender clients ki syphilis screenings mein se 4.12% aur men ki screenings mein se 1.54% reactive aayi, jabki women mein 0.48% [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Bahut saare STIs mein koi symptom nahi hota; sirf testing se pata chalta hai [[who-sti]]. Isliye PrEP ke saath regular STI checks bhi hone chahiye, aur isliye condoms ab bhi zaroori hain: wo risk bahut kam karte hain, bhale hi poori tarah khatam nahi karte [[who-sti]].

## Iske saath kaunse tests hote hain, aur goli suit na kare toh?

Pehli goli se pehle HIV test hoga, aur uska negative aana zaroori hai: PrEP sirf unke liye hai jinhe HIV nahi hai [[who-hiv]]. Agar tumhe pehle se HIV hai, toh tumhe iski jagah poora treatment chahiye. Doctor shayad kidney ka check bhi karein.

Uske baad, jab tak tum PrEP pe ho, regular HIV aur STI tests honge. Agar goliyan suit na karein, toh doses skip karne ki jagah doctor ko batao.

Sabse mushkil kaam hai ise roz lete rehna. Goli ko kisi daily habit se jod lo aur phone pe alarm laga lo. Agar tumhara risk badal jaaye, toh doctor se pucho ki sahi tareeke se kaise band karein. Bina prescription ke PrEP kabhi mat khareedo aur kisi dost ki goliyan mat lo: tests hi ise safe banate hain.

## Bina sharam ke doctor se baat kaise shuru karein?

Tumhe kisi ko apni poori life story nahi sunani. Ek line kaafi hai: "Mujhe jaanna hai ki kya PrEP mere liye sahi hai." Phir partners, condoms aur needles ke baare mein doctor ke sawaalon ka sach-sach jawab do. Doctor ko facts chahiye, koi confession nahi.

Law tumhe kuch protection deta hai. India ke HIV and AIDS (Prevention and Control) Act, 2017 ke under, tumhari informed consent ke bina HIV test nahi ho sakta, aur court order ke bina koi tumhe apna HIV status batane pe majboor nahi kar sakta (Sections 5 aur 8) [[naco-hiv-aids-act-2017-gazette]]; in rights ki poori detail hamari HIV testing guide mein hai. Section 3 healthcare mein discrimination pe rok lagata hai, HIV ke saath jee rahe logon ke against bhi aur unke saath rehne walon ke against bhi; yaani jo HIV-negative partner HIV wale partner ke saath rehta hai, wo bhi cover hota hai [[naco-hiv-aids-act-2017-gazette]]. Aur 2018 mein Supreme Court ke Navtej Singh Johar judgment ke baad se, do adults ke beech consensual same-sex sex crime nahi hai [[scobserver-navtej-johar-2018]]. Gay, bisexual ya trans hona koi confess karne wali baat nahi hai.

Kahan poochein: government hospital ki HIV ya STI services mein (2025 mein India mein district hospitals aur medical colleges mein STIs ke liye 1,127 Suraksha Clinics thi [[naco-sankalak-2025]]), kisi community organisation mein jo tumhare group ke saath kaam karti hai, ya kisi private doctor ke paas. Seedha pucho ki kya wo PrEP prescribe karte hain, aur agar nahi, toh kaun karta hai. Confidential guidance ke liye NACO ki helpline 1097 pe call karo [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Agar koi clinic upar wale consent ya confidentiality ke rules tode, ya tum HIV wale kisi insaan ke saath rehte ho aur tumhare saath discrimination ho, toh tum apne state ke HIV Ombudsman se complaint kar sakte ho; March 2025 tak 34 States aur UTs mein Ombudsman tha [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Ye general information hai, legal advice nahi.

hpv-vaccine-campaign-parents-questions.en:
On 28 February 2026, India began offering a single free dose of HPV vaccine to girls aged 14 at government health facilities, a yearly group of about 1.2 crore girls [[pib-hpv-campaign-launch-2026]]. By 11 September, more than 80 lakh doses had been given [[pib-hpv-80-lakh-doses-2026]]. That pace also means lakhs of parents have been handed a consent decision about a vaccine new to the public programme, often at a crowded health centre where nobody has time to explain. These are the questions parents ask most, answered plainly.

## What does the vaccine protect against, and why at 14?

HPV, the human papillomavirus, is a very common infection passed on through sexual skin contact. Most infections clear on their own, but a few high-risk types can persist for years and turn cells in the cervix, the opening of the uterus, cancerous [[who-cervical]]. Two of them, types 16 and 18, account for more than 80% of cervical cancer cases in India, according to a government backgrounder [[pib-hpv-backgrounder-2026]]. The campaign's vaccine, Gardasil-4, covers those two plus types 6 and 11 [[pib-hpv-campaign-launch-2026]], which mainly cause genital warts.

The vaccine prevents infection; it cannot clear one that has already happened. So it works best when given well before any sexual contact, which is why WHO's priority group is young adolescent girls [[who-hpv]]. Fourteen is not a guess about a girl's private life. It is a seat belt fastened before the journey, not after a crash.

The stakes are not small. The latest GLOBOCAN estimate puts cervical cancer deaths in India at 36,319 in 2024 [[iarc-globocan-india-factsheet-2024]].

## One dose, free, voluntary: how does the campaign work?

The dose is free, and only at government facilities: Ayushman Arogya Mandir health centres, community health centres, sub-district and district hospitals and government medical colleges, in all 36 States and UTs [[pib-hpv-update-march-2026]]. Private clinics charge for HPV vaccines; the public programme does not.

One dose is the national schedule [[pib-hpv-campaign-launch-2026]]. Some parents remember older advice of two or three doses from private paediatricians. WHO has since accepted a single-dose schedule for girls in this age group, because studies show one dose protects well [[who-hpv]]. If a private doctor advises more doses for your child, ask why.

Vaccination is voluntary, and parental consent is mandatory before the dose is given [[pib-hpv-update-march-2026]]. Consent is recorded on U-WIN, the government's digital vaccination register [[pib-hpv-campaign-launch-2026]]. No health worker may vaccinate your daughter without it. The same safeguard means a parent's unanswered doubt can cost a girl her dose, so ask your questions before you say no.

## Is it safe? What side effects should we expect?

HPV vaccines have been used worldwide for years, and WHO considers them safe and effective [[who-hpv]]. The vaccine contains no live virus, so it cannot cause an HPV infection. Common reactions are those of any injection: a sore arm, redness or swelling where the needle went in, sometimes a headache or mild fever for a day or so.

Teenagers sometimes faint after an injection, usually from nerves rather than the vaccine. That is why girls are asked to sit and be watched for a while afterwards. Serious allergic reactions are rare with any vaccine. WHO has found no evidence that HPV vaccines affect fertility [[who-hpv]].

No vaccine is risk-free, and parents deserve straight answers, not frightening forwards or a brush-off at the counter. If something worries you after the dose, such as a rash, breathing trouble or a high fever, go back to the facility or the nearest hospital and say which vaccine she received.

## Already vaccinated, missed it, or a son: what now?

**Already vaccinated privately?** A girl who received Gardasil, Gardasil-9, Cervarix or the India-made Cervavac at a private clinic is recorded on U-WIN rather than vaccinated again [[pib-hpv-update-march-2026]]. Bring her vaccination card.

**Missed the campaign?** The launch phase was a 90-day campaign; after that, the dose moved to routine immunisation days at government facilities [[pib-hpv-campaign-launch-2026]]. Ask your nearest centre which day it is given. She is not alone: Gujarat, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh and Mizoram reported 100% coverage of the girls they identified, but more than 80 lakh doses is still only about two-thirds of one year's group [[pib-hpv-80-lakh-doses-2026]]. If your daughter is already past 14, ask whether she still qualifies; if not, a doctor can advise on private catch-up vaccination [[who-hpv]].

**What about a son?** Boys are not covered by the national programme [[pib-hpv-campaign-launch-2026]]. HPV also causes genital warts and some cancers in men, and men pass the virus on [[who-hpv]]. WHO puts girls first because cervical cancer causes most HPV-related deaths, and vaccinating most girls also protects many boys indirectly, though not men who have sex with men [[who-hpv]]. Parents who want to protect a son can ask a paediatrician about a private dose and its cost. Leaving boys out of the free programme is a policy choice, not proof that HPV is a "women's problem".

## Why will a vaccinated girl still need screening later?

Because the vaccine does not cover every HPV type that can cause cancer. Types 16 and 18 cause more than 80% of India's cervical cancers [[pib-hpv-backgrounder-2026]]; other types cause the rest. A vaccinated girl's risk is much lower, not zero.

Screening finds changes in the cervix years before they become cancer, when treatment is simple [[who-cervical]]. India's record is poor: in 2019-21, only 1.2% of women aged 15-49 had ever been screened [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. WHO's elimination strategy asks countries to screen 70% of women with a high-performance test by 35 and again by 45 [[who-cervical-elimination-launch-2020]].

So the vaccine is half the protection. Today's 14-year-olds are years away from screening age; tell your daughter now that she will need a test, so the word "cervix" is not strange to her when a doctor says it. And if you are a mother who has never been screened, the visit for her free dose is a good moment to ask about a test for yourself.
hpv-vaccine-campaign-parents-questions.hg:
28 February 2026 se India ne government health facilities par 14 saal ki ladkiyon ko HPV vaccine ki ek free dose dena shuru kiya. Yeh har saal lagbhag 1.2 crore ladkiyon ka group hai [[pib-hpv-campaign-launch-2026]]. 11 September tak 80 lakh se zyada doses lag chuki thi [[pib-hpv-80-lakh-doses-2026]]. Is speed ka matlab yeh bhi hai ki lakhon parents ke haath mein ek aisi vaccine ka consent decision aa gaya jo public programme ke liye nayi hai, aur woh bhi aksar ek bheed wale health centre mein, jahan kisi ke paas samjhane ka time nahi hota. Parents sabse zyada jo sawaal poochte hain, unke seedhe jawaab yeh rahe.

## Vaccine kis cheez se bachati hai, aur 14 saal par hi kyun?

HPV, yaani human papillomavirus, ek bahut common infection hai jo sexual contact mein skin-to-skin chhoone se failta hai. Zyadatar infections apne aap theek ho jaate hain, lekin kuch high-risk types saalon tak body mein tike reh sakte hain aur cervix ke cells ko cancer mein badal sakte hain. Cervix yaani uterus ka muh [[who-cervical]]. Government ke ek backgrounder ke mutabik inmein se do, type 16 aur 18, India mein cervical cancer ke 80% se zyada cases ke liye zimmedar hain [[pib-hpv-backgrounder-2026]]. Campaign ki vaccine, Gardasil-4, in dono ke saath type 6 aur 11 se bhi bachati hai [[pib-hpv-campaign-launch-2026]], jo mainly genital warts karte hain.

Vaccine infection ko rokti hai; jo infection pehle ho chuka hai, use clear nahi kar sakti. Isliye yeh tab sabse achha kaam karti hai jab kisi bhi sexual contact se kaafi pehle lag jaaye. Yahi wajah hai ki WHO ka priority group kam umar ki teenage ladkiyan hain [[who-hpv]]. 14 saal ladki ki private life ke baare mein koi andaaza nahi hai. Yeh seat belt jaisa hai: safar se pehle lagaya jaata hai, accident ke baad nahi.

Daav chhota nahi hai. GLOBOCAN ke latest estimate ke hisaab se 2024 mein India mein cervical cancer se 36,319 deaths hui [[iarc-globocan-india-factsheet-2024]].

## Ek dose, free, voluntary: campaign kaise kaam karta hai?

Dose free hai, aur sirf government facilities par milti hai: Ayushman Arogya Mandir health centres, community health centres, sub-district aur district hospitals, aur government medical colleges, saare 36 States aur UTs mein [[pib-hpv-update-march-2026]]. Private clinics HPV vaccine ke paise lete hain; public programme nahi leta.

National schedule ek dose ka hai [[pib-hpv-campaign-launch-2026]]. Kuch parents ko private paediatricians ki purani advice yaad hai, do ya teen doses wali. WHO ab is age group ki ladkiyon ke liye single-dose schedule maan chuka hai, kyunki studies dikhati hain ki ek dose achhi protection deti hai [[who-hpv]]. Agar koi private doctor tumhare bachche ke liye zyada doses ki salah de, toh poocho kyun.

Vaccination voluntary hai, aur dose se pehle parents ka consent mandatory hai [[pib-hpv-update-march-2026]]. Consent U-WIN par record hota hai, jo government ka digital vaccination register hai [[pib-hpv-campaign-launch-2026]]. Iske bina koi health worker tumhari beti ko vaccine nahi laga sakta. Lekin isi safeguard ka matlab yeh bhi hai ki parent ka ek shak, jiska jawaab kisi ne nahi diya, ladki ki dose chhudwa sakta hai. Isliye "na" kehne se pehle apne sawaal zaroor poocho.

## Kya yeh safe hai? Kaun se side effects ho sakte hain?

HPV vaccines duniya bhar mein saalon se use ho rahi hain, aur WHO inhe safe aur effective maanta hai [[who-hpv]]. Vaccine mein koi zinda virus nahi hota, isliye isse HPV infection nahi ho sakta. Common reactions wahi hain jo kisi bhi injection ke hote hain: baanh mein dard, jahan sui lagi wahan laali ya sujan, kabhi-kabhi ek-do din sar dard ya halka bukhaar.

Teenagers kabhi-kabhi injection ke baad behosh ho jaate hain, aksar ghabrahat ki wajah se, vaccine ki wajah se nahi. Isiliye ladkiyon ko shot ke baad kuch der baithne aur nigrani mein rehne ko kaha jaata hai. Serious allergic reactions kisi bhi vaccine se rare hote hain. WHO ko aisa koi evidence nahi mila ki HPV vaccines fertility par asar daalti hain [[who-hpv]].

Koi bhi vaccine bilkul risk-free nahi hoti, aur parents seedhe jawaab ke haqdaar hain, na ki darane wale forwards ke, na hi counter par taal-matol ke. Dose ke baad agar kuch pareshaan kare, jaise rash, saans lene mein dikkat ya tez bukhaar, toh wapas facility ya nearest hospital jao aur batao ki use kaun si vaccine lagi thi.

## Pehle se vaccinated, campaign miss ho gaya, ya beta hai: ab kya?

**Private mein pehle hi vaccine lag chuki hai?** Jis ladki ko private clinic mein Gardasil, Gardasil-9, Cervarix ya India mein bani Cervavac lag chuki hai, use dobara vaccine nahi di jaati, balki U-WIN par record kar liya jaata hai [[pib-hpv-update-march-2026]]. Uska vaccination card saath le jao.

**Campaign miss ho gaya?** Launch phase 90 din ka campaign tha; uske baad dose government facilities par routine immunisation days par milne lagi [[pib-hpv-campaign-launch-2026]]. Apne nearest centre se poocho ki kis din lagti hai. Tumhari beti akeli nahi hai: Gujarat, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh aur Mizoram ne apni identified ladkiyon mein 100% coverage report kiya, lekin 80 lakh se zyada doses bhi ek saal ke group ka abhi sirf lagbhag do-tihai hissa hai [[pib-hpv-80-lakh-doses-2026]]. Agar beti 14 saal se badi ho chuki hai, toh poocho ki kya woh ab bhi eligible hai; agar nahi, toh doctor private catch-up vaccination ke baare mein salah de sakta hai [[who-hpv]].

**Bete ka kya?** National programme mein ladke shaamil nahi hain [[pib-hpv-campaign-launch-2026]]. HPV men mein bhi genital warts aur kuch cancers karta hai, aur men bhi virus aage failate hain [[who-hpv]]. WHO ladkiyon ko pehle rakhta hai kyunki HPV se judi zyadatar deaths cervical cancer se hoti hain, aur zyadatar ladkiyon ko vaccine lagne se kai ladkon ko bhi indirectly protection milti hai, lekin un men ko nahi jo men ke saath sex karte hain [[who-hpv]]. Jo parents bete ko bachana chahte hain, woh paediatrician se private dose aur uske kharche ke baare mein pooch sakte hain. Ladkon ko free programme se bahar rakhna ek policy ka faisla hai, is baat ka saboot nahi ki HPV sirf "auraton ki problem" hai.

## Vaccine lagi ladki ko bhi baad mein screening kyun chahiye?

Kyunki vaccine har us HPV type se nahi bachati jo cancer kar sakta hai. India ke 80% se zyada cervical cancers type 16 aur 18 se hote hain [[pib-hpv-backgrounder-2026]]; baaki doosre types se. Vaccine lagi ladki ka risk bahut kam ho jaata hai, zero nahi.

Screening cervix mein hone wale badlav cancer banne se saalon pehle pakad leti hai, jab ilaaj aasaan hota hai [[who-cervical]]. India ka record kharab hai: 2019-21 mein 15-49 saal ki sirf 1.2% women ne kabhi screening karwayi thi [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. WHO ki elimination strategy countries se kehti hai ki 70% women ka high-performance test 35 ki umar tak aur phir 45 tak ho [[who-cervical-elimination-launch-2020]].

Toh vaccine aadhi protection hai. Aaj ki 14 saal ki ladkiyan screening wali umar se abhi saalon door hain; apni beti ko abhi bata do ki use test karwana hoga, taaki jab doctor "cervix" bole toh yeh shabd use ajeeb na lage. Aur agar tum ek maa ho jisne kabhi screening nahi karwayi, toh beti ki free dose ke liye jaana apne test ke baare mein poochne ka bhi achha mauka hai.

infertility-one-in-six-banjh-myth.en:
Imagine a couple in Gorakhpur, married three years, no child. By now the wife has had blood tests, two ultrasounds and a test of her tubes. She keeps a fast every Monday and wears a thread from a baba her mother-in-law trusts. Her husband has not given a single sample. Nobody has asked him to.

This is a hypothetical, but the pattern is familiar. The word used for her is "banjh", said in the kitchen, at family functions, and sometimes to her face. Medicine has no such word, because medicine does not treat infertility as a woman's defect.

## 1 in 6: a medical condition, not a curse

The World Health Organization estimates that about 17.5% of adults, roughly 1 in 6 people, experience infertility at some point in their lives [[who-infertility-estimates-2023]]. WHO defines it as a disease of the male or female reproductive system: no pregnancy after 12 months or more of regular unprotected sex [[who-infertility]].

The next number matters as much. Lifetime prevalence was 17.8% in high-income countries and 16.5% in low- and middle-income ones [[who-infertility-estimates-2023]]. Infertility is not a rich-country problem or a poor-country problem: the rates are close.

The estimate is global, not a count of Indian couples [[who-infertility-estimates-2023]]. What it does show is that infertility is common, not a rare curse that falls on a few unlucky wives.

## Myth: it is always the woman

WHO's list of causes has two columns. In men: blockages in the tubes that carry semen, hormonal disorders, testicles that do not produce sperm, and sperm with abnormal shape or movement. In women: blocked fallopian tubes, conditions of the uterus such as endometriosis and fibroids, disorders of the ovaries such as polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), and other hormonal problems. Sometimes no cause can be found [[who-infertility]].

Female causes are real and common. PCOS is a leading cause of infertility [[who-pcos-factsheet-2026]], and an ICMR-funded national study found it in 7.2% of Indian women aged 18-40 by the strictest criteria and 19.6% by the broadest [[jama-netw-open-pcos-india-2024]]. It is also manageable, and pregnancy is possible with it [[who-pcos]].

So the truth is not "it is never her". The truth is that nobody knows whose body holds the cause until both are tested, and in many homes only one body is. When only her body is tested, only she can be blamed.

The man's first test is a semen analysis: a laboratory examines a sample, with no needle, no surgery and no pain. Infertility is often confused with impotence. They are different things. A man can have normal erections and still have a low sperm count. A lab report is not a certificate of "mardangi".

## Myth: the pill, masturbation or her 'past' caused it

When no child comes, families go looking for something the woman did.

Reversible contraceptives, including the pill and the Copper-T, do not cause infertility; fertility returns after they are stopped [[who-fp]]. Masturbation, by men or women, is common and physically harmless, and it appears nowhere on WHO's list of causes [[who-infertility]].

What that list does contain is less convenient for gossip. Untreated sexually transmitted infections can block the fallopian tubes, and so can complications of an unsafe abortion or an infection after childbirth. Smoking, heavy drinking and obesity affect fertility in both partners [[who-infertility]]. None of these is a moral failing.

## Myth: a baba can fix it. When to see a doctor, together

Fasts, threads and powders cost a couple the one thing they cannot buy back: time. No ritual opens a blocked tube or raises a sperm count.

The "guaranteed" cures sold to childless couples are often tonics that promise to fix periods or male "weakness". Advertising a drug for "the correction of menstrual disorder in women" or for "the maintenance or improvement of the capacity of human beings for sexual pleasure" has been banned under the Drugs and Magic Remedies Act since 1954. In March 2025 the Supreme Court said "there is no implementation of the 1954 Act in its true letter and spirit" [[sc-ima-order-mar-2025]]. This is general information, not legal advice.

The medical rule is simple. If there is no pregnancy after 12 months of regular unprotected sex, see a doctor [[who-infertility]]. Ask sooner if her periods are irregular or absent, or if age is a worry: a doctor can say how long to wait.

Go together, and insist that both are examined from the first visit. Testing only the wife can mean a year of scans for a problem that was waiting in a semen report nobody ordered. Treatment depends on the cause: it can mean medicines that stimulate ovulation [[who-pcos]], or assisted methods such as IVF [[who-infertility]]. None is guaranteed, and an honest doctor will say so.

## Pressure, cost and the son question

The blame has consequences that are not medical. WHO records that women in infertile couples frequently face violence, divorce, stigma, depression and anxiety [[who-infertility]]. Treatment is paid for largely out of pocket [[who-infertility-estimates-2023]], so a family can spend its savings on the wife's tests before the husband is tested at all.

Then there is the demand behind the demand. In a 2014 ICRW-UNFPA survey in seven Indian states, 76% of men and 81% of women said it was very important to have at least one son [[icrw-unfpa-masculinity-ipv-son-preference-2014]]. For many couples the pressure is not to have a child but to have a boy, which is why a mother of two daughters can be taunted almost as hard as a woman with none. Biology gives that no support: every egg carries an X chromosome, and whether a baby is a girl or a boy depends on which sperm, X or Y, reaches it. That is chance.

> Nobody knows whose body holds the cause until both are tested. In many Indian homes, only one body is.

A couple owes nobody a child. Some will conceive with treatment, some will adopt, and some will build a life without children. All three are whole lives. If taunts turn into threats or violence, call the Women Helpline. If the pressure is crushing either of you, Tele-MANAS on 14416 is free and open round the clock.
infertility-one-in-six-banjh-myth.hg:
Sochiye, Gorakhpur ka ek couple, shaadi ko teen saal ho gaye, bachcha nahi hai. Ab tak biwi ke blood tests ho chuke hain, do ultrasound aur tubes ka ek test bhi. Woh har Somvaar vrat rakhti hai aur us baba ka dhaaga pehenti hai jis par uski saas ko bharosa hai. Uske pati ne aaj tak ek sample nahi diya. Kisi ne usse kaha bhi nahi.

Yeh ek hypothetical hai, lekin pattern jaana-pehchaana hai. Uske liye jo shabd use hota hai woh hai "banjh", jo kitchen mein, family functions mein aur kabhi-kabhi uske munh par bola jaata hai. Medicine ke paas aisa koi shabd nahi hai, kyunki medicine infertility ko aurat ki kami nahi maanti.

## 6 mein se 1: ek medical condition, koi shraap nahi

World Health Organization ka estimate hai ki lagbhag 17.5% adults, yaani roughly 6 mein se 1 insaan, zindagi mein kabhi na kabhi infertility face karte hain [[who-infertility-estimates-2023]]. WHO ise male ya female reproductive system ki bimaari maanta hai: 12 mahine ya usse zyada regular unprotected sex ke baad bhi pregnancy na hona [[who-infertility]].

Agla number bhi utna hi zaroori hai. Lifetime prevalence high-income deshon mein 17.8% thi aur low- aur middle-income deshon mein 16.5% [[who-infertility-estimates-2023]]. Infertility na ameer deshon ki problem hai, na gareeb deshon ki: dono jagah rates kareeb-kareeb ek jaise hain.

Yeh estimate global hai, Indian couples ki ginti nahi [[who-infertility-estimates-2023]]. Lekin yeh itna zaroor dikhata hai ki infertility common hai, koi durlabh shraap nahi jo bas kuch 'badkismat' biwiyon par padta ho.

## Myth: kami hamesha aurat mein hoti hai

WHO ki wajahon ki list mein do column hain. Mardon mein: semen le jaane wali tubes mein blockage, hormonal disorders, testicles ka sperm na banana, aur sperm ki shape ya movement ka abnormal hona. Aurton mein: fallopian tubes ka block hona, uterus ki conditions jaise endometriosis aur fibroids, ovaries ke disorders jaise polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), aur doosri hormonal problems. Kabhi-kabhi koi wajah milti hi nahi [[who-infertility]].

Aurton wali wajahein asli hain aur common bhi. PCOS infertility ki ek leading wajah hai [[who-pcos-factsheet-2026]], aur ICMR-funded ek national study mein 18-40 saal ki Indian aurton mein yeh sabse strict criteria se 7.2% mein mila aur sabse broad criteria se 19.6% mein [[jama-netw-open-pcos-india-2024]]. Ise manage bhi kiya ja sakta hai, aur iske saath pregnancy possible hai [[who-pcos]].

Toh sach yeh nahi hai ki "kami kabhi usme hoti hi nahi". Sach yeh hai ki jab tak dono ka test na ho, koi nahi jaanta ki wajah kiske shareer mein hai, aur kai gharon mein test sirf ek hi shareer ka hota hai. Jab test sirf uska hota hai, toh blame bhi sirf usi par aata hai.

Mard ka pehla test semen analysis hai: lab ek sample ko check karti hai, na sui, na surgery, na dard. Infertility ko aksar impotence, yaani erection ki problem, samajh liya jaata hai. Yeh do alag cheezein hain. Kisi mard ke erections bilkul normal ho sakte hain aur phir bhi sperm count kam ho sakta hai. Lab report "mardangi" ka certificate nahi hoti.

## Myth: pill, masturbation ya uske 'past' ki wajah se hua

Jab bachcha nahi hota, toh family dhoondhne lagti hai ki aurat ne aisa kya kiya tha.

Reversible contraceptives, jinmein pill aur Copper-T shaamil hain, infertility nahi karte; inhe band karne ke baad fertility laut aati hai [[who-fp]]. Masturbation, chaahe mard kare ya aurat, common hai aur shareer ko nuksaan nahi pahunchata, aur WHO ki wajahon ki list mein yeh kahin nahi hai [[who-infertility]].

Us list mein jo hai, woh gossip ke kaam ka kam hai. Bina ilaaj ke sexually transmitted infections fallopian tubes ko block kar sakte hain, aur unsafe abortion ki complications ya delivery ke baad ka infection bhi. Smoking, zyada sharaab aur obesity dono partners ki fertility par asar daalte hain [[who-infertility]]. Inmein se kuch bhi character ki kami nahi hai.

## Myth: baba theek kar dega. Doctor ke paas kab jaana hai, aur saath mein kyun

Vrat, dhaage aur powder couple se woh ek cheez le lete hain jo wapas khareedi nahi ja sakti: time. Koi totka band tube nahi kholta, na sperm count badhata hai.

Bina bachche wale couples ko jo "guaranteed" ilaaj beche jaate hain, woh aksar aise tonic hote hain jo periods ya mardon ki "kamzori" theek karne ka vaada karte hain. Kisi dawa ka "the correction of menstrual disorder in women" ya "the maintenance or improvement of the capacity of human beings for sexual pleasure" ke liye ad karna 1954 se Drugs and Magic Remedies Act ke tahat banned hai. March 2025 mein Supreme Court ne kaha: "there is no implementation of the 1954 Act in its true letter and spirit", yaani is kanoon par sahi maayne mein amal ho hi nahi raha [[sc-ima-order-mar-2025]]. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

Medical rule simple hai. Agar 12 mahine regular unprotected sex ke baad bhi pregnancy na ho, toh doctor se miliye [[who-infertility]]. Agar uske periods irregular hain ya aate hi nahi, ya umar ko lekar fikr hai, toh pehle hi jaiye: doctor bata sakta hai ki kitna intezaar karna theek hai.

Saath jaiye, aur zor dijiye ki pehli visit se hi dono ki jaanch ho. Sirf biwi ke test karwane ka matlab ho sakta hai saal bhar ke scans, ek aisi problem ke liye jo us semen report mein baithi thi jo kisi ne karwayi hi nahi. Ilaaj wajah par depend karta hai: ovulation stimulate karne wali dawaiyan ho sakti hain [[who-pcos]], ya IVF jaise assisted methods [[who-infertility]]. Guarantee kisi ki nahi hai, aur imaandaar doctor yeh khud bata dega.

## Pressure, kharcha aur bete wala sawaal

Is blame ke nateeje sirf medical nahi hain. WHO ke mutabik infertile couples mein aurton ko aksar violence, talaaq, stigma, depression aur anxiety jhelni padti hai [[who-infertility]]. Ilaaj ka kharcha zyada tar apni jeb se dena padta hai [[who-infertility-estimates-2023]], isliye ho sakta hai ki pati ka ek bhi test hone se pehle family apni bachat biwi ke tests par laga de.

Phir is demand ke peeche ek aur demand hai. 2014 ke ICRW-UNFPA survey mein, jo saat Indian states mein hua, 76% mardon aur 81% aurton ne kaha ki kam se kam ek beta hona bahut zaroori hai [[icrw-unfpa-masculinity-ipv-son-preference-2014]]. Kai couples par pressure bachcha paida karne ka nahi, ladka paida karne ka hota hai, aur isiliye do betiyon ki maa ko bhi lagbhag utne hi taane mil sakte hain jitne us aurat ko jiske koi bachcha nahi. Biology iska koi saath nahi deti: har egg mein X chromosome hota hai, aur baby ladki hogi ya ladka, yeh is par depend karta hai ki us tak kaun sa sperm pahunchta hai, X wala ya Y wala. Yeh sirf chance hai.

> Jab tak dono ka test na ho, koi nahi jaanta ki wajah kiske shareer mein hai. Kai Indian gharon mein test sirf ek hi shareer ka hota hai.

Koi bhi couple kisi ko bachcha dene ka karzdaar nahi hai. Kuch log ilaaj se conceive karenge, kuch adopt karenge, aur kuch bina bachchon ke apni zindagi banayenge. Teeno poori zindagiyan hain. Agar taane dhamki ya violence mein badal jaayein, toh Women Helpline par call kijiye. Agar yeh pressure aap dono mein se kisi ko bhi tod raha hai, toh Tele-MANAS 14416 free hai aur chaubees ghante khula rehta hai.

lenacapavir-hiv-prevention-jab-india-202.en:
India has cut new HIV infections roughly in half since 2010, to an estimated 64,470 in 2024 [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. That is real progress, and it still means a new infection every few minutes. The national programme that ran until March 2026 had aimed for an 80% cut from 2010 levels [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. In 2026 one development could help close that gap: a long-acting HIV prevention injection, lenacapavir, moved closer to the Indian market.

## What happened in 2026

On 11 August 2026 a Subject Expert Committee of the Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO), India's drug regulator, recommended waiving local Phase III trials and bioequivalence studies for generic lenacapavir for pre-exposure prophylaxis, or PrEP. The applicants were Dr Reddy's Laboratories and Emcure Pharmaceuticals, and the committee cited an "unmet medical need" [[theprint-lenacapavir-cdsco-2026]]. Skipping trials that would only repeat evidence from abroad saves time, not safety checks: the drug was already approved in the United States and several other countries [[outlook-lenacapavir-cdsco-2026]].

This is a recommendation, not a licence to sell. Each company still needs CDSCO's marketing approval, and must then submit a Phase IV study protocol within three months [[outlook-lenacapavir-cdsco-2026]]. In November 2026 Dr Reddy's became the first licensed generic maker to receive tentative approval from the US Food and Drug Administration, a step aimed at supplying lower-income countries [[medicaldialogues-lenacapavir-fda-2026]]. As of late November we found no Indian launch date.

## What lenacapavir is

The generic product is a 463.5 mg injection given once every six months, for adults and adolescents weighing at least 35 kg who are at increased risk of getting HIV through sex. A person must test HIV-negative before starting [[outlook-lenacapavir-cdsco-2026]].

The trial results behind it are striking. In the PURPOSE 1 trial there were no HIV infections among women receiving the twice-yearly injection, and PURPOSE 2 showed a 96% reduction in HIV incidence compared with background rates [[theprint-lenacapavir-cdsco-2026]].

PrEP itself is not new. It is medicine taken by HIV-negative people to prevent infection, prescribed by a clinician [[who-hiv]]. What changes is the burden. A daily pill has to be taken every day, carried, hidden from family and refilled. Two injections a year remove most of that.

## Who it could matter for most

HIV in India is concentrated. In 2024 prevalence was 8.79% among people who inject drugs, 2.84% among hijra and transgender people, 2.12% among men who have sex with men and 1.13% among female sex workers, against 0.20% among all adults [[naco-sankalak-2025]].

For many in these groups, a strip of pills found at home can mean being outed, thrown out or beaten. Imagine a 22-year-old in Lucknow who has not told his family he is gay and shares a room with his brother. A daily pill is a daily risk. An injection at a clinic twice a year is not.

There is a second gap. In 2024-25 only 83.9% of people living with HIV in India knew their status, short of the UN target of 95% [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Prevention tools only work if testing reaches people first, and a negative test is required before every PrEP start.

## Why approval is not access

Three questions will decide whether lenacapavir reaches the people who need it.

- **Price.** Generics are targeted at about USD 40 per person per year, against about USD 28,000 for the brand in the United States [[medicaldialogues-lenacapavir-fda-2026]]. An Indian price has not been announced.
- **The public programme.** India's free HIV services run through NACO. Whether lenacapavir is bought and offered free at government centres will matter far more than a pharmacy launch. No such decision had been reported by November 2026.
- **Stigma at the clinic.** A drug for gay men, transgender people and sex workers is only useful if they can walk in without being judged.

> A prevention tool that people cannot afford, cannot find, or are ashamed to ask for prevents nothing.

## What you can do now

You do not need to wait for lenacapavir. If you may have been exposed to HIV, emergency PEP must start as soon as possible and no later than 72 hours, and is taken for 28 days [[who-pep]]. If you are at ongoing risk, ask a doctor about oral PrEP today. Free testing is available through government centres; the NACO helpline is 1097. And remember that HIV is treatable: a person on effective treatment with an undetectable viral load does not pass HIV on through sex [[who-hiv]]. An estimated 25.61 lakh people live with HIV in India [[naco-sankalak-2025]], and most of them are living full lives.
lenacapavir-hiv-prevention-jab-india-202.hg:
India ne 2010 ke baad naye HIV infections lagbhag aadhe kar diye hain, 2024 mein inka anumaan 64,470 tha [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Yeh asli tarakki hai, aur iska matlab ab bhi yeh hai ki har kuch minute mein ek naya infection hota hai. March 2026 tak chale national programme ka lakshya 2010 ke muqaable 80% kami ka tha [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. 2026 mein ek kadam is fark ko kam karne mein madad kar sakta hai: lambe samay tak asar karne wala HIV prevention injection, lenacapavir, Indian market ke kareeb aaya.

## 2026 mein kya hua

11 August 2026 ko India ke drug regulator Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO) ki ek Subject Expert Committee ne sifaarish ki ki pre-exposure prophylaxis, yaani PrEP, ke liye generic lenacapavir par local Phase III trials aur bioequivalence studies ki shart hata di jaaye. Applicants Dr Reddy's Laboratories aur Emcure Pharmaceuticals the, aur committee ne "unmet medical need" ka hawaala diya [[theprint-lenacapavir-cdsco-2026]]. Jo trials sirf videsh ke saboot ko dohraate, unhe chhodne se samay bachta hai, safety checks nahi ghatte: yeh dawa United States aur kai aur deshon mein pehle se approved thi [[outlook-lenacapavir-cdsco-2026]].

Yeh sifaarish hai, bechne ka licence nahi. Har company ko ab bhi CDSCO ki marketing approval chahiye, aur uske baad teen mahine ke andar Phase IV study ka protocol dena hoga [[outlook-lenacapavir-cdsco-2026]]. November 2026 mein Dr Reddy's US Food and Drug Administration se tentative approval paane wali pehli licensed generic company bani, jiska maqsad kam aamdani wale deshon ko supply karna hai [[medicaldialogues-lenacapavir-fda-2026]]. November ke aakhir tak humein India mein launch ki koi taareekh nahi mili.

## Lenacapavir hai kya

Generic product 463.5 mg ka injection hai jo har chhe mahine mein ek baar diya jaata hai, un adults aur adolescents ko jinka wazan kam se kam 35 kg ho aur jinhe sex ke zariye HIV hone ka zyada khatra ho. Shuru karne se pehle HIV-negative test zaroori hai [[outlook-lenacapavir-cdsco-2026]].

Iske peeche ke trial results chaunkane wale hain. PURPOSE 1 trial mein saal mein do baar injection lene wali aurton mein ek bhi HIV infection nahi hua, aur PURPOSE 2 mein background dar ke muqaable HIV incidence mein 96% kami dikhi [[theprint-lenacapavir-cdsco-2026]].

PrEP khud nayi cheez nahi hai. Yeh woh dawa hai jo HIV-negative log infection se bachne ke liye lete hain, aur ise clinician likhta hai [[who-hiv]]. Badalta hai bojh. Roz ki goli roz leni padti hai, saath rakhni padti hai, family se chhupani padti hai aur dobara leni padti hai. Saal mein do injection is bojh ka zyada hissa hata dete hain.

## Yeh sabse zyada kiske liye maayne rakhta hai
