India mein HIV kuch groups mein simta hua hai. 2024 mein drugs inject karne walon mein prevalence 8.79% thi, hijra aur transgender logon mein 2.84%, men who have sex with men mein 2.12% aur female sex workers mein 1.13%, jabki sabhi adults mein yeh 0.20% thi [[naco-sankalak-2025]].

In groups ke kai logon ke liye ghar mein mili goliyon ki ek strip ka matlab ho sakta hai raaz khulna, ghar se nikaala jaana ya maar khaana. Sochiye Lucknow ka ek 22 saal ka ladka jisne family ko nahi bataya ki woh gay hai, aur jo apne bhai ke saath kamra share karta hai. Roz ki goli roz ka khatra hai. Saal mein do baar clinic mein injection nahi.

Ek aur kami hai. 2024-25 mein India mein HIV ke saath jee rahe sirf 83.9% logon ko apna status pata tha, jo UN ke 95% target se kam hai [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Prevention ke tools tabhi kaam karte hain jab testing pehle logon tak pahunche, aur har PrEP shuru karne se pehle negative test zaroori hai.

## Approval ka matlab pahunch kyon nahi

Teen sawaal tay karenge ki lenacapavir zaroorat walon tak pahunchta hai ya nahi.

- **Keemat.** Generics ki target keemat lagbhag USD 40 per person per saal hai, jabki United States mein brand lagbhag USD 28,000 ka hai [[medicaldialogues-lenacapavir-fda-2026]]. India mein keemat ka elaan nahi hua hai.
- **Sarkari programme.** India ki free HIV services NACO ke zariye chalti hain. Lenacapavir sarkari centres par free milega ya nahi, yeh kisi pharmacy launch se kahin zyada maayne rakhega. November 2026 tak aise kisi faisle ki report nahi thi.
- **Clinic mein stigma.** Gay men, transgender logon aur sex workers ke liye dawa tabhi kaam ki hai jab woh bina judge hue clinic mein ja sakein.

> Jo prevention tool log khareed na sakein, dhoondh na sakein, ya maangne mein sharmaayein, woh kuch nahi rokta.

## Aap abhi kya kar sakte hain

Lenacapavir ka intezaar karne ki zaroorat nahi. Agar aap HIV ke sampark mein aaye ho sakte hain, toh emergency PEP jitni jaldi ho sake aur 72 ghante ke andar shuru honi chahiye, aur 28 din li jaati hai [[who-pep]]. Agar aapko lagataar khatra hai, toh aaj hi doctor se oral PrEP ke baare mein poochiye. Sarkari centres par free testing milti hai; NACO helpline 1097 hai. Aur yaad rakhiye ki HIV ka ilaaj hai: effective treatment par jis insaan ka viral load undetectable hai, woh sex se HIV nahi failata [[who-hiv]]. India mein anumaanit 25.61 lakh log HIV ke saath jee rahe hain [[naco-sankalak-2025]], aur unmein se zyadatar poori zindagi jee rahe hain.

medical-care-after-sexual-assault-rights.en:
Imagine a 19-year-old reaching a private hospital's emergency desk in Patna at 2 a.m., a few hours after she was raped. The clerk asks for a copy of the FIR and a deposit, then suggests the government hospital across town. None of those demands survives the law. Since 2013, every hospital in India, public or private, has had to treat rape and acid-attack survivors immediately and free of cost, and refusing became a crime [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2013]].

Survivors rarely reach that desk. In NFHS-5 (2019-21), 77% of women aged 18-49 who had faced physical or sexual violence never sought help or told anyone [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. A hospital that turns someone away may be the only door she ever knocks on. Our 72-hour plan covers the survivor's side; this is about what the hospital owes.

## The law: free treatment, any hospital, but not for everyone

The rule began as Section 357C of the old Code of Criminal Procedure, with refusal punishable under Section 166B of the IPC [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2013]]. Since 1 July 2024 it sits in Section 397 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS). Every hospital, whether run by the Centre, a state, a local body "or any other person", must "immediately" give first aid or medical treatment "free of cost" to survivors of rape, acid attack and sexual offences against children under POCSO, and must inform the police [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

"Any other person" takes in the corporate chain, the charitable trust and the five-bed nursing home. "Immediately" means before the paperwork, not after an FIR. "Free of cost" comes with no exception for medicines or tests. A hospital in-charge who breaks the rule faces up to 1 year in jail under Section 200 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

POCSO protects every child under 18, boys included [[pocso-act-2012]]. In 2024 police recorded 892 boys among child victims of penetrative sexual assault [[ncrb-cii-2024]], and each of them is owed free treatment. Acid-attack survivors are covered whatever their gender.

The gap is adult men and transgender people. Under the BNS, rape can only be committed by a man against a woman, and the new code has no counterpart to IPC Section 377 [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Police registered 888 cases under Section 377 in 2023, a count that did not separate victims by gender; in the 2024 data the category is gone [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. In November 2023, Parliament's Standing Committee warned that dropping it would leave non-consensual sexual offences against men and transgender persons unpunished, and the government did not accept its advice [[prs-standing-committee-bns-2023]]. Sexual abuse of a transgender person is punishable under the Transgender Persons Act with six months to two years in prison [[indiacode-transgender-persons-2019]], but that offence is not on Section 397's list either. They need the same medicines on the same clock: go anyway, and ask for each by name.

## Treatment and evidence are different things

A hospital visit can do two jobs, and the law keeps them apart. Treatment is owed at once. The forensic examination, which collects evidence, falls under Section 184 of the BNSS: police must send a rape survivor for it within 24 hours of receiving information, only with her consent, and the doctor must send the report to the investigating officer within 7 days [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

So a survivor can say yes to medicine and no to swabs, or yes to some steps and no to others. Refusing the examination does not cancel the right to free treatment. The honest catch: Section 397 also orders the hospital to inform the police, so a visit can start a police process. Our Q&A on the medical exam walks through each step in the room.

## The medicines that cannot wait: emergency contraception and PEP

The law says "treatment" without listing medicines, but two of them run on a clock. HIV post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) must start as soon as possible and no later than 72 hours after the assault, and is then taken for 28 days [[who-pep]]. Emergency contraception works up to 5 days after unprotected sex, better the sooner it is taken; a copper IUD fitted by a doctor is the most effective option. It is not an abortion, and it does not protect against infections [[who-ec]].

A prescription that sends a survivor to a chemist outside, to pay for herself, is hard to square with "free of cost". If a pregnancy does follow, the abortion rules let survivors of rape end it up to 24 weeks [[gazette-mtp-amendment-rules-2021]].

## STIs, injuries and follow-up visits

Many sexually transmitted infections cause no symptoms, so only a test can tell. Bacterial ones are curable, and a vaccine exists for hepatitis B [[who-sti]]. Before leaving, ask for tests, treatment, the vaccine and the date of the follow-up HIV test after PEP ends.

For acid-attack survivors, care for injuries can last years. India registered 207 acid attacks in 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]], and since 2013 the Supreme Court has required states to pay every acid-attack victim at least Rs 3 lakh for after-care and rehabilitation, Rs 1 lakh of it within 15 days [[sc-laxmi-2013]].

## Mental-health care and One Stop Centres

Not sleeping, feeling numb or reliving the assault are injuries too. Tele-MANAS, the Health Ministry's free, round-the-clock mental-health helpline, answers on 14416 [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]].

What a hospital cannot do alone, a One Stop Centre (Sakhi) is meant to: counselling, police and legal help in one place, under the Women and Child Development Ministry's Mission Shakti [[wcd-mission-shakti]]. In December 2018 the Supreme Court asked every state to set up at least one in every district within a year [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]]. By July 2026, 985 of the 1,033 approved centres were working, and they had assisted over 15.20 lakh women since April 2015 [[pib-osc-lok-sabha-2026-07]].

If a hospital refuses, do not let the argument eat into the 72 hours. Note the name, the time and the hospital, go to the next one, and complain later: under the BNS, refusal is an offence, not a policy. This is general information, not legal advice.
medical-care-after-sexual-assault-rights.hg:
Sochiye, Patna mein raat ke 2 baje hain. Ek 19 saal ki ladki ke saath kuch ghante pehle rape hua hai. Woh ek private hospital ki emergency desk par pahunchti hai. Clerk pehle FIR ki copy maangta hai, phir deposit, aur phir kehta hai ki shehar ke us paar wale sarkari hospital chali jao. Law ke saamne inmein se ek bhi maang nahi tikti. 2013 se India ke har hospital ko, sarkari ho ya private, rape aur acid-attack survivors ka ilaaj turant aur free karna hota hai, aur ilaaj se mana karna crime bana diya gaya [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2013]].

Zyada tar survivors us desk tak pahunchte hi nahi. NFHS-5 (2019-21) mein, physical ya sexual violence jhel chuki 18-49 saal ki 77% auraton ne na kabhi help maangi, na kisi ko bataya [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Yaani jo hospital kisi ko lauta deta hai, ho sakta hai wahi uska akela darwaza ho. Survivor khud kya kare, yeh hamare 72-hour plan wale article mein hai; yeh article batata hai ki hospital ka farz kya hai.

## Law: har hospital mein free ilaaj, par sabke liye nahi

Yeh rule 2013 mein purane Code of Criminal Procedure ke Section 357C ke roop mein aaya, aur ilaaj se mana karne par IPC ke Section 166B mein saza rakhi gayi [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2013]]. 1 July 2024 se yahi rule Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) ke Section 397 mein hai. Hospital Centre ka ho, state ka, local body ka ya "any other person" ka, use "immediately" aur "free of cost" first aid ya medical treatment dena hoga. Yeh haq rape, acid attack aur POCSO wale child sexual offences ke survivors ko mila hai. Saath hi hospital ko police ko khabar karni hogi [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

"Any other person" mein bade corporate hospital bhi aate hain, trust wale hospital bhi, aur paanch bed wala nursing home bhi. "Immediately" ka matlab hai paperwork se pehle, FIR ke baad nahi. "Free of cost" mein dawaiyon ya tests ke liye koi chhoot nahi likhi. Jo hospital in-charge yeh rule tode, use Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ke Section 200 mein 1 saal tak ki jail ho sakti hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

POCSO 18 saal se kam umar ke har bachche ko protect karta hai, ladkon ko bhi [[pocso-act-2012]]. 2024 mein police ne penetrative sexual assault ke child victims mein 892 ladke darj kiye [[ncrb-cii-2024]], aur unmein se har ek free ilaaj ka haqdaar hai. Acid-attack survivors bhi cover hote hain, chahe unka gender kuch bhi ho.

Gap kahan hai? Adult mard aur transgender log. BNS mein rape sirf ek mard ka aurat par kiya gaya crime hai, aur naye code mein IPC Section 377 jaisa koi section nahi hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Police ne 2023 mein Section 377 mein 888 case darj kiye the, aur is ginti mein victims ka gender alag se nahi tha; 2024 ke data mein yeh category hi gayab hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. November 2023 mein Parliament ki Standing Committee ne warn kiya tha ki 377 hatane se mardon aur transgender logon ke khilaf non-consensual sexual offences bina saza ke reh jayenge. Sarkar ne yeh salaah nahi maani [[prs-standing-committee-bns-2023]]. Transgender insaan ke sexual abuse par Transgender Persons Act mein 6 mahine se 2 saal ki jail hai [[indiacode-transgender-persons-2019]], lekin yeh offence bhi Section 397 ki list mein nahi hai. In logon ko bhi wahi dawaiyan chahiye, utni hi jaldi. Phir bhi hospital jaiye, aur har dawa naam lekar maangiye.

## Treatment aur evidence, do alag cheezein hain

Hospital mein do kaam ho sakte hain, aur law dono ko alag rakhta hai. Ilaaj turant milna chahiye. Evidence jama karne wala forensic exam BNSS ke Section 184 mein aata hai: police ko information milne ke 24 ghante ke andar survivor ko is exam ke liye bhejna hota hai, exam sirf uske consent se ho sakta hai, aur doctor ko 7 din ke andar report investigating officer ko bhejni hoti hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

Yaani survivor dawa ke liye haan aur swab ke liye na keh sakti hai, ya kuch steps ke liye haan aur baaki ke liye na. Exam se mana karne par free ilaaj ka haq khatam nahi hota. Ek baat saaf jaan lijiye: Section 397 hospital se police ko khabar karne ko bhi kehta hai, isliye hospital jaane se police process shuru ho sakta hai. Exam room mein kya-kya hota hai, yeh hamare medical exam wale Q&A mein step by step samjhaya gaya hai.

## Woh dawaiyan jo wait nahi kar saktin: emergency contraception aur PEP

Law "treatment" kehta hai, dawaiyon ki list nahi deta. Par do dawaiyon ke saath ghadi chal rahi hoti hai. HIV se bachane wali post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) jitni jaldi ho sake shuru honi chahiye, assault ke 72 ghante ke baad nahi, aur phir 28 din tak leni hoti hai [[who-pep]]. Emergency contraception unprotected sex ke 5 din baad tak kaam karti hai, aur jitni jaldi li jaaye utna behtar; doctor se lagwaya gaya copper IUD sabse effective option hai. Yeh abortion nahi hai, aur kisi infection se nahi bachati [[who-ec]].

Agar hospital parchi likh kar survivor ko bahar ke chemist se apne paise se dawa laane bhej de, toh use "free of cost" ilaaj kehna mushkil hai. Agar phir bhi pregnancy ho jaaye, toh abortion ke rules rape survivors ko 24 hafte tak abortion ki ijazat dete hain [[gazette-mtp-amendment-rules-2021]].

## STIs, chot aur follow-up visits

Kai sexually transmitted infections mein koi symptom nahi dikhta, sirf test se pata chalta hai. Bacterial infections curable hain, aur hepatitis B ka vaccine maujood hai [[who-sti]]. Hospital se nikalne se pehle tests, ilaaj aur vaccine maangiye, aur poochiye ki PEP khatam hone ke baad agla HIV test kab hoga.

Acid-attack survivors ki chot ka ilaaj saalon chal sakta hai. 2024 mein India mein 207 acid attacks darj hue [[ncrb-cii-2024]], aur 2013 se Supreme Court ka order hai ki states har acid-attack victim ko after-care aur rehabilitation ke liye kam se kam Rs 3 lakh dein, jismein se Rs 1 lakh 15 din ke andar [[sc-laxmi-2013]].

## Mental-health care aur One Stop Centres

Neend na aana, sab kuch sunn sa lagna, ya assault baar-baar aankhon ke saamne aana, yeh bhi chot hai. Health Ministry ki free, 24 ghante chalne wali mental-health helpline Tele-MANAS 14416 par jawab deti hai [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]].

Jo kaam hospital akele nahi kar sakta, uske liye One Stop Centres (Sakhi) hain: counselling, police aur legal help ek hi jagah, Women and Child Development Ministry ke Mission Shakti ke tahat [[wcd-mission-shakti]]. December 2018 mein Supreme Court ne har state se kaha tha ki ek saal ke andar har district mein kam se kam ek centre khole [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]]. July 2026 tak 1,033 approved centres mein se 985 chal rahe the, aur April 2015 se ab tak 15.20 lakh se zyada auraton ki help kar chuke the [[pib-osc-lok-sabha-2026-07]].

Agar hospital mana kare, toh behes mein 72 ghante mat gawaiye. Hospital ka naam, time aur jagah note kijiye, agle hospital jaiye, aur complaint baad mein kijiye: BNS ke hisaab se ilaaj se mana karna offence hai, hospital ki koi policy nahi. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

menopause-sexual-health-screening-questi.en:
Consider a 48-year-old in Kanpur. She wakes three times a night soaked in sweat. Her periods arrive when they please. Sex has started to burn, so she avoids it, and her husband has decided she has lost interest in him. Her mother calls it "umar ka asar", the effect of age, and tells her to bear it. No doctor has ever asked her about any of this, and she has never been tested for the two cancers most common in Indian women. She is hypothetical. The pattern is not: in 2019-21, only 2% of Indian women aged 35-49 had ever been screened for cervical cancer [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

## What is actually happening to my body?

Menopause is the point at which periods have stopped for 12 months in a row. It usually arrives between the ages of 45 and 55, as a natural part of ageing [[who-menopause]]. The years before it are called perimenopause. The ovaries make less oestrogen and the levels swing, so periods come closer together or further apart, heavier or lighter.

WHO's list of common symptoms includes hot flushes and night sweats, trouble sleeping, mood changes and anxiety, joint pain, changes in sexual desire, vaginal dryness and pain during sex [[who-menopause]]. Some women barely notice. Others struggle for years. Both are normal. What is not normal is bleeding between periods, after sex or after menopause. That needs a doctor, not a shrug.

## Hot flushes and sleepless nights: do I just have to bear it?

No. Doctors can prescribe menopausal hormone therapy, an effective treatment for hot flushes and night sweats. It suits many women but not all, so it needs a proper check-up and a conversation about your own health history first. Non-hormonal medicines exist too [[who-menopause]].

Daily habits help: a cool bedroom, layers you can take off, regular exercise, less tea, coffee and alcohol late in the day, and no smoking. Exercise and not smoking also protect the bones and the heart, which lose some of oestrogen's protection after menopause.

Low mood is common in these years. If it does not lift, or you start to feel hopeless, tell a doctor or call Tele-MANAS on 14416.

## Sex has started to hurt. Is that just age?

It is a symptom, and it is treatable. With less oestrogen, the lining of the vagina and vulva becomes thinner, drier and less stretchy. That can mean burning, soreness or small tears during sex, and more urine infections.

What helps: a water- or silicone-based lubricant during sex, a vaginal moisturiser used regularly, and low-dose vaginal oestrogen from a doctor [[who-menopause]]. More time and gentler sex help too.

Many women push through the pain because they believe sex is a wife's duty. Pain is a reason to stop and see a doctor, and consent does not expire with age or marriage. Indian law still does not call forced sex by a husband on an adult wife rape; a challenge to that exception is pending in the Supreme Court [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. But the Domestic Violence Act counts sexual conduct that abuses, humiliates or degrades a woman as domestic violence [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]].

## My periods are irregular. Can I still get pregnant?

Yes. In perimenopause, ovulation becomes unpredictable, not absent. A missed period at 46 can be the menopause transition or a pregnancy, so take a test. Doctors usually advise contraception until periods have stopped for a full 12 months, sometimes longer. Ask yours.

This matters because of how Indian couples protect themselves. In NFHS-5, 37.9% of currently married women had been sterilised, but 10.3% relied on traditional methods such as withdrawal or counting "safe days" [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Counting days fails once cycles stop being regular. Withdrawal leads to about 20 pregnancies per 100 users in a year of typical use, against fewer than 1 for an IUD or an implant [[who-fp]]. And with a new partner, condoms still matter: age protects no one from STIs [[who-sti]].

## Why are these the screening years?

Breast cancer makes up 30.4% of all cancers in Indian women. The latest GLOBOCAN estimate for India is 2,37,231 new cases and 96,100 deaths in 2024. Cervical cancer is the second most common, at 10.2% [[iarc-globocan-india-factsheet-2024]]. It can be cured if it is found early, and screening can find changes in the cervix years before they turn into cancer [[who-cervical]].

WHO's elimination strategy asks countries to screen 70% of women with a high-performance test by age 35 and again by 45 [[who-cervical-elimination-launch-2020]]. Both dates fall in the years this article is about. India is nowhere near: 2% of women aged 35-49 had ever had a cervical screening test, and just 0.6% of women aged 15-49 had ever had a breast screening test [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. The survey stops at 49, so it tells us nothing about women in their fifties.

What to ask for, at a government hospital or a gynaecologist: a cervical screening test (an HPV test, a VIA check or a Pap smear) and a clinical breast examination. Between visits, know your normal. A new lump, a change in the breast's size, shape or skin, or a change in the nipple or fluid from it needs a doctor [[who-breast-cancer]].

Since February 2026, 14-year-old girls have been offered a free HPV vaccine [[pib-hpv-campaign-launch-2026]]. As our myth-buster on that vaccine explains, it protects daughters. Their mothers were never offered it, so for them, screening is the protection.

The woman in Kanpur did not need more patience. She needed one doctor's appointment, with her questions and her screening on the same visit.
menopause-sexual-health-screening-questi.hg:
Ek hypothetical socho: Kanpur ki ek 48 saal ki woman. Raat mein teen baar uski neend khulti hai, paseene se bheegi hui. Uske periods jab mann kare tab aate hain. Sex mein ab jalan hoti hai, isliye woh ise taalti hai, aur uske husband ne maan liya hai ki ab uska usme interest nahi raha. Uski maa ise "umar ka asar" kehti hain aur sehne ko kehti hain. Kisi doctor ne usse in baaton ke baare mein kabhi nahi poocha, aur Indian women ke do sabse common cancers ke liye uska kabhi test nahi hua. Yeh woman hypothetical hai. Pattern hypothetical nahi hai: 2019-21 mein 35-49 saal ki sirf 2% Indian women ne kabhi cervical cancer screening karwayi thi [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

## Meri body mein actually ho kya raha hai?

Menopause woh point hai jab periods lagataar 12 mahine se band hon. Yeh usually 45 se 55 saal ki umar ke beech aata hai, aur ageing ka natural hissa hai [[who-menopause]]. Usse pehle ke saalon ko perimenopause kehte hain. Ovaries kam oestrogen banati hain aur levels upar-neeche hote rehte hain, isliye periods kabhi jaldi-jaldi aate hain, kabhi der se, kabhi heavy, kabhi halke.

WHO ki common symptoms ki list mein hot flushes aur night sweats, neend ki dikkat, mood changes aur anxiety, joint pain, sexual desire mein badlaav, vaginal dryness aur sex ke dauraan dard shaamil hain [[who-menopause]]. Kuch women ko zyada kuch mehsoos hi nahi hota. Kuch saalon tak pareshaan rehti hain. Dono normal hain. Jo normal nahi hai, woh hai periods ke beech mein, sex ke baad ya menopause ke baad bleeding. Iske liye doctor chahiye, ise taalna nahi hai.

## Hot flushes aur bina neend ki raatein: kya bas sehna hi hai?

Nahi. Doctor menopausal hormone therapy prescribe kar sakte hain, jo hot flushes aur night sweats ka ek effective treatment hai. Yeh kai women ko suit karti hai, par sabko nahi, isliye pehle proper check-up aur apni health history par doctor se baat zaroori hai. Non-hormonal medicines bhi hain [[who-menopause]].

Roz ki aadatein madad karti hain: thanda bedroom, layers wale kapde jo utaare ja sakein, regular exercise, din ke aakhri hisse mein kam chai, coffee aur alcohol, aur smoking bilkul nahi. Exercise karna aur smoking na karna haddiyon aur dil ko bhi bachate hain, jinhe menopause ke baad oestrogen ki pehle jaisi protection nahi milti.

In saalon mein low mood common hai. Agar woh theek na ho, ya tumhe sab bekaar lagne lage, toh doctor ko batao ya Tele-MANAS 14416 par call karo.

## Sex mein ab dard hota hai. Kya yeh bas umar hai?

Yeh ek symptom hai, aur treat ho sakta hai. Oestrogen kam hone se vagina aur vulva ki lining patli, sookhi aur kam stretchy ho jaati hai. Iska matlab ho sakta hai sex ke dauraan jalan, dard ya chhote cuts, aur zyada urine infections.

Kya madad karta hai: sex ke dauraan water-based ya silicone-based lubricant, regular use hone wala vaginal moisturiser, aur doctor se milne wala low-dose vaginal oestrogen [[who-menopause]]. Zyada time lena aur gentle sex bhi madad karte hain.

Kai women dard seh kar bhi sex karti rehti hain, kyunki unhe lagta hai ki yeh wife ka farz hai. Dard rukne aur doctor ko dikhane ki wajah hai, aur consent umar ya shaadi ke saath khatam nahi hoti. Indian law ab bhi adult wife ke saath husband ke zabardasti kiye sex ko rape nahi maanta; is exception ke khilaaf challenge Supreme Court mein pending hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Lekin Domestic Violence Act aise sexual conduct ko domestic violence ginta hai jo woman ko abuse, humiliate ya degrade kare [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]].

## Mere periods irregular hain. Kya main ab bhi pregnant ho sakti hoon?

Haan. Perimenopause mein ovulation unpredictable ho jaata hai, band nahi hota. 46 ki umar mein miss hua period menopause transition bhi ho sakta hai aur pregnancy bhi, isliye test kar lo. Doctors usually tab tak contraception ki salah dete hain jab tak periods poore 12 mahine band na rahein, kabhi-kabhi usse bhi zyada. Apne doctor se poocho.

Yeh isliye zaroori hai ki Indian couples bachav ke liye kya use karte hain. NFHS-5 mein 37.9% currently married women ki sterilisation ho chuki thi, lekin 10.3% traditional methods par depend thi, jaise withdrawal ya "safe days" ginna [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Jab cycles regular hi na rahein, toh din ginna fail ho jaata hai. Typical use mein withdrawal se ek saal mein har 100 users mein lagbhag 20 pregnancies hoti hain, jabki IUD ya implant mein 1 se kam [[who-fp]]. Aur naye partner ke saath condom ab bhi zaroori hai: umar kisi ko STIs se nahi bachati [[who-sti]].

## Yahi saal screening ke saal kyun hain?

Indian women ke saare cancers mein 30.4% breast cancer hai. India ke liye latest GLOBOCAN estimate hai 2024 mein 2,37,231 naye cases aur 96,100 deaths. Cervical cancer doosra sabse common hai, 10.2% [[iarc-globocan-india-factsheet-2024]]. Jaldi pakda jaaye toh yeh cure ho sakta hai, aur screening cervix ke changes ko cancer banne se saalon pehle pakad sakti hai [[who-cervical]].

WHO ki elimination strategy countries se kehti hai ki 70% women ki high-performance test se screening 35 ki umar tak ho, aur phir 45 tak [[who-cervical-elimination-launch-2020]]. Dono dates unhi saalon mein padti hain jinke baare mein yeh article hai. India iske aas-paas bhi nahi hai: 35-49 saal ki 2% women ne kabhi cervical screening test karwaya tha, aur 15-49 saal ki sirf 0.6% women ne kabhi breast screening test [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Survey 49 par ruk jaata hai, isliye pachaas ke paar ki women ke baare mein yeh kuch nahi batata.

Government hospital ya gynaecologist se kya maangna hai: cervical screening test (HPV test, VIA check ya Pap smear) aur clinical breast examination. Visits ke beech apna normal pehchano. Nayi lump, breast ke size, shape ya skin mein badlaav, ya nipple mein badlaav ya usse fluid aana, in sab ke liye doctor chahiye [[who-breast-cancer]].

February 2026 se 14 saal ki ladkiyon ko free HPV vaccine offer ho rahi hai [[pib-hpv-campaign-launch-2026]]. Jaisa us vaccine par hamara myth-buster batata hai, yeh betiyon ko protect karti hai. Unki maaon ko yeh kabhi offer nahi hui, isliye unke liye protection screening hi hai.

Kanpur ki us woman ko aur sabr ki zaroorat nahi thi. Use ek doctor's appointment chahiye thi, jisme uske sawaal aur uski screening ek hi visit mein ho jaayein.

mother-to-child-hiv-transmission-india.en:
Imagine a 24-year-old in Nashik at a routine antenatal check-up. Her blood test comes back HIV-positive. Within days, the questions at home are not about her health or the baby's. They are about where she "got it from". Nobody asks whether her husband has ever been tested. This is a hypothetical, but the pattern is common, and it gets both the science and the fairness backwards.

The baby's risk is real, and most of it is preventable. In 2024-25, India's estimated rate of mother-to-child HIV transmission was 10.25%: roughly one in ten babies born to mothers with HIV acquired the virus [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. HIV can pass from mother to child during pregnancy, at birth or through breastfeeding, and treatment can block it at each stage [[who-hiv]].

## From one in four to one in ten

Four years earlier, in 2020-21, the estimated rate was more than 25% [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Over the same years, more pregnant women were tested for HIV: 76% in 2020-21, 84% in 2024-25 [[naco-sankalak-2025]].

Read the number honestly, though. It is a modelled estimate, and the true rate could lie anywhere between 6.74% and 16.77% [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Even the best case is far from zero. Mother-to-child transmission was also the reported route for 3.5% of the 1,63,306 people newly diagnosed with HIV in 2024-25 [[naco-sankalak-2025]].

The cost shows up in children. Around 80,000 children were on HIV treatment at government ART centres in March 2025 [[naco-sankalak-2025]], a daily medicine they will need for life. Every point on that transmission rate stands for children the system could have protected.

## The 16% of pregnant women not tested

If 84% of pregnant women were tested for HIV in 2024-25, then 16%, roughly one in six, were not. No test means no treatment for the mother and no plan for the baby. An infection nobody has found cannot be stopped.

The same antenatal visit should include a test for syphilis, a curable infection that can also pass to the baby [[who-sti]]. Only 77% of pregnant women got that test [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Of the 10,545 pregnant women found with syphilis in 2024-25, 86% were treated; about one in seven were not recorded as treated [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. NACO's own report blames a slight dip in syphilis testing on reporting and supply problems. A test kit that never arrives is a mother who is never told.

## How treatment protects the baby

Antiretroviral therapy (ART) brings down the amount of virus in the mother's body. The earlier in pregnancy she starts, the better the baby is protected, and treatment continues through breastfeeding, when the baby can still be exposed [[who-hiv]]. The medicine works when it reaches people: in 2024-25, 97.6% of people on treatment in India whose viral load was tested had the virus suppressed [[naco-sankalak-2025]].

After birth, the baby usually gets preventive medicine for the first weeks and is tested early with a special test. Ordinary HIV antibody tests can mislead in infants, because babies carry their mother's antibodies for months. Ask the ART centre when each of the baby's tests is due, and go back for every one. Treatment is free at government ART centres, which had about 17.54 lakh people on their rolls in March 2025 [[naco-sankalak-2025]].

## Blame lands on the mother: what couples should do instead

Pregnancy is often the first time anyone in a family is tested for HIV, simply because it brings a woman to a clinic. A positive result tells you she has HIV. It does not tell you who had it first. In 2024-25, 26.5% of people newly diagnosed reported sex with a regular partner as the route [[naco-sankalak-2025]], and inside a marriage that route runs both ways. And only 83.9% of people living with HIV in India knew their status [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Many husbands have simply never been tested.

So the useful question is not "who?" but "what now?":

- The partner gets tested the same week.
- If he is positive, he starts treatment too. A person on effective treatment with an undetectable viral load does not pass HIV on through sex [[who-hiv]].
- If he is negative, the couple uses condoms, and he can ask a doctor about PrEP, which our PrEP explainer covers.
- Older children may need a test as well; counsellors at the testing centre can help plan how to talk to the family.

## Her rights at the antenatal clinic

Our guide to free, confidential HIV testing explains the general rules. In a maternity ward, they mean this. Under the HIV and AIDS (Prevention and Control) Act, 2017, she cannot be tested without informed consent (Section 5), and no one, not her husband and not her in-laws, can force her to disclose her status; only a court can order that (Section 8) [[naco-hiv-aids-act-2017-gazette]].

Section 3 bars discrimination in healthcare and forbids isolating or segregating people living with HIV, and those who live with them [[naco-hiv-aids-act-2017-gazette]]. A hospital cannot refuse to deliver her baby because of HIV, or move her to a separate room or ward.

Anyone who spreads hatred against people living with HIV, in words or messages, can face three months to two years in prison, a fine of up to Rs 1 lakh, or both (Sections 4 and 37) [[naco-hiv-aids-act-2017-gazette]]. Complaints go to the state's HIV Ombudsman, and anyone who ignores an Ombudsman's order can be fined up to Rs 10,000, plus up to Rs 5,000 for every day the failure continues [[naco-hiv-aids-act-2017-gazette]].

One honest limit: the Act obliges governments to provide HIV treatment only "as far as possible" (Section 14) [[naco-hiv-aids-act-2017-gazette]]. Free medicine is policy, not an absolute right, so any break in supply deserves public anger, not quiet acceptance. This is general information, not legal advice.
mother-to-child-hiv-transmission-india.hg:
Imagine kijiye, Nashik ki ek 24 saal ki aurat pregnancy ke routine check-up ke liye jaati hai. Uska blood test HIV-positive aata hai. Kuch hi dino mein ghar pe sawaal uthne lagte hain, par uski ya bachche ki health ke baare mein nahi. Sawaal ye hai ki wo ise "kahan se laayi". Koi nahi poochta ki pati ka kabhi test hua hai ya nahi. Ye example hypothetical hai, par ye pattern bahut common hai, aur ismein science aur insaaf, dono ulte samjhe gaye hain.

Bachche pe risk real hai, aur zyada tar ise roka ja sakta hai. 2024-25 mein India mein maa se bachche ko HIV transmission ki estimated rate 10.25% thi, yaani HIV wali maaon se paida hue lagbhag 10 mein se 1 bachche ko virus mil gaya [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. HIV maa se bachche ko pregnancy mein, birth ke waqt ya breastfeeding se ja sakta hai, aur treatment har stage pe ise rok sakta hai [[who-hiv]].

## Chaar mein ek se, das mein ek tak

Chaar saal pehle, 2020-21 mein, ye rate 25% se bhi zyada thi [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Inhi saalon mein zyada pregnant women ka HIV test hone laga: 2020-21 mein 76%, aur 2024-25 mein 84% [[naco-sankalak-2025]].

Par is number ko honestly padhiye. Ye ek modelled estimate hai, aur asli rate 6.74% se 16.77% ke beech kahin bhi ho sakti hai [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Best case mein bhi ye zero se bahut door hai. 2024-25 mein jin 1,63,306 logon mein naya HIV diagnose hua, unmein se 3.5% mein route maa se bachche ko transmission bataya gaya [[naco-sankalak-2025]].

Iski keemat bachche chukaate hain. March 2025 mein lagbhag 80,000 bachche government ART centres pe HIV treatment le rahe the [[naco-sankalak-2025]], ek roz ki dawa jo unhe zindagi bhar leni hogi. Is rate ka har ek point un bachchon ki taraf ishaara karta hai jinhe system bacha sakta tha.

## Wo 16% pregnant women jinka test nahi hua

Agar 2024-25 mein 84% pregnant women ka HIV test hua, toh 16%, yaani lagbhag har chhathi aurat ka, nahi hua. Test nahi, toh maa ka treatment nahi, aur bachche ke liye koi plan nahi. Jo infection kisi ne pakda hi nahi, use roka kaise jaaye?

Pregnancy ki usi check-up visit mein syphilis ka test bhi hona chahiye. Syphilis curable hai, par ye bhi maa se bachche ko ja sakta hai [[who-sti]]. Phir bhi sirf 77% pregnant women ka ye test hua [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. 2024-25 mein 10,545 pregnant women mein syphilis mila; unmein se 86% ka treatment hua, aur lagbhag har saatvi aurat ke treatment ka koi record nahi hai [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. NACO ki apni report syphilis testing mein aayi halki girawat ke liye reporting aur supply problems ko zimmedaar maanti hai. Jo test kit kabhi pahunchi hi nahi, uska matlab hai ek maa jise kabhi bataya hi nahi gaya.

## Treatment bachche ko kaise bachata hai

Antiretroviral therapy (ART) maa ki body mein virus ki maatra kam kar deti hai. Pregnancy mein treatment jitni jaldi shuru ho, bachcha utna zyada safe rehta hai, aur treatment breastfeeding ke poore time chalta hai, kyunki tab bhi bachche tak virus pahunch sakta hai [[who-hiv]]. Dawa tab kaam karti hai jab wo logon tak pahunchti hai: 2024-25 mein India mein treatment le rahe jin logon ka viral load test hua, unmein se 97.6% mein virus suppressed tha [[naco-sankalak-2025]].

Birth ke baad bachche ko usually shuru ke kuch hafton tak prevention wali dawa di jaati hai, aur ek special test se uska jaldi test hota hai. HIV ka normal antibody test chhote bachchon mein galat picture dikha sakta hai, kyunki bachche ke khoon mein kai mahino tak maa ki antibodies rehti hain. ART centre se poochiye ki bachche ka kaunsa test kab hona hai, aur har baar zaroor jaaiye. Government ART centres pe treatment free hai; March 2025 mein wahan lagbhag 17.54 lakh log treatment le rahe the [[naco-sankalak-2025]].

## Blame maa pe: couples ko asal mein kya karna chahiye

Aksar pregnancy hi wo pehla mauka hota hai jab family mein kisi ka HIV test hota hai, sirf isliye kyunki pregnancy aurat ko clinic tak le aati hai. Positive result batata hai ki use HIV hai. Ye nahi batata ki pehle kisko tha. 2024-25 mein naye diagnose hue logon mein se 26.5% ne regular partner ke saath sex ko route bataya [[naco-sankalak-2025]], aur shaadi ke andar ye raasta dono taraf chalta hai. Aur HIV ke saath jee rahe logon mein se sirf 83.9% ko apna status pata tha [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Bahut se patiyon ka kabhi test hi nahi hua.

Isliye kaam ka sawaal "kisne?" nahi hai, balki "ab kya?":

- Pati ya partner usi hafte apna test karwaye.
- Agar wo positive hai, toh wo bhi treatment shuru kare. Jis insaan ka treatment theek chal raha hai aur viral load undetectable hai, usse sex ke through HIV nahi phailta [[who-hiv]].
- Agar wo negative hai, toh dono condom use karein, aur wo doctor se PrEP ke baare mein pooch sakta hai; iske liye hamara PrEP explainer padhiye.
- Bade bachchon ka bhi test zaroori ho sakta hai; testing centre ke counsellors bata sakte hain ki family se baat kaise karein.

## Antenatal clinic mein uske rights

Free aur confidential HIV test wali hamari guide mein general rules bataye gaye hain. Maternity ward mein unka matlab ye hai. HIV and AIDS (Prevention and Control) Act, 2017 ke under, uski informed consent ke bina uska HIV test nahi ho sakta (Section 5), aur koi bhi, na pati, na saas-sasur, use apna status batane pe majboor nahi kar sakta; aisa order sirf court de sakta hai (Section 8) [[naco-hiv-aids-act-2017-gazette]].

Section 3 healthcare mein discrimination pe rok lagata hai, aur HIV ke saath jee rahe logon ko, aur unke saath rehne walon ko, alag-thalag karne ya baaki logon se alag rakhne pe bhi rok lagata hai [[naco-hiv-aids-act-2017-gazette]]. Koi hospital HIV ki wajah se uski delivery karne se mana nahi kar sakta, na hi use alag room ya ward mein daal sakta hai.

HIV ke saath jee rahe logon ke against bol kar ya messages se nafrat phailane wale ko teen mahine se do saal tak ki jail, Rs 1 lakh tak ka fine, ya dono ho sakte hain (Sections 4 aur 37) [[naco-hiv-aids-act-2017-gazette]]. Complaint state ke HIV Ombudsman se hoti hai, aur jo Ombudsman ka order na maane, us pe Rs 10,000 tak ka fine lag sakta hai, plus jitne din order nahi maana jaata, har din ke Rs 5,000 tak [[naco-hiv-aids-act-2017-gazette]].

Ek honest limit bhi hai: ye Act sarkaaron ko HIV treatment sirf "as far as possible" dene ko kehta hai (Section 14) [[naco-hiv-aids-act-2017-gazette]]. Matlab free dawa ek policy hai, absolute right nahi. Isliye supply mein koi bhi break ho, toh chup mat rahiye, awaaz uthaiye. Ye general information hai, legal advice nahi.

msm-sexual-health-after-navtej.en:
Consider a 24-year-old man in Kanpur. He is hypothetical; the conversation is not. He is worried about a night two weeks ago and wants an HIV test. The doctor, who also treats his parents, asks: "Married? Girlfriend?" He says "girlfriend". The questions stop there. He leaves with one blood test and no word about other tests or the prevention medicine made for his situation.

Nothing he did was a crime. On 6 September 2018 a five-judge Supreme Court bench, in Navtej Singh Johar v. Union of India, unanimously read down Section 377 of the Indian Penal Code and decriminalised consensual sex between adults of the same sex [[scobserver-navtej-johar-2018]]. The law did not make him say "girlfriend". The waiting room did.

## 2018 changed the law, not the waiting room

A judgment changes what the police can do. It does not rewrite a clinic's form or retrain a doctor. The family doctor still knows your parents. The intake questions still assume a wife. A man who says "my partner is a man" risks a lecture, or gossip that reaches home before he does. So he edits his answers, and medicine works on the edited version.

The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita replaced the IPC on 1 July 2024 and dropped Section 377 altogether [[scroll-delhi-hc-unnatural-offences-bns-2024]]. Consensual sex between adult men stays legal, but an adult man forced into sex now has no specific offence to name [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. That is one more reason men stay silent.

## The numbers, and why they are probably too low

NACO, the National AIDS Control Organisation, puts HIV prevalence among men who have sex with men at 2.12% in 2024, against 0.20% among all adults [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. That is more than ten times the average. It also means the great majority of these men do not have HIV. The gap is about who testing and prevention reach, not about who the men are.

Of 1,63,306 people newly diagnosed with HIV in 2024-25, nearly 74% reported heterosexual sex as the route and 11.5% shared needles or syringes. Only 5.4% reported homosexual or bisexual sex, and 4.7% gave no route at all [[naco-sankalak-2025]].

That 5.4% is probably too low. The route is whatever a person tells a counsellor on the day of diagnosis, and stigma pushes men to under-report sex with men. A married man, asked in a government hospital how he got HIV, has every reason to choose the answer that keeps his family intact. The 2.12% has its own blind spot: it comes from men the programme reaches, and the men who hide best are the ones it reaches least.

## What to tell a doctor and what to ask for

You do not owe a doctor a label. You owe yourself accurate tests, and those depend on plain facts: whether your partners are men, women or both, what kinds of sex you have, and whether condoms were used. One sentence is enough: "I have sex with men, and I want a full STI check."

Then ask for:

- an HIV test, and a date to repeat it if the risk was recent, because a test taken too soon can miss an infection;
- a syphilis blood test. Syphilis is curable, but many STIs cause no symptoms and only a test tells [[who-sti]];
- throat and rectal swabs if you have oral or anal sex. A clinician can test only the sites they know about;
- the hepatitis B vaccine if you never had it [[who-sti]];
- PEP if a possible exposure happened in the last 72 hours. It must start within that window and is taken for 28 days [[who-pep]];
- PrEP, a medicine an HIV-negative person takes in advance on a doctor's prescription, if your risk is ongoing [[who-hiv]].

Condoms greatly reduce the risk of HIV and other STIs, though not to zero [[who-sti]]. And a partner with HIV whose treatment keeps the virus undetectable does not pass it on through sex [[who-hiv]].

## Conversion "therapy" is misconduct; the discrimination law is narrower

Some men who do tell the truth are offered a "cure". There is none, because being gay or bisexual is not an illness. In a letter dated 25 August 2022 to all state medical councils, the National Medical Commission declared that conducting "conversion therapy" on LGBTQIA+ persons is professional misconduct, after the Madras High Court directed it to do so [[scroll-nmc-conversion-therapy-2022]]. A registered doctor who offers to make you straight can be reported to the state medical council.

Section 21 of the Mental Healthcare Act, 2017 bars discrimination in mental health care on any basis and names sexual orientation [[indiacode-mhca-2017]]. The HIV Act, 2017 forbids HIV testing without informed consent, forced disclosure of HIV status except by court order, and discrimination in healthcare against people living with HIV [[naco-hiv-aids-act-2017-gazette]].

One law covers mental health care; the other is about HIV. Neither is a general rule against a physician's contempt for a gay patient with an ordinary infection. This is general information, not legal advice.

## Finding care that does not judge

India has 1,127 government STI clinics, branded Suraksha Clinics, at district hospitals and medical colleges [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Community organisations that work with gay and bisexual men usually know which doctors in a city treat people properly; ask before you choose.

If talking face to face is too much today, call 1097, NACO's helpline, for confidential counselling round the clock in 16 languages [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. For the strain of hiding, Tele-MANAS on 14416 is free at all hours [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]].

Navtej is about adults. Sexual activity with anyone under 18 is an offence under POCSO whatever the "consent", and anyone who knows of it, doctors included, must report it [[indiacode-pocso-act-2012]]. A 16- or 17-year-old still deserves care, and can call the Child Helpline, 1098.

If the first doctor lectures you, that is a fact about that doctor. Go to another. The man in Kanpur did not need more courage. He needed a clinic where "my partner is a man" is just a line in the notes.
msm-sexual-health-after-navtej.hg:
Kanpur ke ek 24 saal ke ladke ko socho. Woh hypothetical hai; yeh conversation nahi. Do hafte pehle ki ek raat ko lekar woh pareshan hai aur HIV test karwana chahta hai. Doctor, jo uske parents ka bhi ilaaj karta hai, poochta hai: "Shaadi hui hai? Girlfriend hai?" Woh kehta hai "girlfriend". Sawaal wahin ruk jaate hain. Woh ek blood test lekar nikalta hai; baaki tests ke baare mein, ya us prevention medicine ke baare mein jo usi ki situation ke liye bani hai, use koi kuch nahi batata.

Usne jo kiya, usmein koi crime nahi tha. 6 September 2018 ko Supreme Court ki paanch judges ki bench ne Navtej Singh Johar v. Union of India mein unanimously Indian Penal Code ke Section 377 ko read down kiya aur same sex ke adults ke beech consensual sex ko decriminalise kar diya [[scobserver-navtej-johar-2018]]. Usse "girlfriend" law ne nahi kehalwaya. Waiting room ne kehalwaya.

## 2018 ne law badla, waiting room nahi

Judgment yeh badalta hai ki police kya kar sakti hai. Woh clinic ka form dobara nahi likhta, na doctor ko retrain karta hai. Family doctor aaj bhi tumhare parents ko jaanta hai. Intake ke sawaal aaj bhi yeh maan kar chalte hain ki wife hogi. Jo man kehta hai "mera partner ek man hai", use lecture ka risk hai, ya aisi gossip ka jo usse pehle ghar pahunch jaye. Toh woh apne jawab edit kar deta hai, aur medicine usi edited version par kaam karti hai.

Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita ne 1 July 2024 ko IPC ki jagah li aur Section 377 ko poori tarah hata diya [[scroll-delhi-hc-unnatural-offences-bns-2024]]. Adult men ke beech consensual sex legal hi hai, lekin jis adult man ke saath zabardasti sex kiya jaye, uske paas ab naam lene ke liye koi specific offence nahi hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Men ke chup rehne ki yeh ek aur wajah hai.

## Numbers, aur yeh shayad kam kyun hain

NACO, yaani National AIDS Control Organisation, ke hisaab se 2024 mein men who have sex with men mein HIV prevalence 2.12% tha, jabki sabhi adults mein 0.20% [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Yeh average se das guna se zyada hai. Iska yeh bhi matlab hai ki in men ki bahut badi majority ko HIV nahi hai. Yeh gap is baat ka hai ki testing aur prevention kin logon tak pahunchti hai, is baat ka nahi ki yeh men kaun hain.

2024-25 mein HIV ke naye diagnose hue 1,63,306 logon mein se lagbhag 74% ne route heterosexual sex bataya aur 11.5% ne shared needles ya syringes. Sirf 5.4% ne homosexual ya bisexual sex bataya, aur 4.7% ne koi route bataya hi nahi [[naco-sankalak-2025]].

Yeh 5.4% shayad asliyat se kam hai. Route wahi hota hai jo insaan diagnosis ke din counsellor ko batata hai, aur stigma ki wajah se men, men ke saath sex ko kam report karte hain. Ek shaadi-shuda man se jab government hospital mein poocha jaye ki HIV kaise hua, toh uske paas wahi jawab chunne ki poori wajah hai jisse uski family bani rahe. 2.12% ka apna blind spot hai: yeh un men se aata hai jin tak programme pahunchta hai, aur jo men sabse achhe se chhupte hain, un tak yeh sabse kam pahunchta hai.

## Doctor ko kya batayein aur kya maangein

Tum doctor ko koi label dene ke liye majboor nahi ho. Par accurate tests tumhara haq hain, aur woh seedhe facts par depend karte hain: tumhare partners men hain, women hain ya dono, tum kis tarah ka sex karte ho, aur condom use hua ya nahi. Ek sentence kaafi hai: "Main men ke saath sex karta hoon, aur mujhe full STI check chahiye."

Phir yeh maango:

- HIV test, aur agar risk recent tha toh use dobara karwane ki date, kyunki bahut jaldi kiya gaya test infection miss kar sakta hai;
- syphilis ka blood test. Syphilis cure ho jaata hai, lekin kai STIs mein koi symptom nahi hota aur sirf test se pata chalta hai [[who-sti]];
- throat aur rectal swabs, agar tum oral ya anal sex karte ho. Clinician sirf unhi sites ko test kar sakta hai jinke baare mein use pata ho;
- hepatitis B vaccine, agar kabhi nahi lagi [[who-sti]];
- PEP, agar possible exposure pichhle 72 ghanton mein hua hai. Ise isi window ke andar start karna hota hai aur 28 din lena hota hai [[who-pep]];
- PrEP, agar tumhara risk ongoing hai: yeh woh medicine hai jo HIV-negative insaan doctor ke prescription par pehle se leta hai [[who-hiv]].

Condoms HIV aur doosre STIs ka risk bahut kam kar dete hain, par zero nahi [[who-sti]]. Aur jis partner ko HIV hai aur treatment se uska virus undetectable rehta hai, woh sex ke through HIV pass nahi karta [[who-hiv]].

## Conversion "therapy" misconduct hai; discrimination wala law usse chhota hai

Jo men sach bata dete hain, unmein se kuch ko "cure" offer kiya jaata hai. Aisa koi cure hai hi nahi, kyunki gay ya bisexual hona koi bimari nahi hai. 25 August 2022 ke ek letter mein National Medical Commission ne sabhi state medical councils ko bataya ki LGBTQIA+ persons par "conversion therapy" karna professional misconduct hai; usne yeh tab kiya jab Madras High Court ne use aisa karne ka direction diya [[scroll-nmc-conversion-therapy-2022]]. Jo registered doctor tumhe straight banane ka offer de, uski report state medical council mein ki ja sakti hai.

Mental Healthcare Act, 2017 ka Section 21 mental health care mein kisi bhi basis par discrimination mana karta hai aur sexual orientation ka naam leta hai [[indiacode-mhca-2017]]. HIV Act, 2017 teen cheezein mana karta hai: informed consent ke bina HIV testing, court order ke bina kisi ko HIV status batane ke liye force karna, aur HIV ke saath jee rahe logon ke khilaaf healthcare mein discrimination [[naco-hiv-aids-act-2017-gazette]].

Ek law mental health care ke liye hai; doosra HIV ke baare mein hai. Dono mein se koi bhi aisa general rule nahi hai jo kisi physician ko ek aam infection lekar aaye gay patient ko neecha dikhane se roke. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## Aisi care dhoondhna jo judge na kare

India mein 1,127 government STI clinics hain, jinhe Suraksha Clinics kaha jaata hai, district hospitals aur medical colleges mein [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Gay aur bisexual men ke saath kaam karne wali community organisations ko aksar pata hota hai ki sheher mein kaun se doctors logon se theek se pesh aate hain; clinic chunne se pehle unse poocho.

Agar aaj aamne-saamne baat karna bahut bhaari lag raha hai, toh NACO ki helpline 1097 par call karo: confidential counselling, din-raat, 16 languages mein [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Chhupate rehne ke bojh ke liye Tele-MANAS 14416 har waqt free hai [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]].

Navtej adults ke baare mein hai. 18 se kam umar ke kisi bhi insaan ke saath sexual activity POCSO ke under offence hai, "consent" ho ya na ho, aur jise bhi iska pata chale, doctors samet, use report karna zaroori hai [[indiacode-pocso-act-2012]]. 16 ya 17 saal ke insaan ko phir bhi care milni chahiye, aur woh Child Helpline 1098 par call kar sakta hai.

Agar pehla doctor lecture de, toh yeh us doctor ke baare mein ek fact hai. Doosre ke paas jao. Kanpur ke us ladke ko aur himmat ki zaroorat nahi thi. Use ek aisa clinic chahiye tha jahan "mera partner ek man hai" notes ki bas ek line ho.

nacp-hiv-prevention-target-missed.en:
India's fifth National AIDS and STD Control Programme (NACP-V) set itself a hard target. The fully funded central scheme, which ran from 1 April 2021 to 31 March 2026, aimed to cut annual new HIV infections and AIDS-related deaths by 80% from their 2010 levels [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. It had an outlay of Rs 15,471.94 crore [[pib-world-aids-day-backgrounder-2025]]. The programme has now ended. On deaths, India hit the mark. On new infections, the latest estimates show it fell far short, and that gap decides whether HIV is shrinking in India or not.

## The promise: an 80% cut by 2025-26

The yardstick is 2010. That year India had an estimated 1.25 lakh new HIV infections and 1.73 lakh AIDS-related deaths [[pib-world-aids-day-backgrounder-2025]]. An 80% cut meant bringing both down to a fifth of those levels.

The latest national estimates in NACO's report cover 2024 [[naco-sankalak-2025]], not the programme's final year. But to hit the target from there, new infections would have had to fall by more than half again in little more than a year, after taking 14 years to roughly halve.

| | 2010 | 2024 | Change | NACP-V target |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| New HIV infections | 1.25 lakh | 64,470 | down 48.7% | down 80% |
| AIDS-related deaths | 1.73 lakh | 32,160 | down 81.4% | down 80% |

## Deaths: target met

AIDS-related deaths fell from about 1.73 lakh in 2010 to an estimated 32,160 in 2024, a drop of 81.4% [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. That clears the bar. The likeliest reason is treatment. There is no cure for HIV, but antiretroviral therapy (ART) keeps the virus in check and has turned HIV into a manageable long-term condition [[who-hiv]].

By March 2025, 18.60 lakh people in India were on ART, most of them at 800 government centres where it is free [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Among people on treatment whose viral load was tested, 97.6% had the virus suppressed [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. That is a real public-health achievement, and it deserves to be said plainly. It still left an estimated 32,160 people dead in a single year from a condition that medicine can control.

## New infections: halved, not cut by four-fifths

New infections tell a different story. An estimated 64,470 people were newly infected with HIV in 2024, down 48.7% from 2010 [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. That roughly halves the 2010 figure. The promise was to cut it to a fifth.

Why the gap? Part of the answer lies in who is on treatment. Treatment does prevent infections: people on ART whose viral load is undetectable do not pass HIV on through sex [[who-hiv]]. But it only works for people who know they have HIV and stay on medicine. In 2024-25, 83.9% of people living with HIV knew their status, and 86.6% of those diagnosed were on treatment, short of the UN's 95-95-95 goals [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Roughly one in six people with HIV did not know it, and it is hard to protect a partner from an infection you do not know you have.

One route has also grown. The share of new diagnoses linked to shared needles and syringes rose from under 3% in 2017-18 to 12.5% in 2023-24, and stood at 11.5% in 2024-25 [[naco-sankalak-2025]]; our story on the North-East follows that shift.

Consider a 20-year-old in Indore who reads that AIDS deaths are down 81% and decides HIV is finished. They have had sex without condoms with two partners this year and have never been tested; neither have the partners. The headline number protects none of them. Falling deaths describe people already diagnosed and on medicine. The new-infection count is about people like this 20-year-old.

## 1.07: why the number living with HIV is still rising

NACO tracks one number that sums this up: the incidence-mortality ratio. Picture everyone living with HIV as water in a tank. New infections pour in; deaths among people with HIV drain out. When the ratio falls below 1, the tank is emptying and the epidemic is shrinking.

In 2024, India's ratio was 1.07 [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Slightly more is flowing in than out, so the number of people living with HIV, an estimated 25.61 lakh, is still slowly growing [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. The ratio counts deaths from all causes among people with HIV, not only AIDS deaths, which is why it sits near 1 even though new infections are about double the AIDS deaths.

The national rate of new infection looks tiny: 0.05 per 1,000 uninfected people [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. In a country of India's size, that still adds up to tens of thousands of people a year. NACO's own reading is that prevention must be intensified to push the ratio below 1 [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. And because there is no cure [[who-hiv]], every new infection means treatment and check-ups for years to come.

## What would actually bend the curve

The programme's own data, and WHO's guidance, point to where the next gains could come from.

- **Make testing easy for people who come forward.** NACO ran 4.13 crore HIV tests among at-risk people in 2024-25, and 0.40% were positive. People who walked in on their own made up only 14% of tests but had the highest positivity, 1.1% [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. People who come forward by themselves are finding infections. Testing must be easy, private and free of judgment for them.
- **Test partners and children.** With the consent of people living with HIV, 6.6 lakh of their spouses, partners and children were tested in 2024-25, and 4.1% were positive, about ten times the rate among all at-risk people tested [[naco-sankalak-2025]].
- **Use the prevention medicines.** PEP, started as soon as possible and within 72 hours of an exposure, is taken for 28 days [[who-pep]]. PrEP, prescribed by a doctor, prevents HIV in HIV-negative people at ongoing risk [[who-hiv]]. Our explainer on PEP covers the 72-hour window.
- **Reach people who inject drugs** with harm reduction services, which WHO lists among the ways to prevent HIV [[who-hiv]].
- **Protect babies.** In 2024-25, an estimated 10.25% of babies born to mothers with HIV still acquired the virus, down from more than 25% in 2020-21 [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. It is preventable: HIV medicines can prevent mothers from passing the virus to their children [[who-hiv]].

None of this needs a new invention. It needs the 20-year-old in Indore to get tested, and a system that makes that easy. NACO's toll-free helpline, 1097, offers confidential counselling round the clock [[naco]].
nacp-hiv-prevention-target-missed.hg:
India ke paanchwe National AIDS and STD Control Programme (NACP-V) ne apne liye ek mushkil target rakha. Yeh fully funded central scheme 1 April 2021 se 31 March 2026 tak chali, aur iska goal tha ki 2010 ke muqable har saal ke naye HIV infections aur AIDS se judi deaths, dono 80% kam ho jaayein [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Is scheme ka outlay Rs 15,471.94 crore tha [[pib-world-aids-day-backgrounder-2025]]. Ab yeh programme khatam ho chuka hai. Deaths par India ne target hit kiya. Naye infections par latest estimates batate hain ki India bahut peeche reh gaya, aur yahi gap decide karta hai ki India mein HIV ghat raha hai ya nahi.

## Promise: 2025-26 tak 80% ki kami

Benchmark hai 2010. Us saal India mein andaazan 1.25 lakh naye HIV infections hue the aur AIDS se judi 1.73 lakh deaths [[pib-world-aids-day-backgrounder-2025]]. 80% kami ka matlab tha dono ko us level ke paanchwe hisse tak laana.

NACO ki report mein latest national estimates 2024 tak ke hain [[naco-sankalak-2025]], programme ke aakhri saal ke nahi. Par wahan se target tak pahunchne ke liye naye infections ko lagbhag ek saal mein phir se aadhe se bhi zyada girna padta, jabki unhe lagbhag aadha hone mein 14 saal lage the.

| | 2010 | 2024 | Badlav | NACP-V target |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Naye HIV infections | 1.25 lakh | 64,470 | 48.7% kam | 80% kam |
| AIDS se judi deaths | 1.73 lakh | 32,160 | 81.4% kam | 80% kam |

## Deaths: target poora

AIDS se judi deaths 2010 mein lagbhag 1.73 lakh thi, jo 2024 mein ghat kar andaazan 32,160 reh gayi, yaani 81.4% ki girawat [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Target paar ho gaya. Iski sabse badi wajah treatment lagti hai. HIV ka koi cure nahi hai, lekin antiretroviral therapy (ART) virus ko control mein rakhti hai aur isi se HIV ab lambe samay tak manage hone wali condition ban gaya hai [[who-hiv]].

March 2025 tak India mein 18.60 lakh log ART le rahe the, jinmein se zyada tar 800 government centres par the, jahan yeh free milti hai [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Treatment le rahe jin logon ka viral load test hua, unmein se 97.6% mein virus suppressed tha [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Yeh sach mein badi public-health achievement hai, aur ise saaf-saaf kehna chahiye. Phir bhi, ek hi saal mein andaazan 32,160 logon ki jaan chali gayi, us condition se jise dawai se control kiya ja sakta hai.

## Naye infections: aadhe hue, paanchwa hissa nahi

Naye infections ki kahani alag hai. 2024 mein andaazan 64,470 logon ko naya HIV infection hua, jo 2010 se 48.7% kam hai [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Yaani 2010 ka figure lagbhag aadha hua. Promise tha use paanchwe hisse tak laane ka.

Yeh gap kyun raha? Iska ek hissa treatment ke numbers mein dikhta hai. Treatment infections rokta bhi hai: jo log ART le rahe hain aur jinka viral load undetectable hai, unse sex ke zariye HIV nahi phailta [[who-hiv]]. Lekin yeh tabhi kaam karta hai jab insaan ko pata ho ki use HIV hai aur woh dawai leta rahe. 2024-25 mein HIV wale 83.9% logon ko hi apna status pata tha, aur jinka diagnosis ho chuka tha unmein se 86.6% treatment par the, jo UN ke 95-95-95 goals se kam hai [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Mote taur par har chhe mein se ek HIV wale insaan ko pata hi nahi tha. Aur jis infection ka pata hi na ho, usse apne partner ko bachana mushkil hai.

Ek route bhi bada hua hai. Naye diagnoses mein shared needles aur syringes se jude cases ka hissa 2017-18 mein 3% se kam tha, jo 2023-24 mein 12.5% ho gaya, aur 2024-25 mein 11.5% raha [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. North-East par hamari story isi shift ko follow karti hai.

Socho, Indore ka ek 20 saal ka ladka padhta hai ki AIDS deaths 81% gir gayi hain, aur maan leta hai ki HIV khatam ho gaya. Is saal usne do partners ke saath bina condom sex kiya hai aur kabhi test nahi karaya; partners ne bhi nahi. Headline wala number inmein se kisi ko nahi bachata. Girti deaths un logon ki baat hai jinka diagnosis ho chuka hai aur jo dawai le rahe hain. Naye infections ka number is 20 saal ke ladke jaise logon ki baat karta hai.

## 1.07: HIV wale logon ki ginti ab bhi kyun badh rahi hai

NACO ek number track karta hai jo yeh poori kahani ek line mein keh deta hai: incidence-mortality ratio. Socho HIV ke saath jee rahe saare log ek paani ki tanki mein hain. Naye infections se tanki mein paani aata hai; HIV wale logon ki deaths se paani nikalta hai. Jab yeh ratio 1 se neeche hota hai, tanki khaali ho rahi hoti hai aur epidemic ghat raha hota hai.

2024 mein India ka ratio 1.07 tha [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Jitna paani nikal raha hai, usse thoda zyada aa raha hai, isliye HIV ke saath jee rahe logon ki ginti, jo andaazan 25.61 lakh hai, ab bhi dheere-dheere badh rahi hai [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Ek baat aur: yeh ratio HIV wale logon ki har tarah ki death ginta hai, sirf AIDS deaths nahi. Isiliye yeh 1 ke aas-paas hai, jabki naye infections AIDS deaths ke lagbhag double hain.

Naye infection ka national rate bahut chhota dikhta hai: har 1,000 uninfected logon mein 0.05 [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Par India jitne bade desh mein yeh chhota rate bhi har saal dasiyon hazaar log ban jaata hai. NACO khud kehta hai ki is ratio ko 1 se neeche laane ke liye prevention aur tez karna hoga [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Aur kyunki HIV ka koi cure nahi hai [[who-hiv]], har naye infection ka matlab hai aane wale kai saalon tak treatment aur check-ups.

## Asal mein curve kaise mudega

Programme ka apna data aur WHO ki guidance batate hain ki aage ka faayda kahan se aa sakta hai.

- **Jo khud test karane aate hain, unke liye testing aasaan banao.** NACO ne 2024-25 mein at-risk logon ke 4.13 crore HIV tests kiye, aur 0.40% positive nikle. Jo log apne aap walk-in karke aaye, woh total tests ka sirf 14% the, par unki positivity sabse zyada thi, 1.1% [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Matlab jo log khud test karane aate hain, unmein infections pakde ja rahe hain. Unke liye testing aasaan, private aur bina judgment ke honi chahiye.
- **Partners aur bachchon ka test karo.** HIV wale logon ki consent se 2024-25 mein unke 6.6 lakh spouses, partners aur bachchon ka test hua, aur 4.1% positive nikle, jo saare at-risk logon mein mile rate ka lagbhag das guna hai [[naco-sankalak-2025]].
- **Prevention medicines use karo.** PEP jitni jaldi ho sake, aur exposure ke 72 ghante ke andar shuru karni hoti hai, aur 28 din tak li jaati hai [[who-pep]]. PrEP doctor ke prescription se milti hai aur un HIV-negative logon mein HIV rokti hai jinhe lagatar risk rehta hai [[who-hiv]]. PEP par hamara explainer 72 ghante wali window detail mein samjhata hai.
- **Drugs inject karne walon tak pahuncho** harm reduction services ke saath, jinhe WHO HIV rokne ke tareekon mein ginta hai [[who-hiv]].
- **Bachchon ko bachao.** 2024-25 mein HIV wali maaon se paida hue andaazan 10.25% bachchon ko virus ho gaya, jo 2020-21 mein 25% se zyada tha [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Aur yeh roka ja sakta hai: HIV ki dawaiyan maa se bachche tak virus jaane se rok sakti hain [[who-hiv]].

Inmein se kisi ke liye koi nayi khoj nahi chahiye. Zaroorat bas itni hai ki Indore ka woh 20 saal ka ladka test karaye, aur system uske liye yeh aasaan banaye. NACO ki toll-free helpline 1097 par din-raat confidential counselling milti hai [[naco]].

northeast-hiv-needles-mizoram-manipur.en:
In 2024, an estimated 0.20% of adults in India were living with HIV [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. In Mizoram the figure was 2.75%, nearly 14 times as high. Nagaland followed at 1.37% and Manipur at 0.81% [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. These are small states, so they do not appear near the top of the national count of people living with HIV. But measured by the share of people living with the virus, the North-East is where HIV hits hardest, and in parts of the region new infections have risen faster since 2010 than anywhere else in India.

## Three states far above the national rate

| State | Adult HIV prevalence (2024) |
|---|---|
| Mizoram | 2.75% |
| Nagaland | 1.37% |
| Manipur | 0.81% |
| India | 0.20% |

Mizoram's figure is not just a record of old infections. Its rate of new infection is 18 times the national rate of 0.05 per 1,000 uninfected people [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. The virus is still moving.

How it moves differs from state to state. In Mizoram, about two-thirds of people newly diagnosed in 2024-25 reported heterosexual sex, and about a quarter reported shared needles [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. In Arunachal Pradesh (72%), Tripura (67%) and Assam (60%), shared needles and syringes were the most commonly reported route among people newly diagnosed [[naco-sankalak-2025]].

## From under 3% to 11.5%: the needle's share of new diagnoses

Across India, the share of new HIV diagnoses linked to shared needles and syringes rose from under 3% in 2017-18 to 12.5% in 2023-24 and 11.5% in 2024-25 [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. In Assam the shift was sharper still: from just 2.1% in 2017-18 to 60% in 2024-25 [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Punjab, where 56% of people newly diagnosed named needles, shows the same pattern outside the region; our story on Bihar and Punjab covers it.

Why do shared needles spread HIV? The virus is carried in blood. When a needle, a syringe or a drug solution is shared, traces of one person's blood can go straight into another person's bloodstream. WHO lists sharing needles, syringes and other injecting equipment, or drug solutions, as a risk factor for HIV [[who-hiv]].

Needles and sex also feed each other. Someone infected through a shared syringe can pass HIV to a sexual partner who has never touched drugs. Clinic data on syphilis, another sexually transmitted infection, points the same way. At government STI clinics in 2024-25, syphilis positivity was 14% in Arunachal Pradesh, 11% in Sikkim, 7% in Meghalaya and 4% in Mizoram, against 0.9% nationally [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. These are clinic figures, not population rates, but among people seeking STI care, syphilis is far more common in these states than in India as a whole.

## 8.79%: the highest rate of any group

People who inject drugs have the highest HIV prevalence of any group NACO tracks: 8.79% in 2024, nearly 9 in every 100. That compares with 2.84% among hijra and transgender people, 2.12% among men who have sex with men, 1.13% among female sex workers and 0.20% among all adults [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. These figures cover only people the programme reaches; those who stay hidden are missing.

Stigma shapes the data too. Routes are self-reported at diagnosis, and people may hide drug use, so even the national 11.5% may be an undercount.

Imagine a 23-year-old in a north-eastern town who injects drugs and sometimes shares a syringe with friends. He knows testing exists, but he is afraid of being lectured, and of his family finding out. So he does not go. If he has HIV, he will not be treated, and he may pass it on to the friends he shares with and to a girlfriend who has never used drugs.

On HIV testing, at least, the law is on his side. India's HIV and AIDS (Prevention and Control) Act, 2017 forbids HIV testing without informed consent (Section 5), and no one can be forced to disclose their HIV status except by court order (Section 8) [[naco-hiv-aids-act-2017-gazette]]. Section 3 bans discrimination against people living with HIV in healthcare, jobs, education and housing [[naco-hiv-aids-act-2017-gazette]]. This is general information, not legal advice.

## Tripura and Arunachal: new infections above 2010 levels

Nationally, new HIV infections fell by 48.7% between 2010 and 2024 [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. In a handful of states they went the other way: up 456% in Arunachal Pradesh, 447% in Tripura, 59% in Meghalaya and 29% in Punjab [[naco-sankalak-2025]].

The bases are small: an estimated 1,171 new infections in Tripura in 2024 and only a few hundred in Arunachal [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. But put this list next to the needle list. All four states where NACO says injecting drug use is the main route, Arunachal Pradesh, Tripura, Assam and Punjab, had more new infections in 2024 than in 2010, though Assam's rise was small [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. That does not prove needles caused the rise, but the overlap is hard to ignore.

Knowledge is uneven across the region. In 2019-21, only 12% of young women aged 15-24 in Tripura and 14% of young men in Meghalaya had comprehensive knowledge of HIV, against 69% of young women in Mizoram [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Mizoram shows that knowledge alone is not enough.

## What works: clean needles, testing and treatment without judgment

The tools are known. The hard part is reaching the people who need them.

- **Harm reduction.** WHO lists harm reduction services for people who inject drugs among the ways to prevent HIV [[who-hiv]]. At its simplest, that means clean needles and syringes, so that nobody has to share.
- **Testing that follows the needle.** NACO's index testing offers tests to the sexual partners, needle-sharing partners and children of people with HIV, with the consent of the person living with HIV. In 2024-25, 4.1% of those tested were positive, about ten times the rate among all at-risk people tested [[naco-sankalak-2025]].
- **Treatment as prevention.** A person on effective treatment with an undetectable viral load does not pass HIV on through sex [[who-hiv]], and treatment at government ART centres is free [[naco-sankalak-2025]].
- **No judgment.** A lecture at the clinic counter can teach someone not to come back. A health system that wants to reach people who inject drugs has to treat them as patients, not as problems.

If you or someone you love injects drugs, the first step is a test, not a confession. NACO's helpline 1097 [[naco]] gives confidential advice round the clock, and Tele-MANAS on 14416 [[tele-manas]] offers mental health support.
northeast-hiv-needles-mizoram-manipur.hg:
2024 mein India ke andaazan 0.20% adults HIV ke saath jee rahe the [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Mizoram mein yahi figure 2.75% tha, yaani lagbhag 14 guna. Uske baad Nagaland 1.37% aur Manipur 0.81% par the [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Yeh chhote states hain, isliye HIV ke saath jee rahe logon ki national ginti mein yeh upar nahi dikhte. Lekin agar dekhein ki kitne percent log virus ke saath jee rahe hain, toh HIV ki sabse zyada maar North-East par hai, aur is region ke kuch hisson mein 2010 ke baad naye infections India mein sabse tezi se badhe hain.

## Teen states, national rate se kahin upar

| State | Adult HIV prevalence (2024) |
|---|---|
| Mizoram | 2.75% |
| Nagaland | 1.37% |
| Manipur | 0.81% |
| India | 0.20% |

Mizoram ka figure sirf purane infections ka nahi hai. Wahan naye infection ka rate national rate se 18 guna hai; national rate har 1,000 uninfected logon par 0.05 hai [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Matlab virus wahan ab bhi phail raha hai.

Yeh kaise phail raha hai, yeh har state mein alag hai. Mizoram mein 2024-25 mein naye diagnose hue logon mein se lagbhag do-tihai ne heterosexual sex bataya, aur lagbhag ek-chauthai ne shared needles [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Arunachal Pradesh (72%), Tripura (67%) aur Assam (60%) mein naye diagnose hue logon ne sabse zyada shared needles aur syringes ko route bataya [[naco-sankalak-2025]].

## 3% se kam se 11.5% tak: naye diagnoses mein needle ka hissa

Poore India mein naye HIV diagnoses mein shared needles aur syringes se jude cases ka hissa 2017-18 mein 3% se kam tha, jo 2023-24 mein 12.5% aur 2024-25 mein 11.5% ho gaya [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Assam mein yeh badlav aur bhi tez tha: 2017-18 mein sirf 2.1% se 2024-25 mein 60% [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Punjab mein bhi naye diagnose hue 56% logon ne needles bataya, yaani yeh pattern North-East ke bahar bhi hai; Bihar aur Punjab par hamari story ise cover karti hai.

Shared needles se HIV kyun phailta hai? Virus khoon mein rehta hai. Jab needle, syringe ya drug solution share hota hai, toh ek insaan ke khoon ka zara sa hissa seedha doosre insaan ke bloodstream mein pahunch sakta hai. WHO needles, syringes, doosra injecting equipment ya drug solution share karne ko HIV ka risk factor maanta hai [[who-hiv]].

Needles aur sex ek doosre ko badhava bhi dete hain. Jise shared syringe se infection hua ho, woh sex ke zariye aise partner tak bhi HIV pahuncha sakta hai jisne kabhi drugs ko haath tak nahi lagaya. Syphilis, jo ek aur sexually transmitted infection hai, uska clinic data bhi isi taraf ishara karta hai. 2024-25 mein government STI clinics mein syphilis positivity Arunachal Pradesh mein 14%, Sikkim mein 11%, Meghalaya mein 7% aur Mizoram mein 4% thi, jabki national average 0.9% hai [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Yeh clinic ke figures hain, poori population ke nahi, par STI care lene aane walon mein in states mein syphilis poore India ke muqable kahin zyada hai.

## 8.79%: sabse zyada rate wala group

NACO jin groups ko track karta hai, unmein sabse zyada HIV prevalence drugs inject karne walon mein hai: 2024 mein 8.79%, yaani har 100 mein se lagbhag 9. Compare kijiye: hijra aur transgender logon mein 2.84%, men who have sex with men mein 2.12%, female sex workers mein 1.13% aur saare adults mein 0.20% [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Yeh figures sirf un logon ke hain jin tak programme pahunchta hai; jo log chhupe rehte hain, woh inmein nahi hain.

Stigma data par bhi asar daalta hai. Route diagnosis ke waqt log khud batate hain, aur ho sakta hai ki log drug use chhupa lein, isliye national 11.5% wala figure bhi asal se kam ho sakta hai.

Sochiye, North-East ke kisi chhote shehar mein ek 23 saal ka ladka hai jo drugs inject karta hai aur kabhi-kabhi doston ke saath ek hi syringe use karta hai. Use pata hai ki testing hoti hai, par use darr hai ki wahan use lecture milega aur ghar walon ko pata chal jaayega. Isliye woh nahi jaata. Agar use HIV hai, toh uska treatment nahi hoga, aur woh un doston ko bhi infection de sakta hai jinke saath woh syringe share karta hai, aur apni girlfriend ko bhi, jisne kabhi drugs nahi liye.

Kam se kam HIV test ke maamle mein law uske saath hai. India ka HIV and AIDS (Prevention and Control) Act, 2017 informed consent ke bina HIV test par rok lagata hai (Section 5), aur court order ke alawa kisi ko apna HIV status batane ke liye majboor nahi kiya ja sakta (Section 8) [[naco-hiv-aids-act-2017-gazette]]. Section 3 healthcare, naukri, padhai aur ghar ke maamle mein HIV wale logon ke saath discrimination par rok lagata hai [[naco-hiv-aids-act-2017-gazette]]. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## Tripura aur Arunachal: naye infections 2010 se bhi zyada

Poore desh mein 2010 se 2024 ke beech naye HIV infections 48.7% gire [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Lekin kuch states mein ulta hua: Arunachal Pradesh mein 456% badhe, Tripura mein 447%, Meghalaya mein 59% aur Punjab mein 29% [[naco-sankalak-2025]].

Yeh percentages chhoti ginti par nikle hain: 2024 mein Tripura mein andaazan 1,171 naye infections hue aur Arunachal mein sirf kuch sau [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Lekin is list ko needle wali list ke saath rakh kar dekhiye. NACO ke hisaab se jin chaar states mein injecting drug use sabse bada route hai, yaani Arunachal Pradesh, Tripura, Assam aur Punjab, un sab mein 2024 mein naye infections 2010 se zyada the, haalanki Assam mein badhotri thodi hi thi [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Isse yeh saabit nahi hota ki badhotri needles ki wajah se hui, par yeh mel nazarandaaz karna mushkil hai.

Is region mein jaankari bhi barabar nahi hai. 2019-21 mein Tripura mein 15-24 saal ki sirf 12% young women aur Meghalaya mein sirf 14% young men ko HIV ki comprehensive knowledge thi, jabki Mizoram mein 69% young women ko [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Mizoram dikhata hai ki sirf jaankari kaafi nahi hai.

## Kya kaam karta hai: saaf needles, testing aur bina judgment ka treatment

Tareeke sabko pata hain. Mushkil hai un logon tak pahunchna jinhe inki zaroorat hai.

- **Harm reduction.** WHO drugs inject karne walon ke liye harm reduction services ko HIV rokne ke tareekon mein ginta hai [[who-hiv]]. Sabse simple shabdon mein, iska matlab hai saaf needles aur syringes, taaki kisi ko share na karna pade.
- **Needle ke raaste par testing.** NACO ki index testing mein HIV wale insaan ki consent se uske sexual partners, needle share karne wale partners aur bachchon ka test hota hai. 2024-25 mein inmein se 4.1% positive nikle, jo saare at-risk logon mein mile rate ka lagbhag das guna hai [[naco-sankalak-2025]].
- **Treatment bhi prevention hai.** Jo insaan sahi treatment le raha hai aur jiska viral load undetectable hai, usse sex ke zariye HIV nahi phailta [[who-hiv]], aur government ART centres par treatment free hai [[naco-sankalak-2025]].
- **Koi judgment nahi.** Clinic ke counter par diya gaya lecture kisi ko dobara na aana sikha sakta hai. Agar system ko drugs inject karne walon tak pahunchna hai, toh unhe problem nahi, patient samajhna hoga.

Agar aap ya aapka koi apna drugs inject karta hai, toh pehla kadam test hai, koi safai dena nahi. NACO ki helpline 1097 [[naco]] par din-raat confidential advice milti hai, aur Tele-MANAS 14416 [[tele-manas]] par mental health support milta hai.
